chapters.title: Chapter 51 -51-Void Arrow, Eternal Core Furnace
paragraphs: Seeing this, Angel God and Dwarven God exchanged glances and immediately turned to flee.
But Daniel was faster.
Another Aetherlance!
Angel God’s shield shattered. HP drained completely!
Another shot.
Dwarven God’s war hammer cracked to pieces. HP drained completely!
[Ding! You have slain Angel God (Phantom) (legendary-grade BOSS)]
[Event Points +98,000,000]
[Gold Coin +9,500]
[Special Item Acquired: Angel Holy Crystal (legendary-grade / bound)]
[Ding! You have slain Dwarven God (Phantom) (legendary-grade BOSS)]
[Event Points +92,000,000]
[Gold Coin +10,500]
[Blueprint Acquired: Froststeel Armory (S-grade)]
At the same moment, every player in the spectator stands was utterly stunned.
"What... what did I just see?!"
"All four legendary-grade bosses were killed by God Faustus?!"
"Are you kidding me? No human could do this!"
"God Faustus... are you secretly a god yourself?!"
"Hahaha... God Faustus is invincible! What a face‐showing performance!"
"Did you see the expressions on those gods just now? They were terrified! Hahaha!"
"Thinking about that arrogant Titan Giant getting one-shot... I can’t stop laughing, hahaha..."
[Player tipped you 100 Silver Coins]
[Player tipped you 50 Gold Coins]
[Player tipped you 200 Gold Coins]
The barrage of chat messages and tips was non-stop, flooding the screen.
Daniel began examining his spoils.
He first looked at the skill book.
[Arrow of Nature (S-rank)]
Effect: Condenses natural elements into arrows for attack, dealing 300% damage, with armor-piercing and continuous natural damage (bleeding).
Cooldown: 30 seconds
MP Cost: 800
Class Restriction: Archer
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
Arrow of Nature?
An idea struck him immediately, and he sold the skill book to his guild.
[Ding! You sold item: Arrow of Nature skill book (S-rank) to Doom Guild for 1 Copper Coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[Since this is a skill book, choose: Quality Boost / Quantity Boost!]
"Quality Boost!"
After so many experiments, Daniel had already discovered the pattern.
Boosted items retained their original properties—the effect was simply their supercharged version.
[Ding! Congratulations! You obtained 1 Gold Coin and the Void Arrow (SSS-rank)]
[Void Arrow (SSS-rank)]
Effect: Condenses all elemental Strength (Light, Dark, Fire, Water, Wind, Earth, Lightning, Nature, etc.) into arrows, dealing 500% damage!
Special Effects:
Elemental Advantage: Can select attributes to exploit enemy weaknesses; doubled damage when effective.
Ignores Defense: Arrows ignore 50% of target’s defense and all resistances, inflicting continuous bleeding damage.
Silencing Strike: On hit, silences the target for 3 seconds (unable to use skills).
Cooldown: 20 seconds
MP Cost: 1,500
Class Restriction: Exclusive to Archers
Description: Legendary Elemental Arrow, condensing all elemental Strength in the world—nothing can withstand it!
Daniel took a deep breath.
A Divine Skill!
And still exclusive to Archers!
With this skill, he would never worry about running out of arrows again.
The stronger he became, the higher the arrow’s damage!
Plus, he could select attributes based on enemy weaknesses, with added silence and bleed effects!
With this, his future battles would be unstoppable.
He turned to the second item.
[Froststeel Armory (S-grade Blueprint)]
Effect: Allows crafting of special froststeel armor, used to equip or train elite troops.
Froststeel Armor Attributes: +200% Defense, +150% HP, +100% Frost Resistance, with Frostguard Skill (attacks freeze enemies).
Construction Requirements: Must be built in a basic city or higher, requires iron and froststeel ore mining facilities.
Daniel, as usual, sold it to the guild.
[Ding! You sold item: Froststeel Armory Blueprint (S-grade) to Doom Guild for 1 Copper Coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[Since this is a special building blueprint, choose: Quality Boost / Quantity Boost!]
[Ding! Congratulations! You obtained 1 Gold Coin and Eternal Core Furnace (supreme-grade building blueprint)]
[Eternal Core Furnace (supreme-grade building blueprint)]
Type: Legendary Dwarven forging sanctuary
Construction Requirements: Must be built deep inside a volcano or near magma chambers, consumes massive rare resources.
Effects:
Infinite Forging: Furnace energy never depletes; can forge continuously 24/7.
Divine Craftsman Blessing: Dwarven craftsmen in range get +80% success, +300% chance for rare output.
Super Forging: Chance to craft items beyond craftsman’s normal quality limits.
Furnace Guardian: Automatically generates lava shields around the furnace, fortifying the forge space against intruders.
Racial Bonus: Dwarves in range get +200% to all stats, +500% forging speed.
Description: Supreme-grade Dwarven artifact, legendary site of the first-generation Dwarven God’s forging. Owning it grants access to endless weapon production!
Daniel’s eyes widened.
This... was terrifying!
If he had a team of Dwarven craftsmen...
A sudden thought flashed through his mind.
Dwarven craftsmen!
Right!
Now he had Polaris City, the Prosperity Sanctuary, and the Core of the Earth Furnace...
If he could recruit a batch of Dwarven craftsmen...
His territory would become the human race’s premier equipment production hub!
His heart raced at the idea.
Once this event ended, he must find a way to bring some dwarves over!
Even if he had to bind them, he would!
After all, he was now a Count—commanding troops and doing tasks was normal.
And who knows? They might not want to leave once they arrive!
For the dwarves, the Core of the Earth Furnace was like a swordsman encountering a legendary greatsword—they wouldn’t sleep for nights!
He turned to the last piece of loot.
[Angel Holy Crystal (legendary-grade / bound)]
Effect: Upon use, allows you to make a wish to an Angel God (the magnitude of the wish depends on the Angel God’s will).
Description: Supreme-grade token of the angels, containing a fragment of an Angel God’s will. Only those favored by fate can acquire it.
Daniel frowned.
Make a wish to the Angel God?
It was good... but he remembered the [Angel’s Vengeance Mark] on his body.
The Angel King was still hunting him!
This Angel Holy Crystal... enter angel territory, and he would be chased; not entering, and he couldn’t use it!
Hey! A one-way road with a dead end!
Moreover, it was a bound item—otherwise, he could have sold it.
Forget it. It was a good item; he’d keep it for now.
[Ding! Sacred Spring bathing will commence in 10 seconds. Please prepare!]
Daniel raised an eyebrow and turned his gaze to the Sacred Spring before him.

chapters.title: Chapter 52 -52-Four Core Attributes +10,000!
paragraphs: Before him, the Sacred Spring emitted wisps of gentle steam.
Its waters were crystal clear, reflecting the golden glow that seemed to radiate from the depths.
Without a moment’s hesitation, Daniel stepped into the spring.
The warm water instantly enveloped his entire body, a comforting heat rushing through every vein.
[Ping! You are now bathing in the Sacred Spring...]
[four core attributes +1]
[four core attributes +1]
[four core attributes +1]
The system notifications repeated every few seconds. Daniel closed his eyes and simply allowed himself to soak in this rare moment of serenity.
For some reason, he felt as though his entire being was being gently relaxed.
Every tension, every anxiety accumulated over more than two centuries seemed to dissipate with the warmth of the spring.
The calm was unlike anything he had felt in his life. It was almost as if the Sacred Spring had absorbed every ounce of worry lodged within him.
An hour passed in tranquil silence.
[Ping! Sacred Spring bathing session completed.]
[Attribute Increase Summary:]
Strength: +10,000
Intelligence: +10,000
Agility: +10,000
Constitution: +10,000
[Current Four Core Attributes:]
Daniel opened his eyes, feeling the surging power of his Strength. Even he found it difficult to believe what had just happened.
All four of his core attributes had increased by ten thousand points. The sheer magnitude of the gain was nearly unimaginable.
No wonder the five great gods had all been willing to throw themselves at the phantom, fighting to claim it.
The attraction wasn’t just prestige—it was the chance to acquire such a miraculous Strength boost.
Yet, he knew better. The gods’ own four core attributes were likely terrifyingly high. If there weren’t enormous rewards, no deity would stoop to participate.
Other players might view this assembly of gods as a mere system event.
But Daniel understood that nothing in the Stellar World occurred randomly. Every occurrence was linked, forming a vast web of cause and effect.
He opened his activity panel to check the latest stats.
[Current Event Points: 512,847,200]
[Current Gold Coins Obtained: 270,000]
[Current Spectator Seat Tips: 40,830 Gold Coins]
"Gold coins..." he muttered.
Adding the ten billion gold coins he had previously collected from guild earnings, he couldn’t help but let a slight smile curve his lips.
Money? At this point, he hardly had any real concept of it.
With the Millionfold Boost in hand, any problem in the Stellar World that could be solved with gold coins was no longer an issue. Nothing was beyond his reach.
He closed the panel and cast a final glance over the snowy plains. Then he crushed the event scroll in his hand.
A flash of white light enveloped him. In an instant, his figure vanished entirely from the spectator feed.
[Spectator Seats]
"God Faustus has appeared!"
"I still can’t wrap my head around it. How did he do it? Are all these gods really that weak?"
"Is this the gap between humans and gods?"
"Don’t even mention it. I can’t even defeat a level 15 wild boar right now. I’m just going to isolate myself."
"God Faustus is invincible!"
"This event was over in a flash, but watching it was worth every second!"
"Seriously, how did that one arrow deal hundreds of thousands of damage? His four core attributes must be at least in the thousands!"
"...White light flickered across the screens. Players everywhere were simultaneously teleported out of the Beast Maze and returned to the central plazas of their respective main cities.
The excitement that had erupted in the spectator seats carried over into the main world.
[World Channel]
"Holy shit! We’re finally out!"
"Did you guys complete it? On my six-star map, our team of ten just defeated a level 40 gold-grade BOSS! Everyone got a gold-grade piece of equipment. Amazing!"
"Impressive, brother! On our five-star map, we only cleared some small monsters. We couldn’t beat the BOSS..."
"Our four-star map? Ten people worked together for three hours and finally defeated that gold-grade BOSS! It dropped a gold-grade item!"
"Jealous! I only earned a few hundred points..."
"Hahaha, did you know? God Faustus cleared a nine-star map all by himself!"
"A nine-star map? Alone?"
"Not just that! I watched the entire thing. First, he cleared the nine-star map, defeating the Beast God Phantom, and then moved on to the ten-star map!"
"Ten stars?! That actually exists?"
"Yes! The Sacred Spring in the snow country! It has four legendary-grade BOSSes: Angel God, Titan God, Elven Goddess, Dwarven God!"
"Holy shit! Holy shit! Holy shit!"
"And then?"
"And he killed them all! One arrow per boss!"
"Originally, there were supposed to be five, but the Beast God was killed early in the nine-star map, which gave him access to the ten-star map."
"...Damn it! I’m shattered!"
"All four legendary-grade BOSSes in the ten-star map were slain by him? Not one escaped?!"
"Is he even human?"
"I suddenly feel my gold-grade BOSS isn’t worth it anymore..."
"Stop talking. I feel depressed."
"What exactly is God Faustus’ strength? Can a level 100 really defeat legendary-grade BOSSes?"
"Those legendary-grade BOSSes are around level 50, but their attribute points are extremely high. Even so, they were each taken down by God Faustus."
"How did he even manage it?"
"I don’t know. But I do know one thing—he is a god."
"Hahaha... A human god? That’s interesting!"
"God Faustus is invincible!"
Meanwhile, inside the core channels of the major guilds, the atmosphere grew tense.
[Rhine Guild·Core Group]
"One person cleared the nine-star map, even reaching the ten-star map."
"All five legendary-grade god phantoms were slain by him."
"Do you realize what this means?"
Silence fell. After a long pause, someone cautiously asked, "President, should we still target him?"
"...Target him? With what?"
"He can wipe out our entire guild alone."
"From now on, keep a low profile around Doom Guild members."
"Forget it. I think we should just avoid them entirely."
[Ragnarok]
"Latest news: Rhine has backed down!"
"Of course. Wouldn’t you back down in their place?"
"I just want to know... How did God Faustus do it?"
"I don’t know. And I don’t want to know either."
"Why?"
"Because knowing doesn’t help. We simply can’t do it."
"...Heartbreaking."
[Stormbound Guild]
Vantheon’s face darkened, fingers clenching white.
"President, do we still—"
"Silence!"
Vantheon took a deep breath, teeth gritted.
"From now on, no one is to provoke Doom Guild."
"If you see Faustus, go around him. Anyone who causes trouble will have to leave the guild."
The channel fell completely silent. Everyone understood the president had caved.
Yet they also understood something else. Not caving was impossible. That person could not be provoked.

chapters.title: Chapter 53 -53-Redemption, Chronoverse Prologue Codex
paragraphs: Daniel stood in the Luminara city square and he opened the event panel.
[Beast Maze Event Settlement]
[Your Total Points: 512,847,200]
[Server Rank: #1]
[Loading Redemption Shop...]
A dazzling array of items appeared directly before him.
From F-grade to supreme-grade, from equipment to skill books, from materials to consumables—everything imaginable was here!
Even just the equipment categories were immense: weapons, armor, accessories, special... and each of these had subcategories: swords, staves, bows, and so on.
The materials section was even more insane: ores, herbs, beast hides, elemental crystals, dragon scales, phoenix feathers... if you could imagine it, it could be found here.
Daniel’s eyes swept across the list.
He directly skipped the ordinary items.
His gaze landed directly on two supreme-grade items.
[Singer’s Gem (supreme-grade / special item)]
Price: 210,000,000 points
Effect:
Song of Time: All item bonuses and all potion durations extended by 100× (including buffs, temporary attribute items, etc.)
Song of Souls: Immunity to all illusions, all awe effects, and all mind-control effects (including god-grade awe, charm, fear, confusion, etc.)
Siren’s Song: When activated, charms all targets within 100 meters for 5 seconds (cooldown 24 hours)
Description: The ultimate treasure of the merfolk. Legend has it that the mermaid queen once tamed deep-sea leviathans with her voice. This gem contains the purest strength of the merfolk!
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
Extend duration by 100×?
What did that mean?
A potion that normally lasts 1 minute would now last 100 minutes.
A temporary attribute boost that lasts 10 minutes would now last 1,000 minutes.
One bottle of potion would be worth a hundred for anyone else!
And on top of that, immunity to all mind-control effects...
From now on, any awe, illusion, charm, or fear would be completely useless against him!
He glanced at the price: 210 million points.
Without hesitation, he redeemed it.
[Ding! You spent 210,000,000 points and redeemed "Singer’s Gem (supreme-grade)"]
[Item has been added to your inventory]
Daniel turned to the second item.
[Chronoverse Prologue Codex (supreme-grade / special item)]
Price: 300,000,000 points
Status: Not Activated
Activation Requirement: Must collect the ten elemental cores (Light, Darkness, Fire, Water, Wind, Earth, Thunder, Metal, Soul, Nature!)
Post-Activation Effects:
Time-Space Mastery: Grants preliminary control over time and space, including time acceleration/deceleration and spatial folding/travel.
Prologue Chronicle: Records every time-space operation performed by the user, forming a personal skill book.
Time-Space Anchor: Allows placement of up to three anchors anywhere; teleport instantly back to an anchor from any location.
Prologue Protection: Automatically triggers time reversal to 3 seconds prior when receiving fatal damage (cooldown 7 days)

Description: The legendary prologue written by the Creator God, recording the universe’s fundamental time-space secrets. Collect all ten elemental cores to unlock its mysteries and master the power of time and space.
Daniel took a deep breath.
Time and space attributes!
This was one of the highest-level strength systems in the Stellar world.
In his past life, he’d seen a god with time mastery—able to accelerate himself tenfold and slow enemies tenfold, fighting BOSSes like a casual stroll.
And another who could manipulate space freely, traversing forbidden zones at will.
But those were only superficial manipulations of time-space elements.
The Chronoverse Prologue Codex could allow someone to truly master the essence of time and space!
The ten elemental cores...
He quickly recalled:
Core of Light, Core of Darkness, Core of Fire, Core of Water, Core of Wind, Core of Earth, Core of Thunder, Core of Nature, Core of Metal, Core of Soul
He knew the origin of several, some even had specific locations.
But Core of Nature and Core of Soul...
Those were nearly impossible to obtain.
No matter. He would secure it first, then deal with the rest.
300 million points? Worth it.
[Ding! You spent 300,000,000 points and redeemed "Chronoverse Prologue Codex (supreme-grade)"]
[Item has been added to your inventory]
After redeeming these two items, he had 2,847,200 points remaining.
Daniel casually redeemed some materials and equipment, then closed the panel.
Opening his inventory, he looked at the two supreme-grade items, a slight smile on his lips.
Equipping Singer’s Gem, future potion durations would stretch long enough to make a BOSS doubt reality!
The Chronoverse Prologue Codex—the day he collected all ten elemental cores would mark the moment he became truly invincible.
He drew a deep breath, activated God Speed, and headed to the main portal.
Destination: Polaris City!
A flash of white light.
Daniel appeared beside the Polaris City portal.
This was his second visit to the city.
The first time had been rushed—the day he purchased the territory.
Now, he finally had time to explore his own city.
Polaris City’s architecture was simple.
Stone houses, low and sturdy, thick walls, narrow windows.
Built to withstand the northern winds and potential attacks from the demon race.
Streets were narrow, paved with cobblestones, lined with various shops.
Blacksmiths, general stores, inns, taverns... modest, but functional. Everything essential was here.
In the distance, tall, thick city walls were built from solid stone blocks, with soldiers patrolling above.
The city was shrouded in a grayish hue, conveying a sense of austerity and age.
But at this moment, the city was undergoing massive transformation.
Scaffolding lined both sides of the streets, craftsmen climbing, hammering, and sawing.
New buildings sprouted: shops, houses, workshops.
By the portal, a middle-aged man in a refined robe approached quickly.
[Polaris City Governor · Roland (LV210 · epic-grade NPC)]
Tall and upright, elegant features, neatly combed gray hair, radiating competence from every gesture.
"Your Excellency, Count!"
Roland bowed respectfully.
"You’ve finally arrived!"
Daniel nodded.
"Governor Roland, thank you for your efforts."
Roland had been specially assigned by Augusta, a top-tier talent.
An LV210 epic-grade NPC, experienced and capable.
With him in charge, Daniel could comfortably be a hands-off ruler.
Roland shook his head with a smile.
"Not at all, Your Excellency. It will be my honor to serve you."
"Please, follow me. I’ll show you the progress of Polaris City’s construction!"

A dazzling array of items appeared directly before him.
From F-grade to supreme-grade, from equipment to skill books, from materials to consumables—everything imaginable was here!
Even just the equipment categories were immense: weapons, armor, accessories, special... and each of these had subcategories: swords, staves, bows, and so on.

A potion that normally lasts 1 minute would now last 100 minutes.

From now on, any awe, illusion, charm, or fear would be completely useless against him!
He glanced at the price: 210 million points.

chapters.title: Chapter 54 -54-Completion of Two Supreme-Grade Buildings
paragraphs: The two walked through the streets, Governor Roland introducing as they went.
"Currently, Polaris City has a total population of approximately 32,000, of which 28,000 are natives, and around 4,000 are newly recruited talents."
"The commercial district has been fully planned. There are currently 327 shops, 185 of which are leased, mainly dealing in ironware, furs, and foodstuffs."
"The residential area is under expansion. In a month, it is expected to accommodate 100,000 residents."
"The wall reinforcement project has already begun. It is expected to finish within three months, doubling the city’s defensive capabilities."
"Additionally, per your instructions, we’ve designated a training ground specifically for cultivating wolf riders."
Roland glanced at Daniel.
"Your Excellency, those wolfkin... are they truly reliable?"
Daniel smiled.
"They’ve signed servitude contracts. Betrayal means death."
"Just make sure they work properly."
Roland nodded, no longer questioning.
Soon, they arrived at a wide open space.
This area was in the northeast corner of the city, adjacent to the city walls, covering roughly 100,000 square meters.
"Your Excellency, this is the designated industrial forging district."
Roland pointed ahead.
"The two buildings you mentioned—where shall we construct them?"
Daniel opened his inventory and pulled out two scrolls that glimmered with golden light:
Temple of Eternal Prosperity!
Eternal Core Furnace!
Both were supreme-grade construction projects, and their placement would have far-reaching consequences. This required careful consideration.
Following Roland’s advice, Daniel quickly selected the locations on the map.
"Temple of Eternal Prosperity will be built here, at the city’s center, to radiate its influence across the entire city."
"And the furnace..."
He looked toward the northwest mountainous area of Polaris City, where a volcano emitted a thin plume of smoke.
It was a dormant volcano, said to have been inactive for hundreds of years.
"Build it on the volcano."
Roland froze.
"A volcano? Your Excellency, that’s extremely dangerous..."
"Don’t worry."
"If it weren’t for this volcano, I’d have a real headache!"
Daniel smiled, interrupting him, and crushed the two scrolls.
Golden light burst forth!
The ground beneath them trembled.
Rumble—Rumble—!
In the planned area ahead, a majestic temple rose from the earth.
Constructed entirely of white jade, 50 meters high, covering tens of thousands of square meters.
The walls were etched with intricate runes, radiating a faint golden glow.
Atop the temple sat a massive gem, its light reaching throughout the city.
Temple of Eternal Prosperity—completed.
At the same time, from the volcano in the southwest of Polaris City, a deafening roar echoed.
Dark red light shot skyward, illuminating half the horizon.
A colossal furnace emerged from the magma, made entirely of obsidian and silver-grade materials, about 100 meters tall, engraved with ancient Dwarven runes.
The surrounding lava automatically receded, creating a safe area!
Eternal Core Furnace—completed.
[Ding! Temple of Eternal Prosperity has been completed]
[All residents of Polaris City: Morale +100, Food production +200%, Commercial tax revenue +100%...]
[Ding! Eternal Core Furnace has been completed]
[All Dwarves in Polaris City (if present): All stats +200%, Forging speed +500%...]
[No Dwarves detected; effect not yet activated. Human craftsmen success rate +40%, speed +200%, all stats +50%...]
The city’s working residents suddenly stopped their tasks.
They stared blankly at the temple in the distance, feeling strength surging within them.
"What... what is happening?"
"I feel so powerful!"
"My illness... my illness is cured!"
"Your Excellency! It must be the Count!"
"Long live the Count!"
Cheering erupted, echoing across the city.
Roland stood before the temple, witnessing all of this, his heart in turmoil.
He had worked in the glorious main city for five years, accompanying Lord Augusta on many major events.
But at this moment, he was deeply shocked.
In the blink of an eye, two supreme-grade buildings were completed instantly.
What kind of skill was this? Was this what it meant to be an adventurer favored by the Creator?
A single temple benefitting the entire city.
And the furnace... built on a volcano!
Wait—a furnace on a volcano!
Wasn’t this the legendary supreme-grade Dwarven forging sanctuary?
Roland’s breathing quickened.
This Count... who exactly was he?
He took a deep breath, suppressing his astonishment.
No wonder Uncle Augusta had repeatedly instructed him to fully support this Count!
Following someone like this, the future was limitless.
Two days later.
A weary group appeared outside the gates of Polaris City.
Over three hundred wolfkin, young and old, male and female.
At their head was an old wolfkin—the very one who had led the signing of the servitude contracts.
They had traveled for two full days to reach the city.
The old wolfkin looked at the city before him, his cloudy eyes reflecting a mixture of emotions.
From now on, the wolfkin clan would live here.
What awaited them... they did not know.
The city gates opened, and a group of human soldiers came out.
The leading officer glanced at the wolfkin and nodded.
"Follow me. Governor Roland has already arranged everything."
Entering the city, the wolfkin were stunned.
Wide streets, orderly buildings, busy crowds...
Nothing like the dilapidated frontier settlements they had imagined.
The deeper they went, the more awed they became.
In the distance, a magnificent temple stood in the city center, radiating a faint golden light.
Further beyond, a dark red glow shot into the sky!
These two buildings were more imposing and awe-inspiring than anything they had ever seen.
"What... what is that?"
A young wolfkin stammered, pointing at the Sanctuary Garden under construction.
The old wolfkin opened his mouth, speechless.
The temple’s footprint was larger than the entire wolfkin settlement.
Its size was nearly equal to the already-completed Temple of Eternal Prosperity.
And the materials used for construction—every stone and gem—were incredibly rare.
One block alone could sustain their whole tribe for a year!
The old wolfkin exhaled deeply, extinguishing the last spark of hope.
In the face of such overwhelming power, there was no room for resistance.
Obedience and diligence... perhaps that was the only way the wolfkin could survive.
The group was led to an open area, adjacent to the city walls, covering about 20,000 square meters, designated for their use.
"This is your quarters," the officer said, pointing ahead.
"Over there is the training ground, specifically for training wolf riders."
"Any supplies you need, request them from logistics."
"Any problems you cannot solve, go to Governor Roland."
The officer finished his instructions and left.
The wolfkin looked at each other in disbelief.
A training ground?
Supplies freely available?
This... this is the treatment of servants?

chapters.title: Chapter 55 -55-The Strength of the Masses is Great
paragraphs: The old wolfkin fell silent for a moment, then spoke gravely.
"Listen carefully, everyone. All of this happened because our wolfkin tribe chose to oppose humans!"
"By all rights, even if the humans wiped out every wolfkin among us, it wouldn’t have been unjust. But—"
His tone shifted, becoming heavier.
"Count Faustus has given us a chance to live. A place to stay, and even promised us sufficient supplies!"
"I earnestly plead with all of you: for the future of the wolfkin tribe, we must seize this rare opportunity and train the wolf riders diligently for the Count."
"And anyone who dares slack off... don’t blame me for being harsh!"
After the old wolfkin spoke, the rest of the wolfkin fell into collective silence.
Indeed. In the world of beastfolk, facing hostile forces, total annihilation was not unusual.
But this Count had done the opposite—providing them with abundant resources for survival...
Even though they were destined to serve as slaves, at least they would not have to worry about basic survival!
One by one, the wolfkin nodded, shifting their mindset, and stepped into their new home.
Lord’s Manor
Daniel sat in the main seat, listening to Roland’s report.
"Your Excellency, your commercial operations in the nine major main cities have now been fully rolled out."
"The properties you purchased previously have now been half-leased, generating rental income of approximately 8 million Gold Coins per month."

"The End Times Trading Company stores have opened in all nine main cities, dealing in equipment, potions, and materials. Their prices are 20% lower than NPC shops, and business is booming. Monthly profits are expected to exceed 50 million Gold Coins."
"Furthermore, the portals you built in the nine main cities now have a daily usage of over 20 million people, and your share income is approximately 17 million Gold Coins per day."
Roland paused, looking at the ledger in his hands, his voice trembling.
"Summing it all up, your current stable monthly income is roughly... 3 billion Gold Coins."
"Annual income: approximately 30 billion Gold Coins."
He looked up at Daniel.
"Your Excellency, you are already one of the wealthiest lords in the entire empire."
Daniel nodded, expression calm.
30 billion Gold Coins?
Sounds impressive.
But opening the system panel and checking his total assets...
[Current Gold Coins: 10,247,836,000,000]
Over ten trillion!
Even the "small change" exceeded this sum.
He spoke lightly.
"Allocate 500 billion Gold Coins to Polaris City first."
"Fully advance city construction, commercial development, and military buildup."
"I will make Polaris City the most prosperous city in the northern border of the empire!"
The ledger nearly slipped from Roland’s hands.
Five... five hundred billion?!
He had been a governor for many years and had seen many wealthy lords—but never someone this rich!
He drew a deep breath, suppressing his shock, and nodded solemnly.
"As you command, Your Excellency!"
At that moment, a system notification rang out.
[Ding! Your "Doomgreen Forest Purge Operation" has new progress]
[Total goblins killed: 12,847,326]
[Merit Points Earned: 23,854,197]
Daniel raised an eyebrow.
12 million goblins?
And this was just a few days?
He opened the event backend to check the details.
[Current participating players: 532,847,196]
[Highest single-player kill: 2,847 (player "Sunborn")]
[Most active period: 8–11 PM daily]
[Most popular regions: Eastern and southern edges of Doomgreen Forest]
A slight smile curved Daniel’s lips.
This was the strength of the masses!
No matter how strong he was, how many goblins could he kill alone in a day?
Ten thousand? A hundred thousand?
But with the players participating, tens of millions of goblins could be killed in a single day!
And the players were enthusiastic—they could farm merit points, get equipment, and level up. Why wouldn’t they?
Daniel only needed to post the task, set the reward share, and sit back to collect both money and merit points.
Multi-win! Perfect!
"The strength of the masses... truly the greatest."
He murmured to himself, a small smile in his eyes.
Future events like this should be run often.
Exploit—or rather, wisely leverage—the players’ strength.
Everyone profits together. Brilliant!
Meanwhile, Doomgreen Forest.
A seven-person squad moved through the woods.
At their head was a burly greatsword warrior, carrying a golden-glimmering greatsword.
[Sunborn · LV52 · Greatsword Warrior]
"Captain, where are we farming today?"
A player dressed as an assassin leaned closer.
Sunborn opened the map and pointed at a marked location.
"There’s a goblin settlement ahead. I discovered it yesterday."
"About 200 goblins, with a level 50 leader."
"We’re seven. If we coordinate properly, we can take them all down."
The others’ eyes lit up.
"Two hundred! That’s a ton of merit points!"
"Let’s go! Move out!"
Ten minutes later, the seven crouched in the grass, observing the settlement.
It was a small goblin village, with dozens of crude huts made of wood and hides.
Over 200 goblins moved between the huts—some cooking, some sharpening weapons, some fighting and roughhousing.
In the center, a slightly larger goblin sat on a rock, gnawing on a bloody bone.
[Goblin Leader · LV42 · Silver-grade]
Sunborn studied them carefully, then quietly assigned roles.
"Tank, draw aggro and keep them contained."
"Mages and archers, focus on small goblins first, then all fire on the leader."
"Healers, watch the tank’s HP."
"Assassin, flank and look for a chance to strike the leader."
"Understood?"
"Understood!"
The battle began.
The tank charged first, shield smashing the nearest goblin’s face.
"Argh—!"
The goblin screamed. Scores turned their heads.
"Humans! Kill them!"
They charged.
The tank backed up a few steps, bracing with the shield.
The mage raised a hand, a rain of fire covering the horde.
The archer fired rapidly, one arrow per goblin.
The assassin circled behind, plunging a dagger into the leader’s back.
"Argh—!"
The leader flew into a rage, swinging a bone club at the assassin.
The assassin barely dodged, rolling back and creating distance.
At the critical moment, the tank rushed forward and slashed the leader’s leg.
"Green-skin scum, your opponent is me!"
"Damned humans, die!"
The battle lasted half an hour.
The seven coordinated perfectly, gradually compressing the goblins’ activity space.
Small goblins fell in waves.
The leader’s HP slowly declined.
Finally, Sunborn brought his greatsword down on the leader’s head.
The fight was over.
[Ding! You killed goblins ×237, Goblin Leader ×1]
[Merit Points +1,247]
[Equipment Obtained: Bronze-grade ×23, Iron-grade ×5, Silver-grade ×1]
Sunborn wiped the blood from his face and grinned.
"Good job, everyone!"
"This run paid off big time!"

sentences.text: The old wolfkin fell silent for a moment, then spoke gravely.
"Listen carefully, everyone.
All of this happened because our wolfkin tribe chose to oppose humans!"
"By all rights, even if the humans wiped out every wolfkin among us, it wouldn’t have been unjust.
But—"
His tone shifted, becoming heavier.
"Count Faustus has given us a chance to live.
A place to stay, and even promised us sufficient supplies!"
"I earnestly plead with all of you: for the future of the wolfkin tribe, we must seize this rare opportunity and train the wolf riders diligently for the Count."
"And anyone who dares slack off... don’t blame me for being harsh!"
After the old wolfkin spoke, the rest of the wolfkin fell into collective silence.
Indeed.
In the world of beastfolk, facing hostile forces, total annihilation was not unusual.
But this Count had done the opposite—providing them with abundant resources for survival...
Even though they were destined to serve as slaves, at least they would not have to worry about basic survival!
One by one, the wolfkin nodded, shifting their mindset, and stepped into their new home.
Lord’s Manor
Daniel sat in the main seat, listening to Roland’s report.
"Your Excellency, your commercial operations in the nine major main cities have now been fully rolled out."
"The properties you purchased previously have now been half-leased, generating rental income of approximately 8 million Gold Coins per month."
"The End Times Trading Company stores have opened in all nine main cities, dealing in equipment, potions, and materials.
Their prices are 20% lower than NPC shops, and business is booming.
Monthly profits are expected to exceed 50 million Gold Coins."
"Furthermore, the portals you built in the nine main cities now have a daily usage of over 20 million people, and your share income is approximately 17 million Gold Coins per day."
Roland paused, looking at the ledger in his hands, his voice trembling.
"Summing it all up, your current stable monthly income is roughly...
3 billion Gold Coins."
"Annual income: approximately 30 billion Gold Coins."
He looked up at Daniel.
"Your Excellency, you are already one of the wealthiest lords in the entire empire."
Daniel nodded, expression calm.
30 billion Gold Coins?
Sounds impressive.
But opening the system panel and checking his total assets...
[Current Gold Coins: 10,247,836,000,000]
Over ten trillion!
Even the "small change" exceeded this sum.
He spoke lightly.
"Allocate 500 billion Gold Coins to Polaris City first."
"Fully advance city construction, commercial development, and military buildup."
"I will make Polaris City the most prosperous city in the northern border of the empire!"
The ledger nearly slipped from Roland’s hands.
Five... five hundred billion?!
He had been a governor for many years and had seen many wealthy lords—but never someone this rich!
He drew a deep breath, suppressing his shock, and nodded solemnly.
"As you command, Your Excellency!"
At that moment, a system notification rang out.
[Ding!
Your "Doomgreen Forest Purge Operation" has new progress]
[Total goblins killed: 12,847,326]
[Merit Points Earned: 23,854,197]
Daniel raised an eyebrow.
12 million goblins?
And this was just a few days?
He opened the event backend to check the details.
[Current participating players: 532,847,196]
[Highest single-player kill: 2,847 (player "Sunborn")]
[Most active period: 8–11 PM daily]
[Most popular regions: Eastern and southern edges of Doomgreen Forest]
A slight smile curved Daniel’s lips.
This was the strength of the masses!
No matter how strong he was, how many goblins could he kill alone in a day?
Ten thousand?
A hundred thousand?
But with the players participating, tens of millions of goblins could be killed in a single day!
And the players were enthusiastic—they could farm merit points, get equipment, and level up.
Why wouldn’t they?
Daniel only needed to post the task, set the reward share, and sit back to collect both money and merit points.
Multi-win!
Perfect!
"The strength of the masses... truly the greatest."
He murmured to himself, a small smile in his eyes.
Future events like this should be run often.
Exploit—or rather, wisely leverage—the players’ strength.
Everyone profits together.
Brilliant!
Meanwhile, Doomgreen Forest.
A seven-person squad moved through the woods.
At their head was a burly greatsword warrior, carrying a golden-glimmering greatsword.
[Sunborn · LV52 · Greatsword Warrior]
"Captain, where are we farming today?"
A player dressed as an assassin leaned closer.
Sunborn opened the map and pointed at a marked location.
"There’s a goblin settlement ahead.
I discovered it yesterday."
"About 200 goblins, with a level 50 leader."
"We’re seven.
If we coordinate properly, we can take them all down."
The others’ eyes lit up.
"Two hundred!
That’s a ton of merit points!"
"Let’s go!
Move out!"
Ten minutes later, the seven crouched in the grass, observing the settlement.
It was a small goblin village, with dozens of crude huts made of wood and hides.
Over 200 goblins moved between the huts—some cooking, some sharpening weapons, some fighting and roughhousing.
In the center, a slightly larger goblin sat on a rock, gnawing on a bloody bone.
[Goblin Leader · LV42 · Silver-grade]
Sunborn studied them carefully, then quietly assigned roles.
"Tank, draw aggro and keep them contained."
"Mages and archers, focus on small goblins first, then all fire on the leader."
"Healers, watch the tank’s HP."
"Assassin, flank and look for a chance to strike the leader."
"Understood?"
"Understood!"
The battle began.
The tank charged first, shield smashing the nearest goblin’s face.
"Argh—!"
The goblin screamed.
Scores turned their heads.
"Humans!
Kill them!"
They charged.
The tank backed up a few steps, bracing with the shield.
The mage raised a hand, a rain of fire covering the horde.
The archer fired rapidly, one arrow per goblin.
The assassin circled behind, plunging a dagger into the leader’s back.
"Argh—!"
The leader flew into a rage, swinging a bone club at the assassin.
The assassin barely dodged, rolling back and creating distance.
At the critical moment, the tank rushed forward and slashed the leader’s leg.
"Green-skin scum, your opponent is me!"
"Damned humans, die!"
The battle lasted half an hour.
The seven coordinated perfectly, gradually compressing the goblins’ activity space.
Small goblins fell in waves.
The leader’s HP slowly declined.
Finally, Sunborn brought his greatsword down on the leader’s head.
The fight was over.
[Ding!
You killed goblins ×237, Goblin Leader ×1]
[Merit Points +1,247]
[Equipment Obtained: Bronze-grade ×23, Iron-grade ×5, Silver-grade ×1]
Sunborn wiped the blood from his face and grinned.
"Good job, everyone!"
"This run paid off big time!"

chapters.title: Chapter 56 -56-Conspiracy, Empire-Wide Mobilization
paragraphs: Similar scenes were unfolding across Doomgreen Forest.
Thousands upon thousands of players formed squads of varying sizes, hunting goblins in the dense forest.
Some, like Sunborn’s team, were highly coordinated and extremely efficient.
Some were inexperienced, stumbling along, but still enjoying themselves.
Some got lucky, picking off lone goblins and returning to turn in their tasks with delight.
Some got unlucky, encountering large goblin patrols and being chased all over the forest.
But no matter the outcome, everyone was farming merit points.
Everyone was getting stronger.
This was the strength of hundreds of millions of players.
Daniel sat in Lord’s Manor, watching the constantly updating numbers in the backend, a smile gradually forming on his lips.
To leverage the strength of the players—this was truly a joyous thing.
One day later
Luminara.
Daniel entered the Intelligence Bureau and approached the task window.
"Submit task."
He handed over the Goblin High Priest’s letter, supplementary documents, and the wolfkin tribe leader’s token, one by one.
The clerk behind the window examined them for a moment, eyes flickering with surprise.
[Ding! Congratulations on completing the Intelligence Bureau commission: Threat in Doomgreen Forest (S-rank)]
[Task Rating: SSS (overachieved)]
[Total goblins killed: 312,847,326]
Rewards:
Merit Points +60,854,197
Gold Coins +30,000
Contribution Points +5,000
[Extra Reward: Intelligence Bureau Honor Medal (special) ×1]
The clerk respectfully handed back a medal.
"Your Excellency, your task record has been updated. Minister Rex is waiting inside; he wishes to discuss an urgent matter."
Daniel nodded, pocketed the medal, and headed further inside.
Several intelligence officers were busy organizing documents; seeing him, they nodded respectfully.
"Your Excellency, the Minister is waiting for you."
One officer led him across the hall to a closed wooden door.
Inside was a modest room piled with documents.
Rex sat behind a desk, frowning at an intelligence report.
Seeing Daniel, a small smile appeared on his face.
"Your Excellency, Count, you’re here."
He gestured for Daniel to sit, getting straight to the point.
"The evidence you submitted has been verified."
"The situation is more severe than we imagined."
He pushed a file across the desk.
"According to our intelligence, over the past month, the beastfolk, dwarves, and dark elves have all had close contact with goblins."
"Some beastfolk tribes have even begun joint operations with goblins."
"The dwarves, though outwardly neutral, have internal divisions; a radical faction has sided with goblins."
"The most troubling are the dark elves."
Rex’s voice darkened.
"They usually stay hidden in the underground world, rarely interfering in surface matters. But this time, they sent envoys to meet the Goblin High Priest."
"As for who—or what force—is driving the goblins... that’s still unclear."
"But one thing is certain: this is a vile conspiracy against the human race!"
He leaned back in his chair, massaging his forehead.
"The Emperor has issued the latest decree!"
"The entire nation is on high alert and mobilization. Unless there’s a miracle, a great war is inevitable!"
"If you don’t mind, Your Excellency, the Empire needs your strength!"
[Ding! You have received an urgent imperial decree: Full-Scale Mobilization!]
[Ding! Do you accept the S-rank full-scale mobilization task?]
[Task Details (Duration: 24 hours):]
Gold Coin → Merit Points: 500 Gold Coins = 1 Merit Point (unlimited)
Supplies → Merit Points: War machines, equipment, strategic resources can be exchanged for merit points (calculated by quality and quantity)
Territory Construction: Leveling up territory construction grants merit points (calculated by degree of improvement)
[Task Rewards: Merit Points, EXP, Gold Coins, Contribution Points...]
[Time Limit: 24 hours]
[Special Note: After this task concludes, the Empire will rate each lord’s mobilization contribution. The results will affect their authority and Contribution Points in the upcoming war.]
Daniel squinted slightly at the task description.
500 Gold Coins for 1 Merit Point?
For someone with Millionfold Boost, this was effectively free!
He accepted the task immediately.
"Your Excellency seems very interested?"
Rex sipped his tea. "I have to say, this is a rare opportunity."
"The Emperor is offering unlimited exchanges to maximize the Empire’s strength before the war."
He set down his cup, shaking his head.
"Unfortunately, 500 Gold Coins for 1 Merit Point is still a steep price for most lords. Very few can spend millions of Gold Coins."
"I estimate that there won’t be more than ten lords in the entire Empire capable of exchanging enough to reach a million merit points."
He looked at Daniel, a hint of anticipation in his voice.
"You, Duke... with your investments in the nine main cities, should be able to exchange quite a lot. A few million merit points should be no problem."
Daniel looked at him.
"A few million?"
He smiled but said nothing.
He then opened the system panel and started the operation.
[Ding! You spent 500 billion Gold Coins to exchange for 1 billion Merit Points!]
[Current Merit Points: 1,083,175,020]
The room fell silent for a moment.
Rex’s teacup froze mid-air.
His eyes widened.
"...Your Excellency... what did you just—?"
Daniel replied calmly, "Exchanged some merit points."
"Some... how many?"
"One billion."
Rex slowly set down the teacup.
He looked at the tea, then at Daniel, then back at the tea.
"I need to confirm... You just said you exchanged one billion merit points?"
"Correct."
"At 500 Gold Coins per Merit Point... one billion Merit Points would require..."
He did the mental calculation, then froze.
"500 billion Gold Coins?"
Daniel nodded.
"Five hundred billion Gold Coins."
Rex remained silent for five seconds.
Then he leaned back, regarding Daniel with a new perspective.
"Your Excellency... may I ask something?"
"Ask."
"Just... how rich are you?"
Daniel thought for a moment.
"Beyond imagination."
Rex let out a wry smile.
"I’ve been Intelligence Minister for decades, and I’ve seen countless wealthy people."
"But someone like you... this is the first time."
He shook his head, drank the tea in one gulp.
"If I didn’t already know your adventurer status, I’d have insisted you come with us!"
"Five hundred billion Gold Coins just like that!"
"I believe, Your Excellency, that you are truly the talent the Empire needs!"
Daniel nodded, unconcerned by the praise.
Instead, he opened the system backend and began editing player tasks.
Such an opportunity... how could he not make full use of it?

chapters.title: Chapter 57 -57-Promotion to Legendary Rank
paragraphs: [Ding! You are editing an A-rank task: Merit Points Exchange!]
[Task Details: 1 Gold Coin = 1 Merit Point (covered by Doom Guild)]
[Task Start: 1 hour from now, Duration: 24 hours]
[Task Description:]
Each player limited to exchanging 10,000 Merit Points (to prevent abuse)
Exchanged Merit Points can be freely used (equipment, skill books, military rank upgrades, etc.)
After double-checking, Daniel clicked Publish!
The next second, World Channel exploded!
"What... what is this?!"
"Am I seeing this right? 1 Gold Coin = 1 Merit Point?!"
"God Faustus has lost it? Imperial Merit Points are extremely valuable. He’s offering 1 Merit Point per Gold Coin?!"
"This can’t be real... isn’t this giving it away for free?!"
"Are you idiots? It’s officially issued as a task. Even if it were fake, it becomes real!"
"Hahaha... amazing! I saved 300 Gold Coins; now I can get 300 Merit Points!"
"I only have 100 Gold Coins... if I’d known, I wouldn’t have bought that crappy sword!"
"Hurry! Only one hour to go!"
"Why is God Faustus doing this? Isn’t he losing money?"
"Who cares why! We can get Merit Points, that’s enough!"
"Exactly! God Faustus must have his reasons; we just enjoy the benefits!"
"Last time during the goblin hunt, I exchanged Merit Points for a full iron-grade equipment set—leveled up instantly!"
"Jealous! I didn’t participate, regret it so much!"
"This time, we’re going all out!"
[Eternal Eagle Guild]
"What do you guys think?"
"Can’t figure it out."
"1 Gold Coin for 1 Merit Point... the value of Imperial Merit Points is unquestionable. Doing this, isn’t he losing a fortune?"
"He doesn’t seem to be lacking Gold Coins. Unless... he doesn’t care about Merit Points at all?"
"Also, he’s God Faustus."
"So... what do we do? Exchange or not?"
"Exchange! Why not? Each person can get 10,000 Merit Points; exchange as much as you can!"
"Notify all members to prepare Gold Coins immediately!"
Daniel watched the World Channel frenzy, a faint smile forming on his lips.
Losing money? How could he lose money?
He had Millionfold Boost.
500 billion Gold Coins exchanged for 1 billion Merit Points—this was the first layer.
Then he offered players 1 Gold Coin = 1 Merit Point.
Players received Merit Points, used them to grow stronger.
Stronger players level up faster.
What players didn’t know:
Every time a player exchanged 1 Gold Coin for 1 Merit Point, he triggered Millionfold Boost, receiving 1 million Gold Coins back!
All he paid were the system’s Merit Points.
Merit Points could be obtained with Gold Coins from the Empire:
500 Gold Coins → 1 Merit Point
1 Merit Point → Player gains 1 Gold Coin
Player’s 1 Gold Coin triggers Boost → returns 1 million Gold Coins to him
1 million Gold Coins → exchange for 2,000 Merit Points
And repeat.
This was a highly profitable, multi-win operation.
One hour passed quickly.
[Ding! Your task "Merit Points Exchange" is now live]
[Current participants: 11,043,957]
[Merit Points spent: 147,326,000]
[Gold Coins gained: 147,326,000]
[Millionfold Boost triggered: Gold Coins +14,732,600,000,000]
Daniel looked at the long string of numbers on the system panel, expression unchanged.
Merit Points spent were less than one-fifth.
He currently had 1 billion Merit Points, just used 180 million, leaving over 800 million.
Half an hour later:
[Current participants: 95,387,948]
[Merit Points spent: 742,817,000]
The number of participants and exchange speed slowed noticeably.
This indicated that most players were running out of Gold Coins.
After all, the server had only opened a few days, and ordinary players saving even a few hundred Gold Coins was already impressive.
Those able to spend 10,000 Gold Coins on Merit Points were already minor tycoons.
Nearly 700 million Merit Points had been exchanged—enough for the players to use for a while.
Next, it was time for business.
Daniel opened the task panel and spent Gold Coins to stack Merit Points to 3 billion.
He nodded at the long list of numbers in the Merit Points panel.
However, his military rank was still Apprentice—the medal Adrian had given him back in Starter Village.
[Apprentice Merit Medal]
Effect: +20 to all core attributes, unlocks basic military exchange permissions.
It was time for an upgrade.
He opened the Military Rank Exchange interface.
[Imperial Honor Military Rank System (Nine Levels)]
Apprentice: 1,000 Merit Points
Cadet: 10,000 Merit Points
Official: 100,000 Merit Points
Special Ops Level 3: 500,000 Merit Points
Special Ops Level 2: 1,000,000 Merit Points
Special Ops Level 1: 5,000,000 Merit Points
Honor: 100,000,000 Merit Points
Hero: 500,000,000 Merit Points
Legendary: 1,000,000,000 Merit Points
Daniel’s gaze landed at the top.
He was currently Apprentice level and could ascend all the way.
From Apprentice to Legendary, a total of 1,606,611,000 Merit Points were required.
He had 3 billion Merit Points, more than enough.
[Ding! You spent 10,000 Merit Points and promoted to "Cadet"!]
[Ding! You spent 100,000 Merit Points and promoted to "Official"!]
[Ding! You spent 10 million Merit Points...]
System notifications sounded continuously.
Daniel’s military rank soared.
[Ding! You spent 1 billion Merit Points and your rank has been upgraded to "Legendary"!]
Golden light shimmered. A brand-new medal appeared on his chest.
[Legendary Merit Points Medal]
Effect:
Four Core Attributes +2,000
All portals and transport within the Empire are free
50% discount at official imperial shops
During national wars, commanded troops gain +10% Attack and Defense
Unlock exclusive treasury at the military supply depot to exchange rare resources
Can mobilize portions of the imperial army (requires military position coordination)
Description: Supreme-grade honor for humans; in the history of the Empire, fewer than ten people have ever earned this medal!
Daniel looked at these effects, a faint smile on his lips.
Four Core Attributes +2,000—100 times higher than Apprentice level!
Free transport and 50% shop discounts were expected.
The most critical was the fourth effect:
During national wars, commanded troops gain 10% Attack and Defense bonus.
10% equates to one extra combatant per ten soldiers.
For a million-strong army, that’s an extra 100,000 effective troops!
And in battle, the effect cannot be summarized by simple math.
This 10% bonus was extremely powerful.

[Millionfold Boost triggered: Gold Coins +14,732,600,000,000]
Daniel looked at the long string of numbers on the system panel, expression unchanged.
Merit Points spent were less than one-fifth.
He currently had 1 billion Merit Points, just used 180 million, leaving over 800 million.
Half an hour later:
[Current participants: 95,387,948]
[Merit Points spent: 742,817,000]
The number of participants and exchange speed slowed noticeably.
This indicated that most players were running out of Gold Coins.
After all, the server had only opened a few days, and ordinary players saving even a few hundred Gold Coins was already impressive.
Those able to spend 10,000 Gold Coins on Merit Points were already minor tycoons.
Nearly 700 million Merit Points had been exchanged—enough for the players to use for a while.
Next, it was time for business.
Daniel opened the task panel and spent Gold Coins to stack Merit Points to 3 billion.
He nodded at the long list of numbers in the Merit Points panel.
However, his military rank was still Apprentice—the medal Adrian had given him back in Starter Village.
[Apprentice Merit Medal]
Effect: +20 to all core attributes, unlocks basic military exchange permissions.
It was time for an upgrade.
He opened the Military Rank Exchange interface.
[Imperial Honor Military Rank System (Nine Levels)]
Apprentice: 1,000 Merit Points
Cadet: 10,000 Merit Points
Official: 100,000 Merit Points
Special Ops Level 3: 500,000 Merit Points
Special Ops Level 2: 1,000,000 Merit Points
Special Ops Level 1: 5,000,000 Merit Points
Honor: 100,000,000 Merit Points
Hero: 500,000,000 Merit Points
Legendary: 1,000,000,000 Merit Points
Daniel’s gaze landed at the top.
He was currently Apprentice level and could ascend all the way.
From Apprentice to Legendary, a total of 1,606,611,000 Merit Points were required.
He had 3 billion Merit Points, more than enough.
[Ding!
You spent 10,000 Merit Points and promoted to "Cadet"!]
[Ding!
You spent 100,000 Merit Points and promoted to "Official"!]
[Ding!
You spent 10 million Merit Points...]
System notifications sounded continuously.
Daniel’s military rank soared.
[Ding!
You spent 1 billion Merit Points and your rank has been upgraded to "Legendary"!]
Golden light shimmered.
A brand-new medal appeared on his chest.
[Legendary Merit Points Medal]
Effect:
Four Core Attributes +2,000
All portals and transport within the Empire are free
50% discount at official imperial shops
During national wars, commanded troops gain +10% Attack and Defense
Unlock exclusive treasury at the military supply depot to exchange rare resources
Can mobilize portions of the imperial army (requires military position coordination)
Description: Supreme-grade honor for humans; in the history of the Empire, fewer than ten people have ever earned this medal!
Daniel looked at these effects, a faint smile on his lips.
Four Core Attributes +2,000—100 times higher than Apprentice level!
Free transport and 50% shop discounts were expected.
The most critical was the fourth effect:
During national wars, commanded troops gain 10% Attack and Defense bonus.
10% equates to one extra combatant per ten soldiers.
For a million-strong army, that’s an extra 100,000 effective troops!
And in battle, the effect cannot be summarized by simple math.
This 10% bonus was extremely powerful.

chapters.title: Chapter 58 -58-Empire General, Independent Legion Commander
paragraphs: With the promotion of his military rank completed, Daniel’s gaze turned toward military posts.
A rank symbolizes personal honor, but a post is where real power lies!
Having a rank without a post makes one a mere figurehead.
Having both rank and post—that is what makes a true commander!

The Empire’s military hierarchy was comprehensive, ranging from the lowest Ten-Man Captain all the way to the Supreme Marshal of the Empire. Each level carried its own distinct authorities and responsibilities.
Daniel opened the interface for exchanging military posts.
[Currently available posts for exchange:]
Non-commissioned Officer Level:
Level 1 – Ten-Man Captain: requires 10,000 merit points (commands 10 soldiers)
Level 2 – Twenty-Man Captain: requires 30,000 merit points (commands 20 soldiers)
Level 3 – Fifty-Man Captain: requires 60,000 merit points (commands 50 soldiers)
Junior Officer Level...
General Officer Level:
Level 10 – Brigadier: requires 20 million merit points (commands 20,000 soldiers)
Level 11 – Major General: requires 50 million merit points (commands 50,000 soldiers)
Level 12 – Lieutenant General: requires 100 million merit points (commands 100,000 soldiers)
Commander Level:
Level 13 – General: requires 500 million merit points (can independently command a legion; no troop limit during wartime)
Level 14 – Grand General: requires 1 billion merit points (can command 2–4 legions; Emperor’s approval required)
Level 15 – Marshal: requires 2 billion merit points (can command 5–8 legions; Emperor’s approval required)
Empire Marshal Level:
Level 16 – Army Group Marshal: requires 5 billion merit points (special approval from the Emperor)
Level 17 – Theater Marshal: requires 10 billion merit points (special approval from the Emperor)
Level 18 – Grand Marshal: requires 15 billion merit points (special approval from the Emperor)
Level 19 – Imperial Marshal: requires 20 billion merit points (special approval from the Emperor; awarded only to royal family members or those who achieve unparalleled feats)
Daniel’s eyes fixed on Level 13. He checked the details.
General, also known as Independent Legion Commander!
This was the highest post that the Duke of Augusta could directly exchange.
Beyond this level, one had to submit an application to His Majesty the Emperor, which would require approval after a long, cumbersome review process.
It required 500 million merit points.
He had more than enough merit points now—he could exchange it directly.
[Ding! You have spent 500,000,000 merit points and have been promoted to "General"!]
[General Post Authorities]
Independent Command Authority – Can independently lead operations without reporting to superiors.
Wartime Expansion Authority – During war, troop numbers are unlimited (peace-time numbers are limited by territory).
Recruitment Authority – Can recruit soldiers (NPCs) in the main city and owned territories.
War Machine Procurement Authority – Can directly purchase equipment from the Empire’s war machine stock at a 20% discount.
Legion Banner – Possess an exclusive legion banner; within its radius, allied troops receive +10% to all attributes.
Military Tribunal Authority – Can establish military tribunals within the legion to judge disciplinary issues.
Loot Distribution Authority – Can distribute loot independently, without reporting to superiors.
Fixed Material Allocation – Can claim a large quantity of military supplies weekly.
Daniel’s lips curled into a slight smile as he scanned the long list of privileges.
Wartime expansion authority guaranteed the ability to employ a "human wave" tactic.
Fixed material allocation meant he could get a lot of supplies every week for free.
Recruitment authority allowed him to raise NPC soldiers and build his own army.
War machine authority meant his army could manufacture equipment directly on the frontlines without transporting it back and forth.
Most importantly, independent operation authority meant that in the future, he could strike anyone he wanted within legal limits, without needing permission.
With all of this, he could officially form his own army.
Combined with a 20% bonus from his rank and a 10% bonus from the banner, his troops were naturally 30% stronger than others!
These 500 million merit points were spent incredibly wisely.
After completing the post promotion, Daniel didn’t stop. He opened the military engineering exchange interface again.
[War Machine Blueprints]
Common-grade: 100 merit points/piece
Bronze-grade: 1,000 merit points/piece
Iron-grade: 10,000 merit points/piece
Silver-grade: 100,000 merit points/piece
Gold-grade: 1,000,000 merit points/piece
Platinum-grade: requires merit unlock (currently unavailable)
Blackgold-grade: requires merit unlock (currently unavailable)
[Basic Equipment List:]
Trebuchet – long-range siege engine; attacks walls and structures
Ballista – long-range piercing engine; attacks large targets or dense formations
Shield Wagon – mobile cover; resists arrows and magic
Siege Ladder – climbing equipment for walls
Battering Ram – siege engine; strikes gates
Caltrops – defensive device; blocks cavalry charges
Arrow Tower – defensive building; auto-shoots enemies
Watchtower – reconnaissance building; expands vision
Camp – temporary base; provides rest and defense
Banner – boosts morale; increases troop strength
Daniel’s eyes scanned the detailed list. Without hesitation, he exchanged all gold-grade blueprints.
With his current wealth of merit points, why settle for anything less than the best?
Next, Daniel opened another exchange interface.
[Formation Layout Exchange]
Equipment is static, but formations are alive.
An excellent formation could double a legion’s combat effectiveness.
Common-grade: 100 merit points/piece
Bronze-grade: 1,000 merit points/piece
Iron-grade: 10,000 merit points/piece
Silver-grade: 100,000 merit points/piece
Gold-grade: 1,000,000 merit points/piece
Platinum-grade: requires merit unlock
[Basic Formations List:]
Arrowhead Formation – offensive; sharp vanguard breaks through lines
Fish Scale Formation – defensive; layered like scales, nearly impregnable
Scissors Formation – encirclement; wings spread to surround enemies
Rolling Drum Formation – all-rounder; can attack and defend flexibly
Loose Formation – deceptive; lures enemies in
Dense Formation – tightly packed; shields and soldiers face forward head-on
Cone Formation – assault; sharp front line penetrates defenses
Pocket Formation – baiting; center falls back while wings encircle
Again, Daniel exchanged all of them without hesitation.
If he wanted to truly arm his Strength, it had to be with the best!
After exchanging these two sets of blueprints, Daniel turned toward the Lord’s Manor.
His merit points were now ridiculously abundant—it was time to upgrade his noble title.
No matter how high a title could go, it was never too high!
Augusta was reviewing documents. Looking up, she saw Daniel approaching.
"Count Faustus? How may I assist you?"
Daniel stepped in front of him and got straight to the point.
"Lord of the City, I want to be promoted to Duke!"

chapters.title: Chapter 59 -59-Empire Duke: Recruiting Troops
paragraphs: Augusta’s quill froze mid-air, his face full of astonishment as he looked at Daniel.
"Duke?"
He set down the pen and spoke.
"Count Faustus, you should know that between Count and Duke, there is Marquis," Augusta explained.
"To skip directly to Duke, three conditions must be met."
"First, you need over 1 billion merit points."
"Second, your Empire Contribution Points must be sufficient."
"Third, you require special approval from His Majesty the Emperor."
Daniel nodded.
"I have the merit points."
He opened his panel and proactively showed Augusta.
[Military Rank: Legendary Merit Medal]
[Military Post: General]
Augusta’s pupils constricted.
He drew a deep breath and looked at Daniel.
"Y-you... how did you manage this?"
Daniel smiled.
"Didn’t His Majesty open gold coin exchanges for merit points?"
"I just... exchanged a little."
Augusta fell silent for three seconds, then discreetly checked the merit point exchange details.
Soon, his entire body froze.
"A little exchanged? You mean the 3 billion merit points?"
He knew exactly how many gold coins it would take to get that many merit points.
And hadn’t Daniel just purchased all nine main city properties? How did he still have so much capital to exchange for these merit points?
This kid... how rich is he?!
Yet he didn’t ask further.
Augusta nodded.

"The merit points are enough, and your Empire Contributions are also sufficient. The teleportation network you built, plus the intelligence reports you recently submitted, the funds you provided for imperial preparations... all count."
"As for His Majesty..."
He paused, then stood.
"I will report to His Majesty immediately."
"With your contributions, the Emperor will surely approve."
Half an hour later...
[Ding! Global Announcement!!!]
[Player "Faustus," due to outstanding contributions, has been specially approved by His Majesty the Emperor for promotion to "Duke"! ]
[As the first player to receive the Duke title, the following rewards are granted:]
Contribution Points +100,000
Gold Coin +10,000,000
Honorary Title: Pillar of the Empire
This achievement has been recorded in the Stellar Chronicles, immortalized for all history!
[Duke Authorities:]
Judicial Immunity – Except for the Emperor, no one can judge or sentence the Duke.
Unlimited Task Issuance – Can publish tasks to anyone (special tasks excluded; rewards at own expense).
Territorial Limit Expansion – Can hold main city-level territories (unlimited in number and population).
Recruitment Cap Increase – Army recruitment limit increased to 1 million soldiers.
Tax Privilege – Can levy up to 15% tax in territories.
Appointment Authority – Can appoint officials of Viscount rank and below.
Parliament Seat – Permanent member of the Imperial Parliament with voting rights on major decisions.
Imperial Audience – Can request an audience with the Emperor at any time...
"Wait, are we even playing the same game?"
"Exactly! I feel like they’re playing some single-player cracked version while we’re still grinding tasks and running maps..."
"Seriously, last time I entered the Police Department for a quest and almost got thrown out like a beggar. Meanwhile, Faustus casually chats with the Lord of the City?!"
"This is insane... comparing people like this is infuriating!"
"See it, everyone? People like this completely break game balance. This Faustus is literally on another level!"
"Here come the fixed NPCs..."
Daniel looked at the long list of Duke-exclusive authorities, a faint smile tugging at his lips.
Duke!
From commoner to Duke in just one week.
The rules were becoming less and less restrictive.
He was getting closer and closer to becoming the master of the board.
One day, he would be the one who made the rules.
Leaving the Lord’s Manor, Daniel didn’t waste a moment and headed straight for the War Bureau.
War Bureau Minister Kasel Drovane was studying something over a war table. Seeing him enter, he froze.
"Your Grace, the Duke?"
He quickly saluted.
Daniel waved him off.
"Minister Kasel, I’m going to recruit an army!"
Kasel’s eyes lit up.
"The Duke is forming his own army?"
"Yes."
"My territories are on the edge of Abyss Demon lands, and the entire Empire has been preparing for war lately. I want to contribute to the Empire as well!"
Daniel nodded.
"Please show me the recruitment list."
"As you wish, Your Grace!"
Kasel hurriedly unrolled a massive scroll, filled with detailed information.
[Recruitable NPC Soldiers:]
Imperial Infantry (LV80-100, iron-grade): 10 gold coin/person
Imperial Archers (LV80-100, iron-grade): 12 gold coin/person
Imperial Cavalry (LV100-120, iron-grade): 20 gold coin/person
Imperial Heavy Infantry (LV100-120, iron-grade): 18 gold coin/person
Imperial Heavy Cavalry (LV120-150, bronze-to-iron grade): 10–30 gold coin/person
Imperial Mages (LV100-150, bronze-to-silver grade): 10–50 gold coin/person
Imperial Priests (LV100-150, bronze-to-silver grade): 10–45 gold coin/person
Imperial Scouts ...
[Recruitable High-Ranking Officers:]
Chief Strategic Officer Hudson (LV230, epic-grade): 10 million gold coin
Archery Commander Elina (LV215, epic-grade): 8 million gold coin
Cavalry Commander Cassius (LV220, epic-grade): 8.5 million gold coin
Mage Corps Leader Lorin (LV210, epic-grade): 8 million gold coin
Scout Commander Shade (LV210, epic-grade): 9.4 million gold coin
Lieutenant General Fred (LV225, epic-grade): 60 million gold coin
Logistics Officer Rand (LV205, blackgold-grade): 7.5 million gold coin
Lieutenant General Victor (LV245, epic-grade): 10 million gold coin ...
Daniel scanned the list, then waved decisively.
"Recruit them all!"
Kasel nearly dropped the scroll in shock.
"All... all of them?"
"Infantry 100,000; archers 50,000; cavalry 30,000; heavy infantry 30,000; heavy cavalry 20,000; mages 10,000; priests 10,000; scouts 10,000; engineers 20,000; logistics 20,000..."
He calculated rapidly.
"A total of 1 million soldiers, plus over 50 high-ranking officers..."
"The total annual recruitment cost alone is nearly 50 billion gold coins!"
He looked up at Daniel.
"Your Grace, are you certain?"
Daniel nodded.
"Certain."
He opened the transaction interface and transferred directly.
[You have transferred 50,000,000,000 gold coin to the Empire War Bureau]
Kasel stared at the incoming number, overwhelmed.
Then he drew a deep breath.
"Your Grace, you are the most decisive lord I’ve ever seen!"
"These soldiers and officers are yours from now on!"
A flash of white light streaked across the sky.
Daniel returned to Polaris City.
By the portal, a massive crowd had already gathered.

chapters.title: Chapter 60 -60-Polaris Promoted to Main City
paragraphs: It was the 1 million-strong army he had just recruited, arriving in waves through the portal.
At the front were the dozens of high-ranking officers he had hired.
Leading them was a burly middle-aged man, square-jawed, thick brows and large eyes, clad in exquisite armor.
[Chief Strategic Officer Hudson (LV220 · epic-grade)]
He led his group to Daniel and dropped to one knee.
"Your Grace, the Duke!"
"Hudson reporting with his unit!"
Behind him, hundreds of thousands of Imperial warriors also knelt on one knee.
"Hail, Your Grace, the Duke!"
The voices thundered across the plaza, full of unstoppable momentum.
This scene caused countless players running tasks in the square to freeze in shock.
Was Faustus already this powerful?
Epic-grade NPCs are all his subordinates?!
Holy shit!
Most players didn’t even have the right to speak to epic-grade NPCs...
Daniel nodded in satisfaction as he looked over his officers and soldiers.
"Rise."
He turned to Hudson.
"From now on, you’re in charge of Polaris City’s defenses and troop training."
"In one month, I want to see a fighting-ready army."
Hudson and the others nodded solemnly.
"As you command!"
The army marched into the city and began setting up camp.
Polaris City was rapidly expanding, with city planning so large it was almost absurd—there was plenty of land to use.
Governor Roland hurried over, a look of delight on his face.
"Your Grace, the Duke, you’ve returned!"
"What’s the matter?"
"Polaris City’s urban prosperity, army strength, economic development—all have skyrocketed. It’s already taking shape as a strong city!"
"All of this is thanks to your brilliant leadership!"
Daniel’s eyes lit up. He opened the territory panel.
[Polaris City (Basic City)]
Population: 23,218,247
Commercial Prosperity: S-grade
Industrial Development: SS-grade
Agricultural Development: A-grade
Defense Level: S-grade
[Promotion Conditions: All met]
[Promotion Cost: 500 million gold coin]
[Promote?]
Daniel raised an eyebrow. He hadn’t expected the city to meet the promotion requirements so quickly.
"Confirm."
In the next moment, golden light burst from Lord’s Manor, instantly enveloping the entire city.
Boom—!
The ground shook.
The city walls automatically rose and thickened.
Streets widened, paved with smooth stone slabs.
Buildings upgraded, becoming more grandiose.
A massive magical barrier rose from Lord’s Manor, covering the entire city.
[Ding! Polaris City has been successfully promoted to "Mid-tier City"!]
[New Buildings: Intermediate Walls, Magical Shield, Large Warehouse, Mid-tier Barracks, Mid-tier Training Ground...]
Daniel nodded in satisfaction.
But he didn’t stop and opened the territory panel again.
[Polaris City (Mid-tier City)]
[Conditions for First-rank City:]
Population ≥ 100,000 ✓ (Met)
Army ≥ 50,000 ✓ (Met)
Commercial Prosperity ≥ A-grade ✓ (S-grade)
Industrial Development ≥ A-grade ✓ (SS-grade)
Agricultural Development ≥ A-grade ✓ (A-grade)
Defense Level ≥ A-grade ✓ (S-grade)
[Promotion Cost: 2 billion gold coin]
[Promote?]
Daniel clicked confirm without hesitation.
Boom—!
Stronger tremors shook from beneath the ground.
The golden light was even brighter than before, covering the entire city.
City walls rose from 10 meters to 20 meters.
Streets widened further, paved with finer stone slabs.
Buildings upgraded again; many wooden structures became stone.
Another protective barrier rose from Lord’s Manor, stacking with the previous one.
[Ding! Polaris City has been successfully promoted to "First-rank City"!]
[Rewards:]
Gold Coin +200 million
Contribution Points +10,000
First-rank City Construction Chest ×1
Daniel opened the chest.
[Obtained: Advanced Watchtower Blueprint ×1]
[Obtained: Magic Tower Construction Permit ×1]
[Obtained: Polar Knight Barracks Blueprint ×1]
His eyes lit up as he collected everything.
He then looked at the territory panel again.
[Polaris City (First-rank City)]
[Conditions for Main City Promotion: All met]
[Promotion Cost: 10 billion gold coin]
He continued the promotion.
Boom—!
The entire city trembled.
This time, the golden light was brighter than the previous two combined.
Walls rose from 30 meters to 50 meters, forged from silver-grade metal and stone.
Streets automatically widened to eight lanes, paved with magical stone bricks.
All buildings upgraded; wooden structures completely disappeared, replaced by stone and metal constructions.
A third protective barrier rose from Lord’s Manor, stacking with the previous two, forming three layers of protection.
At the city center, a massive portal was automatically generated, connecting the nine main cities.
At the city gate, a huge stone monument emerged from the ground, engraved in gold letters:
Polaris!
[Ding! Congratulations! Polaris City has been successfully promoted to "Main City"!]
[As the first player to promote their territory to Main City, the following rewards are granted:]
Gold Coin +500 million
Contribution Points +200,000
Attribute Points +2,000
Honorary Title: Lord of Pioneers
Special Building: Heart of the Main City (can be placed in Lord’s Manor to boost city-wide stats)
[Global Announcement!!!]
[Player "Faustus" has successfully promoted Polaris City to Main City, becoming the first player to own a Main City-level territory!]
[Polaris City officially becomes the 10th Main City of the Human Race!]
[This achievement has been recorded in the Stellar Chronicles, immortalized forever.]
World Channel erupted:
"Wait, can we even play this game anymore???"
"Main City??? Polaris City???"
"Wasn’t that the small frontier city Faustus bought? How did it become a Main City?!"
"How long has it been since Faustus bought it? And it’s already a Main City?!"
"I haven’t even become a Baron, and he’s not only a Duke but owns a Main City..."
"Nine Main Cities became ten?!"
"No way... there are now ten Main Cities for humans!"
"Holy shit! Invincible!"
"Faustus, the eternal God!"
Daniel closed the World Channel and looked at the city, now completely transformed.
Three months ago, it had been a dilapidated frontier town.
Now, it had become the 10th Main City.
Walls soared fifty meters high, engraved with defensive runes.
Several special buildings stood in the city, each radiating unique light.
On the skyline, the golden glow of Sanctuary Garden, the silver light of Temple of Eternal Prosperity, and the red glow of Eternal Core Furnace intertwined.
Wide streets were bustling with people; shops lined every corner, vibrant and lively.
Outside, the 1 million-strong army trained, their shouts shaking the air.
He had created an entirely new Chapter in Stellar’s history.
Taking a deep breath, he entered Lord’s Manor and placed the Heart of the Main City at the core.
A soft light instantly enveloped the city.
[Heart of the Main City Effects:]
All city residents +10% to all attributes
All city troops +15% to all attributes
All city commercial tax revenue +20%
All city industrial output +20%
All city agricultural output +20%
Immigration attraction probability +200%
Special talent attraction probability +300%
