chapters.title: Chapter 61 -61-Crafting Platinum-Grade War Machines from Gold-Grade Blueprints
paragraphs: Daniel nodded in satisfaction.
There was no doubt—the bonuses were substantial and would have a tremendous impact on Polaris City’s future development.
After roughly scanning the panel information, he turned to Roland.

"Roland, Polaris City has just been promoted to Main City, and affairs will be busy. For now, all administrative tasks are entrusted to you. I will recruit a group of reliable partners to help govern as soon as possible."
"Also, do everything you can to attract immigrants and increase food production to prepare for the upcoming war!"
Roland saluted solemnly.
"As you command, Your Grace!"
After giving a few more instructions, Roland hurried off with Daniel’s orders.
But Daniel did not idle. He immediately pulled a stack of blueprints from his pocket and began examining them.
[Gold-Grade Trebuchet Blueprint]
[Gold-Grade Ballista Blueprint]
[Gold-Grade Shield Wagon Blueprint]
He pulled out the first blueprint and began studying it.
With the aid of his legendary-grade engineering skills, the contents of the blueprint rapidly integrated into his mind.
The structural principles of all the machines decomposed and recombined in his brain again and again...
Ten minutes later:
[Ding! You have mastered "Trebuchet Manufacturing (Gold-Grade)"]
[Current Proficiency: Beginner]
He took out the prepared materials and began construction.
Half an hour later:
[Ding! You have manufactured "Trebuchet (Platinum-Grade)"]
[Quality: Platinum-Grade (exceeding original blueprint level)]
[Attributes:]
Attack Range: 500m → 800m
Attack Power: 5,000 → 12,000
Firing Rate: 3 shots/min → 5 shots/min
Durability: 10,000 → 25,000
Special Effect: 20% chance to trigger "Explosive Throw", doubling damage!
"Beautiful!"
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
The Earth Core Furnace enhancement was truly terrifying!
He had turned a gold-grade blueprint into a platinum-grade machine!
He glanced at the remaining blueprints, excitement flickering in his eyes.
With a major war approaching, the better prepared he was, the higher his chance of victory.
Time was of the essence—he immediately pulled out the second blueprint to study it.
Meanwhile, Polaris City’s construction continued at a furious pace.
The 1 million-strong army was setting up camp, with coordinated shouts echoing from the training grounds in the suburbs.
The temple’s light shone over the entire city, and the glow from the furnaces illuminated the night sky.
All of this was preparation for the imminent war.
And the young man intensely studying the blueprints was the very heart of it all.
Polaris City, Eastern District Tavern
Night had fallen, but this frontier city was more lively than during the day.
Streets bustled with people, shops shone brightly, and laughter and chatter echoed from the taverns.
Sunborn pushed open the tavern door. The smell of beer, roasted meat, and sweat hit him instantly.
"The captain is here!"
At a large table in the corner, six people simultaneously raised their cups.
Sunborn smiled as he walked over and sat in the empty seat.
The greatsword on his back gleamed faintly in the dim light. Intricate patterns etched into the blade marked it as high-grade equipment.
"Holy shit, Captain, this sword is insane!"
A tall, thin archer leaned in, eyes nearly pressed against the blade.
"Platinum-grade! It’s actually platinum-grade!"
"It’s the first time I’ve ever seen a living platinum-grade piece of equipment!"
Sunborn grinned, removing the sword and placing it on the table.
The six people immediately surrounded it, chattering excitedly.
"Attack Power +3,500, Strength +200, Agility +150, with the skill Solar Slash... these stats are ridiculous!"
"Stop looking! Even if you keep staring, it’s not yours."
"Captain, how many merit points did it cost to exchange for this?"
Sunborn took a sip from his cup, eyes filled with gratitude.
"50,000 merit points."
They all gasped.
"I spent half a month and only saved 3,000..."
"That’s why I’m thanking you guys," Sunborn said seriously, looking at them.
"If you hadn’t pooled your money to help me exchange merit points, I wouldn’t have gotten this sword."
"This sword is the squad’s shared property. When we fight bosses, I go in first, and everyone gets a share of any good loot."
"Captain, don’t make it sound so formal," said the priestess, waving her hand and smiling.
"You get stronger, the squad gets stronger, loot drops are more likely. Think of it as an investment, got it?"
"Exactly!"
Everyone else nodded in agreement.
Sunborn smiled, saying no more, but he mentally noted this favor.
"Oh, Captain, what about that thing you helped us with for the Doom Guild?"
The archer leaned in to ask.
Sunborn smacked his forehead.
"Almost forgot! It all went through!"
He opened the guild panel and handled each operation one by one.
[Ding! You have joined Doom Guild]
[Ding! You have joined Doom Guild]
The six people received notifications consecutively. First stunned, then erupting in cheers.
"Holy shit! We really got in!"
"I’ve been trying for half a month and couldn’t get through—Captain, how did you do it?"
Sunborn smiled.
"I have a friend in the guild management who helped pass the word."
"Captain, you’re incredible! Even the big guilds have trouble getting in!"
"Come on, let’s drink! Celebrate all of us becoming members of Doom Guild!"
The seven clinked cups and drank in one go.
Although Doom Guild had previously filled 100 million members at once, many were kicked out due to overcrowding.
Daniel had been too lazy to process them slowly, so he accepted everyone with one click.
In his free time, he began screening members.
For example, IDs with the prefix Stormbound were almost always troublemakers—Daniel kicked them out immediately.
Similarly, infamous IDs from previous servers received no mercy.
Through this, nearly 1 million member slots opened up.
But Daniel didn’t fill them randomly.
Instead, he used a recommendation system, letting elite frontier players recommend friends.
This increased loyalty and engagement while forming high-quality squads.
For instance, Sunborn’s seven-man squad had members of different levels and professions. Even the mage was a newly registered newbie.
Thanks to Sunborn’s recommendation, the mage was directly accepted into Doom Guild.
Experienced squads like this could level up quickly.
Other players, seeing Sunborn get attention, would similarly strive to contribute more to the guild, then invite their friends and family.
Showing off in front of familiar people—it was a point of pride.

chapters.title: Chapter 62 -62-Three Days to Build 200 War Machines
paragraphs: After a few rounds of drinking, the seven-person team had become slightly tipsy, when the priestess suddenly leaned in, lowering her voice to a mysterious whisper.

"By the way, do you all know? The bonus for secondary classes in Polaris City is higher than in all nine main cities!" Her eyes gleamed with excitement, and she glanced around to make sure no one else was listening.
"Really?" one of the teammates asked, raising an eyebrow.

"Of course it’s true!" she said, opening her in-game interface with a fluid motion. The screen glowed softly, displaying complex numbers and progress bars. She pointed at the statistics, her finger tracing the percentages carefully.
"Look at this. My alchemy proficiency gain here in Polaris City is fifty percent faster than in Luminara!" She emphasized the progress bar, watching the numbers tick upward.

"And the success rate—when I make intermediate potions in Luminara, the success rate is only around fifty-five percent. But in Polaris City, it reaches eighty-five percent!" Her voice was full of amazement, almost trembling with excitement.

"Plus, high-quality outputs happen frequently. When I make ten bottles of intermediate healing potions, I usually get three or four superior-quality ones!" She smiled, revealing the faint gleam of satisfaction in her eyes.
The group exchanged astonished glances, leaning closer to examine the glowing interface. The soft flicker of candlelight reflected off their eyes, highlighting their disbelief and curiosity.
"That’s insane," someone muttered quietly, his tone a mixture of awe and skepticism.
"You don’t believe me? Try it for yourself!" she said, her expression serious yet playful. Her hands hovered over the interface, ready to demonstrate the stats again.
Nearby, a table of other players overheard the conversation.
They leaned forward, intrigued, and joined in eagerly.

"She’s right," a blacksmith said, his voice deep and steady. "I’ve been forging iron in Polaris City for half a month, and my proficiency has almost increased by two levels!" He gestured toward his crafting station, where faint sparks still hovered in the air.

"Me too! Before, when I crafted equipment in the main city, succeeding on five out of ten items was lucky. Here, I succeed on eight out of ten!" another player added, brushing imaginary dust from his virtual gloves.

"And prices are low here, so materials are cheap. The equipment I make can still be sold in the nine main cities for a significant profit," another chimed in, calculating in his head the potential gold he could earn.
"The only downside is there are fewer NPCs, so you can’t take high-level quests," one player pointed out, frowning slightly as he considered the limitations.

"But there are plenty of construction tasks! Polaris City is investing heavily in development now, and there are quests every day. You can earn guild points faster than farming monsters!" another explained, tapping the table with excitement.

"I heard Doom Guild has a building for secondary-class players. What was it called... the Sanctuary Garden? Items made there get extra bonuses!" a fourth player added, leaning in, eager to share what he knew.

"Exactly! My friend got in, and when he came out, he was floating with excitement. He said the success rate was ninety-five percent and mind power doubled. I almost wanted to hit him!" someone said, laughing loudly, shaking his head at his friend’s exaggerated claims.
"Then why don’t you join?" someone asked, curiosity tinged with mockery.
"I haven’t joined Doom Guild!" the other replied, throwing back his head to laugh.
Laughter echoed across the tavern, mixing with the clinking of glasses and the low hum of conversation.
Amid the lively chatter, the priestess leaned closer to Sunborn, her voice dropping once again.
"Captain, there’s something I want to discuss with you," she said, her tone now serious and deliberate.
"What is it?" he asked, his eyes narrowing slightly as he tried to read her expression.
"I... I signed a long-term contract with one of the management members of Doom Guild," she admitted, her fingers nervously twisting a ring on her hand.
Sunborn froze for a moment, his mind racing to process the news.
"What kind of contract?" he asked cautiously.

"They provide materials and workspace, and I handle potion production. The potions go to the guild, and I earn a commission plus guild points," she explained, her voice growing animated as she described the arrangement.
She paused briefly, her eyes lighting up with a mixture of excitement and anticipation.
"Captain, do you know what this means?" she asked, leaning forward, almost bouncing in her seat.

"In Polaris City, with the Sanctuary Garden bonus, my success rate and potion quality are absurdly high. Before, producing one intermediate potion cost me five gold coins, and I could sell it for eight. That’s a profit of three," she continued, her hands moving in expressive gestures to illustrate the numbers.
"Now, the cost is still five, but the quality is higher. I can sell it for twelve, making seven! And with the high success rate, losses are minimal, so actual profits are even greater!"
"The guild supplies the materials, so I don’t advance any costs. I get three gold coins and 100 guild points per potion. I can make two or three hundred per day. Can you imagine the profit?"
Sunborn quickly calculated in his head and drew a sharp breath.
"Five or six hundred gold coins a day?!" he exclaimed, the numbers spinning in his mind as he tried to grasp the scale of her statement.
"Not just that! As my proficiency increases, I can craft even higher-level potions!" she said, her grin widening, eyes squinting in pure delight.
"Captain, once I get rich, I’ll treat you to a big feast!"
"Holy shit, sounds good!" he replied, a smile spreading across his face.
"I don’t need a feast," another team member interjected, grinning. "Just buy me a gold-grade bow and arrow, and I’m satisfied!"
The team erupted into laughter again, the sound carrying through the tavern. Sunborn watched them, smiling quietly to himself, feeling a surge of gratitude and luck.
Polaris City, Doom Guild, Faustus... it was all falling into place.
The tavern continued to buzz with activity, players sharing stories, checking their interfaces, and enjoying the evening glow.
The soft hum of magical energy from enchanted lanterns added a faint sparkle to the air.
Meanwhile, in Polaris City, the Duke’s Estate stood proudly, its white stone walls gleaming in the afternoon sun.
The estate, located in the city center near the Sanctuary Garden, resembled a small castle with multiple towers and high walls.
It had been specially built by Roland for Daniel, combining living quarters, office spaces, and meeting halls in one expansive structure.
Deep inside the estate was a building that looked unremarkable from the outside.
Its stone walls and simple wooden door blended seamlessly into the surrounding architecture.
Inside, however, it opened up into a vast space, filled with dozens of war machines in all shapes and sizes.
Towering trebuchets, robust ballistae, heavy shield wagons, and intricately designed siege ladders were arranged meticulously.
Each machine glimmered faintly with silver light, engraved with detailed runes that pulsed softly.
This was Daniel’s private workshop.
He stood before a platinum-grade trebuchet, carefully inspecting its components.
The polished wood shone under the soft lighting, and the ropes and mechanisms were taut and precise.
Three full days had passed, and he had barely slept, his focus entirely devoted to this work.
With the aid of a legendary-grade engineer and the amplification provided by the Eternal Core Furnace, his crafting speed was extraordinary.
Sparks flew occasionally as magical energy infused the metal parts.
Opening the system panel, Daniel scanned the completed war machines.

Trebuchet (platinum-grade) ×15
· Range: 800 meters
· Attack Power: 12,000
· Fire Rate: 5 shots per minute
· Special: 20% chance to trigger "Explosive Throw," doubling damage
Heavy Trebuchet (platinum-grade) ×8
· Range: 1000 meters

· Fire Rate: 3 shots per minute
· Special: 30% chance to trigger "Seismic Effect," +50% wall damage

· Range: 600 meters
· Attack Power: 8,000
· Penetration: Can pierce 5 enemies
· Special: 15% chance to trigger "Piercing," ignoring defense

The sheer efficiency and craftsmanship were unmatched, even in the entire empire.

chapters.title: Chapter 63 -63-Version 1.0 Major Event: War Horn
paragraphs: Ten minutes later, Hudson stood at the workshop entrance, utterly stunned.
He had seen countless War Machines over his years in the Imperial Army. He had faced every conceivable battlefield scenario.
Yet even he was shocked.
Nearly two hundred machines, perfectly arranged in the massive space, each glowing faintly silver and radiating immense power.
He approached a trebuchet, reaching out to touch the runes engraved on it.
"As expected... all Platinum-Grade..."
His voice trembled.
"Your Grace, the Duke... these... you built all of these?"
Daniel nodded.
"Three days."
Hudson fell silent.
He had seen countless skilled engineers in the Imperial Army.
But someone building 200 platinum-grade war machines in three days—he had never seen that before.
"Your Grace, these war machines are worth a fortune."
He drew a deep breath, speaking seriously.
"One Platinum-Grade Trebuchet sells for at least 5 million gold coins on the market."
"Nearly two hundred of them here... total value exceeds 1 billion gold coins."
"And they are priceless in terms of demand!"
Daniel smiled.
"1 billion? Roughly."
He paused, then said:
"Transport all these war machines to Luminara."
Hudson froze.
"Your Grace, you intend to sell them?"
"No."
Daniel shook his head.
"I am donating them to the Empire."
Luminara, War Bureau
Kasel was in his office handling documents when suddenly a commotion erupted outside.
Frowning, he stood and opened the door.
He, too, froze.
In the War Bureau plaza, nearly two hundred War Machines were neatly arranged.
Trebuchets, ballistae, shield wagons, battering rams... every type was present.
Each machine glimmered with faint silver light and was engraved with intricate runes.
Officials from the War Bureau, passing players, and NPCs who had heard the news all surrounded the machines.
"Holy shit! These are all Platinum-Grade War Machines?!"
"Am I seeing things? So many platinum-grade machines?!"
"How much is this worth?!"
"Who sent them?"
"I don’t know..."
Kasel hurried over for a closer look.
The more he examined, the more he was shocked.
Trebuchet, Platinum-Grade, attack range 800m, 300m further than the Empire’s standard Gold-Grade.
Ballista, Platinum-Grade, incredible penetration, can pierce five layers of shields.
Shield Wagon, Platinum-Grade, immune to arrows, reduces magic damage.
Each was a masterpiece.
Each exceeded the Empire’s standard Gold-Grade by a huge margin.
He turned to the officer in charge of receiving the machines.
"Who sent these?"
The officer swallowed hard.
"P... Polaris City, Duke Faustus."
Kasel’s pupils contracted.
At that moment, Daniel appeared in the plaza.
He approached Kasel and said calmly:
"Minister Kasel, these war machines are a donation from Polaris City on behalf of its citizens to the Empire."
"I hope they will be of use in the upcoming war."
Kasel was silent for three seconds.
Then he straightened, placing his right fist over his chest and saluting solemnly.
"Your Grace, on behalf of the Empire, we thank you for your generosity."
"These war machines will save countless Imperial soldiers’ lives."
"Your deeds will be remembered by the Empire forever."
[Ding! You have donated Platinum-Grade War Machines ×199 to the Empire]
[Merit points calculated based on machine quality and quantity...]
[Merit Points gained: 6,000,000,000]
[Current Merit Points: 6 billion]
[Ding! Congratulations! You have completed S-Rank Task "Full-Scale War Preparation"!]
[Task Rating: SSS (overachieved)]
[Rewards:]
Merit Points +100,000,000
Gold Coin +500,000
Contribution Points +50,000
Honorary Title: Pillar of War
Kasel took a deep breath as he looked at the machines.
Six billion merit points.
Combined with previous exchanges, the Duke’s merit points had likely surpassed the heavens.
He spoke seriously:
"Your Grace, since you have completed the war preparation task, next..."
He handed over a scroll.
"This is the latest imperial decree!"
[Ding! You have received SSS-Rank Task: Sound the War Horn!]

[Task Background: The Empire has discovered that goblins, beastfolk, dark elves, and dwarf insurgents are secretly forming an alliance to wage war on humans. Rather than passively defending, it is better to strike first!]
[Task Objectives (must complete at least one):]
Occupy Territory: Capture at least 10 territories of non-human races.
Eliminate Enemies: Kill at least 2 billion non-human units (soldiers and civilians; merit points calculated by level).
Pillage Resources: Capture at least 100 million non-human population (as slaves or labor).
[Task Rewards:]
Merit Points, Gold Coins, Contribution Points: calculated by completion rate
Special Reward: completing all three objectives grants the title "King of War"!
[Task Duration: Long-Term]
[Special Notes: This task is a special Empire-issued war mission for adventurers. It aims to consume the Strength of non-human races. The more enemies killed, the greater the rewards.]
Daniel read the task description, his eyes narrowing slightly.
2 billion kills, 100 million captured, 10 territories.
The scale of this mission was unprecedented.
In his previous life, he had faced similar tasks—but that was two months after the game launched.
Now, it was less than a month in.
The timeline had accelerated drastically!
Clearly, the butterfly effect of this life had created a massive impact.
But this did not hinder Daniel’s plans. Faster timelines meant earlier acquisition of resources and more opportunities for the player community to gain experience.
He looked at Kasel.
"Can all adventurers accept this task?"
Kasel nodded.
"Yes! The Empire hopes to weaken the Strength of these major non-human races first through this war."
"After all, the real threat is not only these non-human races."
He said this with deep meaning.
Daniel understood.
Behind the non-human races, there were even greater powers at work.
"For the Empire!"
Daniel saluted briefly.
Kasel returned the salute.
"For the Empire!"
At that moment, a blood-red system announcement echoed across the Stellar world.
[Global Emergency Announcement!!!]
[Ding! Under the leadership of player "Faustus," Universe #616 has successfully triggered Version 1.0 Major Event—"War Horn"!]
[Version Event Details:]
All players must choose a faction—Humans, Non-Human Races, or Neutral.
Note: Once chosen, the faction cannot be changed until the event ends.
Faction Warfare: Players of different factions can attack each other and earn points.
Faction Leaderboard: Real-time ranking; rewards distributed after the event ends.
[Faction Selection Time: 24 hours]
[Unselected players default to Neutral faction]
[Event Duration: Until the end of the Version Event]

chapters.title: Chapter 64 -64-Polaris Legion: Armed to the Teeth
paragraphs: [World Channel]
"Version Event?! No way, Faustus is at it again?!"
"Faustus, are you the GM? You have to be the GM! If you don’t answer, we’ll just assume yes!"
"Two events in a month... this efficiency..."
"Faction selection? Humans, non-human races, Neutral? How do we choose?"
"Obviously pick Humans! Universe #616 is Faustus’ territory!"
"Exactly! Follow the master, eat meat and drink soup!"
"I’m only level 20... can I participate?"
"Yes! Killing lower-level non-human races still earns points."
"Wait, I’m level 15... will I get one-shot?"
"Don’t worry, group up! We have numbers!"
"Did anyone pick the non-human faction?"
"Pick non-human? Are you crazy? Wait to get surrounded by Human forces?"
"Neutral’s safe."
"Neutral’s boring. I want to kill enemies!"
"Charge! For EXP!"
Polaris City
Daniel hurried back, watching the celebration on World Channel, a small smile on his lips.
The Version Event had been moved up.
No matter—he had already prepared new resources.
He opened the system war store and began operating.
[Ding! You spent 3 billion merit points to exchange for "Exp Card (Gold-Grade) ×1,500,000"]
[Exp Card Effect: Grants 1,000,000 EXP when used]
[Ding! You spent 2.5 billion merit points to exchange for "Standard Equipment Chest (Silver–Gold Grade) ×1,500,000"]
[Chest contains random equipment of corresponding grade]
[Ding! You spent 1.5 billion merit points to exchange for "Companion Egg (Bronze–Silver Grade) ×300,000"]
[Companion Egg randomly hatches, bound to the user]
[Ding! You spent 800 million merit points to exchange for "Skill Book (D–A Grade) ×300,000"]
[Skill Book randomly grants corresponding class skill]
Total spent: 6.8 billion merit points.
Daniel remained calm.
He opened the guild warehouse and stored all these resources inside.
[You stored in Guild Warehouse: Exp Card ×1,500,000]
[You stored in Guild Warehouse: Standard Equipment Chest ×1,500,000]
[You stored in Guild Warehouse: Companion Egg ×300,000]
[You stored in Guild Warehouse: Skill Book ×300,000]
Then he summoned two people.
The first was Polaris Vice Legion Commander—Victor.
[Vice Legion Commander Victor (LV245 · Epic-Grade NPC)]
"Victor, prioritize distributing these resources to the Polaris Legion."
Daniel allocated a batch of materials.
[Standard Equipment Chest ×1,000,000]
[Skill Book ×100,000]
In addition, there were gold coins and food supplies.
Victor stared at the pile in shock.
"Your Grace, all of this... for the warriors?"
"Yes," Daniel nodded.
"War is about to begin. I need a capable army."
"And now I have plenty of money, so every warrior will be fully equipped—armed to the teeth!"
"Distribute these resources as quickly as possible."
Victor took a deep breath and saluted solemnly.
"Understood! Polaris will not disappoint you!"
The second was Doom Legion Vice Legion Commander, promoted from a high-ranking officer.
[Vice Legion Commander Alan (LV235 · Epic-Grade NPC)]
In the current Polaris City and Doom Guild system, one notable feature was that nearly all high-level core positions were NPCs.
This was not coincidental—it was Daniel’s deliberate design.
NPC loyalty was system data, clear and visible.
NPCs under contract could not betray—slave contracts, employment contracts, military post contracts all had system enforcement.
Players’ loyalty, on the other hand, was invisible and unreliable.
Friends today could turn on each other tomorrow for a single piece of equipment.
Alliances today could dissolve tomorrow, players jumping to enemy guilds.
Daniel had seen too many examples of this.
Moreover, the average player level was around 40, with most gear being iron-grade.
Polaris Legion NPC warriors started at level 80, minimum iron-grade equipment, and elite units were all silver-grade or higher.
In terms of high-end combat power, the gap was enormous.
Furthermore, managing a city or commanding an army required specialized knowledge and military literacy, which players currently lacked.
Players have their own goals and interests—grinding monsters is fine, but managing? Not a chance.
In Daniel’s plan, at this stage, it was best to let players focus on grinding, completing quests, and earning points.
When they matured, and true talent emerged, promotion would be considered later.
For now, NPC management was the safest choice.
"Alan, I have a task for you."
Daniel looked at the resolute man before him.
"Train the adventurer groups in the Doom Legion for me."
He allocated a batch of resources and funds from Polaris City’s stockpile.
"These are the legion’s starting resources."
"Recruit members in Doom Guild and form a capable fighting force."
"Any questions?"
Alan’s eyes lit up.
"No! Your Grace, rest assured!"
After handling this, Daniel opened the guild exchange interface.
He placed the remaining resources inside.
[Guild Shop Update!]
[Exp Card (Gold-Grade): 500 guild points each]
[Standard Equipment Chest (Silver–Gold Grade): 500 guild points each]
[Companion Egg (Bronze–Silver Grade): 1,000 guild points each]
[Skill Book (D–A Grade): 300 guild points each]
[Guild Channel]
"Holy shit! The guild warehouse just updated!"
"Exp Cards! 100 guild points each! I exchanged mine!"
"The equipment chests are god-tier! I got a gold-grade armor!"
"Companion eggs are god-tier! I hatched a silver-grade pet!"
"I want one too! Don’t take it!"
"Wait, check the exchange requirements!"
"To redeem these, you must be a Regular Member. Better resources require Elite-Grade. Top-tier discounted items require Core-Level membership!"
"Holy shit! I’m only a trainee-level member, I can’t exchange!"
"Why? Everyone’s equal, why the discrimination? I refuse!!"
"Exactly, equality! Why treat differently? Faustus is discriminating! Friends, let’s unite...!"
[Ding! Players "TearsofForest" and "StarlightWanderer" have been removed from the guild for inappropriate remarks. All guild members are reminded to speak responsibly and maintain unity!]
[Guild Leader Notice: Those chasing equality and freedom, leave the guild. Anyone kicked will never set foot in Polaris City!]
The golden announcement scrolled five times in the guild channel to ensure visibility.
The channel went silent.
"Faustus is ruthless. People who don’t understand the situation deserve this!"
"Exactly. Someone was even hitting Faustus himself—what did they expect? Faustus, please post a guild point task, I have no money to reach Elite-Grade!"
"Hahaha, I’m a core member, I can exchange everything..."
"Charge! Buy gold coins to exchange for guild points!"

chapters.title: Chapter 65 -65-Stormbound Guild Joins the Non-Human Faction
paragraphs: "Hahaha, I’m a core member, I can exchange everything..."
"Charge! Buy gold coins to exchange for guild points!"
[World Channel]
"Doom Guild is giving out goodies again!"
"300,000 Exp Cards! 300,000 pieces of equipment! 300,000 Companion Eggs! 300,000 Skill Books!"
"I should have joined Doom Guild earlier!"
"Exactly! Now it’s so hard to get in, even if you meet the requirements, you might not be accepted!"
"Yeah... I’ve been applying for so long and still got rejected, sob..."
"Ha! That’s nothing. I applied fifty times and got rejected. Damn auditors, did I offend them?"
"Bro, you didn’t break any rules, right? Doom Guild auditors are NPCs, which means Faustus himself personally rejected your application..."
"Hahaha, so funny... not ignored, just flat-out rejected..."
"F*** you... nonsense!"
Meanwhile, inside Doom Guild, another announcement rang out.
[Doom Guild Announcement: Doom Legion is now recruiting all members!]
Recruitment Requirements: Level 30+ and 100 copper coins
Legion Benefits: Participate in legion activities to earn massive guild points; outstanding performance receives additional rewards
Maximum Legion Size: 5 million
Registration: Private message Vice Legion Commander Alan
The guild channel erupted again.
"Doom Legion? Clearly for combat—looks like the guild is about to make a big move!"
"Five million members! That’s huge!"
"I’m in! Faustus must’ve seen my request—guild points too!"
"Guild points? I’m in!"
"I’m only level 27, not 30..."
"Go level up! You still have time!"
Half an hour later, Alan reported.
"Your Grace, Duke, 4.2 million have signed up."
"There are still 800,000 spots left."
Daniel nodded.
"Keep recruiting!"
Out of nearly 100 million guild members, 5 million was still not even full.
Daniel found this surprising.
The level 30 minimum was not very high; the top player tier was already around level 70.
He turned to look out the window.
In Polaris City’s nightscape, Sanctuary Garden emitted a soft glow, and the Eternal Core Furnace lit half the sky.
The War Horn was about to sound!
Blackstone Plains
Located on the border between Human territory and the non-human races’ domain.
The terrain was flat, soil poor, and barren, covered entirely in black rocks—hence the name.
Normally, few people ventured here, aside from occasional merchant caravans and scouts.
But now, a human village on the plain’s edge was engulfed in bloodshed.
Flames shot into the sky, screams echoed.
"Kill them all! Leave no one alive!"
Vantheon stood at the village entrance, staff in hand.
A pillar of fire descended from above, blasting a wooden house to splinters.
The screams inside abruptly ended.
[Ding! You killed 7 Human villagers. Gained 70 faction points.]
A cruel smile curved his lips.
Behind him, thousands of Stormbound Guild members poured into the village like a tide, killing anyone in sight and burning every house.
Elderly, women, children—none escaped their blades.
"Guild Leader, east side cleared!"
"Guild Leader, a few hiding in the west cellar... found them too, heh heh!"
"Kill!"
Vantheon nodded in satisfaction.
He opened the faction panel, watching the points steadily climb.
[Stormbound Guild Current Faction Points: 127,846]
[Global Non-Human Faction Ranking: #1]
Three days ago, when the Version Event began and the faction selection window popped up, he had barely hesitated.
Humans?
Bah! That damned Faustus had kicked all Stormbound Guild members out of Doom Guild.
Fine—but even after fifty applications, Vantheon himself had been flatly rejected.
Never had he been so humiliated.
Since Faustus wouldn’t allow him in, he would join the non-human races faction!
Let Faustus see the consequences of crossing him.
To Vantheon’s delight, the first task for joining the non-human faction was to capture a human village.
Even better, the system rewarded faction points for each kill.
Faction points could be exchanged at the non-human races’ supply depot for rare resources.
So, although the original task required taking the village, for more points, he ordered a full massacre.
In just three days, over twenty guild members had completed the faction-class change into rare non-human classes.
Some became Beastfolk Berserkers, drastically increasing Strength.
Some became Dark Elf Assassins, doubling Agility.
Some became Goblin Priests, gaining bizarre curse abilities.
Vantheon himself class changed into an Inferno Mage.
This was a hidden Dark Elf class, capable of manipulating both shadows and fire—terrifying power.
[Inferno Mage (S-Rare Class)]
Level: 60
Skills:
Shadowfire Arrow: Fires arrows infused with shadow and fire, dealing 320% damage
Shadow Shelter: Enter shadows, immune to physical attacks for 3 seconds
Flamestorm: Summons fire rain over a wide area
Shadowfire Explosion: Explodes surrounding shadow flames, dealing massive damage
Vantheon stared at his attribute panel, brimming with pride.
"Faustus, just wait."
"When I gather enough points to exchange for legendary equipment, I’ll come for you first!"
"Then we’ll see who’s truly number one among humans!"
He kicked a corpse aside and strode toward the next house.
Behind him, the night of Blackstone Plains glowed red with fire.
Three days later
Bearclaw Highlands
Daniel stood atop a hill, surveying the horizon.
On his shoulder, a small stone dragon dozed, lightly snoring.
Thanks to Daniel’s constant feeding, the little dragon had been sleeping more, and each time it woke, its power had grown.
[Earthmount Dragon (Ancient Dragon · LV89)]
Strength: 2,240
Constitution: 2,240
Agility: 970
Intelligence: 970
Daniel petted its head. The dragon nuzzled his hand, then resumed sleeping.
Three figures flew in from a distance and landed beside him.
[Polaris Legion Chief of Staff Hudson (LV230 · Epic-Grade)]
[Doom Legion Vice Legion Commander Alan (LV235 · Epic-Grade)]
[Polaris Legion Vice Commander Victor (LV245 · Epic-Grade NPC)]
All three saluted simultaneously.
"Your Grace, the Duke!"
Daniel nodded.
"Have the investigations been completed?"
Hudson stepped forward, spreading out a massive map.
"Your Grace, the Dwarven tribes deep within Bearclaw Highlands have been fully scouted."
He pointed to a red skull marker on the map.
"This is their main city—Ironforge."
"Its scale is comparable to a human main city: population ~10.8 million, standing army 1.8 million."
"The Dwarven High Warlord is personally stationed there."
"There are 12 epic-grade elites, and countless sub-epic-grade units."

chapters.title: Chapter 66 -66-Marching Against the Mid-Tier Dwarven Tribes
paragraphs: Daniel raised an eyebrow.
A stronghold comparable to a human main city, personally guarded by the Dwarven High Warlord...
And an army of 1.8 million!
Indeed, this would be a tough nut to crack.
Victor spoke up.
"However, they’re not invincible."
"Around Ironforge, there are 37 small-to-medium Dwarven tribes, ranging from basic cities to First-Rank Cities."
"These tribes are obstacles on our march, but also..."
He looked at Alan.
Alan continued.
"...they’re excellent training grounds."
"Your Grace, we have drafted the operational plan."
He unfurled another map, dense with arrows and markers.
[Operational Plan Overview]
Phase 1: Clear the Periphery
Objective: Eliminate 37 small-to-medium tribes surrounding Ironforge
Force Composition: Doom Legion (5 million adventurers) as main force, Polaris Legion provides support
Mission Goal: Defeat enemies, pillage resources, and train adventurer units
Estimated Duration: 7 days
Phase 2: Siege of Ironforge
Objective: Cut off Ironforge from the outside world
Force Composition: Polaris Legion as main force; Doom Legion handles vanguard and attrition
Mission Goal: Contain without direct assault, deplete enemy resources, wait for the right opportunity
Estimated Duration: 3–5 days
Phase 3: Full Assault
Objective: Capture Ironforge, eliminate the Dwarven High Warlord
Force Composition: Full army engagement
Mission Goal: Completely destroy Dwarven main forces, pillage population and resources
Estimated Duration: 1–2 days
Each phase contained detailed troop movements and siege arrangements, showcasing the professionalism of the three generals.
Daniel nodded slightly at the plan.
"Good thinking."
He looked at Hudson.
"Hudson, anything you wish to add?"
Hudson’s voice was grave.
"Your Grace, I have a concern."
"Speak."
"The defenses of Ironforge are formidable. Dwarven war machines are renowned across the continent."
"Their walls are equipped with at least 500 gold-grade or higher ballistae and trebuchets."
"They also possess unique machines: [Thunder Cannon] and [Lava Thrower], whose power rivals platinum-grade."
"A frontal assault will result in heavy casualties."
Daniel paused for a second. Then he smiled.
"Casualties?"
He opened his bag and pulled out a scroll.
[Seraphic Revival (Supreme-Grade)]
Effect: Sacrifice a large amount of gold coins to revive any dead NPC.
"Hudson, do you know what this is?"
Hudson froze.
Daniel said calmly:
"With this, I can revive fallen warriors. Our troops can fight for the Empire without hesitation, spilling blood freely!"
"Need resources? I have money."
"Need more soldiers? I can recruit them."
"Need strength? One battle and we have it."
He tucked away the scroll and looked into the distance.
"I don’t fear losses."
"What I fear is not having a chance to train."
Hudson drew a deep breath.
He looked Daniel in the eye and saluted solemnly.
"Your Grace, you are brilliant!"
Victor and Alan were also thrilled.
"So, Your Grace, when do we depart?"
Daniel looked at the map, placing his finger on Ironforge.
"Now!"
Bearclaw Highlands, North Wind Howling
A 6 million-strong army advanced steadily.
At the front was Doom Legion’s 5 million adventurers, a black mass stretching beyond sight.
They were divided into hundreds of formations, each commanded by an officer, and all coordinated under Vice Legion Commander Alan.
Despite the massive numbers, there was no chaos.
Daniel stood atop a small hill at the rear, nodding with satisfaction.
"Alan, well done."
Alan grinned beside him.
"Your Grace, these players may not be individually strong, but they follow orders."
"I set rules: disobedience results in expulsion; good performance earns guild points."
"With sufficient rewards, obedience is guaranteed!"
Daniel nodded.
Indeed, Alan had grasped the players’ weak points.
As long as guild points and rewards were in place, they would obey—even running unarmed into enemy lines wouldn’t be a problem.
Behind the players was Polaris Legion’s 1 million NPC army.
This was the true elite force.
All units were level 80+, fully equipped and highly trained.
Infantry formations, archer formations, cavalry formations, mage corps, summoners, priests...
All worked in harmony, moving with precision.
Most striking of all were the War Machines at the center.
Over 300 trebuchets, ballistae, and shield wagons, operated by specialized engineer units, advanced steadily.
Many were platinum-grade machines personally crafted by Daniel, each devastatingly powerful.
"Report—!"
A mounted scout galloped in and reined before Hudson.
"General Hudson, a Dwarven tribe spotted 20 li ahead!"
"Mid-tier City scale, approx. 100,000 troops, walled defenses!"
Hudson’s spirits lifted.
"It’s finally arrived."
He looked at Daniel.
"Your Grace, shall we attack?"
Daniel nodded.
"Follow the plan."
Anvil Tribe – Mid-Tier City Dwarven Settlement
Built into the mountains, surrounded by a 20-meter stone wall, with archer towers every 100 meters.
Dwarven warriors lined the walls, axes and warhammers in hand, eyes vigilant.
In the center, a massive forge belched smoke, clanging sounds of hammering never ceasing.
Anvil Chieftain Bronzebeard stood on the wall, brow furrowed.
"Humans... why are they attacking us?"
He could not understand.
The Dwarves had been secretly supporting goblin activities, but in a very discreet manner.
Humans should not have discovered this so quickly.
Yet the evidence was before him.
Scouts reported that millions of troops were advancing toward Anvil Tribe.
"Chieftain, what should we do?"
A dwarf officer asked anxiously.
Bronzebeard took a deep breath.
"Alert Ironforge of the human attack immediately and request reinforcements!"
"Also, order preparations for battle! Activate all war machines!"
"Let the humans witness the might of dwarves!"
With his command, the war machines on the walls activated.
[Dwarven Thunder Cannon (Platinum-Grade) ×50]
A unique Dwarven magical artillery piece, crafted from silver-grade and thundersteel, engraved with lightning runes.
Fires a compressed lightning sphere that explodes on impact.
Range: 1,000m
Attack Power: 25,000
Special Effect: Lightning explosion radius 50m, double damage to metal armor
[Dwarven Lava Thrower (Platinum-Grade) ×80]
A special trebuchet launching molten lava spheres mined from the earth’s core.
Explodes on impact, splattering lava that burns continuously.
Range: 800m
Attack Power: 20,000
Special Effect: Splash damage, burns for 10 seconds
[Dwarven Steam Repeater (Gold-Grade) ×200]
A Dwarven engineering marvel, powered by steam to rapidly fire bolts, far faster than ordinary ballistae.
Range: 600m
Firing Rate: 30 bolts/min
Attack Power: 5,000
Special Effect: Pierces +2 targets

sentences.text: Daniel raised an eyebrow.
A stronghold comparable to a human main city, personally guarded by the Dwarven High Warlord...
And an army of 1.8 million!
Indeed, this would be a tough nut to crack.
Victor spoke up.
"However, they’re not invincible."
"Around Ironforge, there are 37 small-to-medium Dwarven tribes, ranging from basic cities to First-Rank Cities."
"These tribes are obstacles on our march, but also..."
He looked at Alan.
Alan continued.
"...they’re excellent training grounds."
"Your Grace, we have drafted the operational plan."
He unfurled another map, dense with arrows and markers.
[Operational Plan Overview]
Phase 1: Clear the Periphery
Objective: Eliminate 37 small-to-medium tribes surrounding Ironforge
Force Composition: Doom Legion (5 million adventurers) as main force, Polaris Legion provides support
Mission Goal: Defeat enemies, pillage resources, and train adventurer units
Estimated Duration: 7 days
Phase 2: Siege of Ironforge
Objective: Cut off Ironforge from the outside world
Force Composition: Polaris Legion as main force; Doom Legion handles vanguard and attrition
Mission Goal: Contain without direct assault, deplete enemy resources, wait for the right opportunity
Estimated Duration: 3–5 days
Phase 3: Full Assault
Objective: Capture Ironforge, eliminate the Dwarven High Warlord
Force Composition: Full army engagement
Mission Goal: Completely destroy Dwarven main forces, pillage population and resources
Estimated Duration: 1–2 days
Each phase contained detailed troop movements and siege arrangements, showcasing the professionalism of the three generals.
Daniel nodded slightly at the plan.
"Good thinking."
He looked at Hudson.
"Hudson, anything you wish to add?"
Hudson’s voice was grave.
"Your Grace, I have a concern."
"Speak."
"The defenses of Ironforge are formidable.
Dwarven war machines are renowned across the continent."
"Their walls are equipped with at least 500 gold-grade or higher ballistae and trebuchets."
"They also possess unique machines: [Thunder Cannon] and [Lava Thrower], whose power rivals platinum-grade."
"A frontal assault will result in heavy casualties."
Daniel paused for a second.
Then he smiled.
"Casualties?"
He opened his bag and pulled out a scroll.
[Seraphic Revival (Supreme-Grade)]
Effect: Sacrifice a large amount of gold coins to revive any dead NPC.
"Hudson, do you know what this is?"
Hudson froze.
Daniel said calmly:
"With this, I can revive fallen warriors.
Our troops can fight for the Empire without hesitation, spilling blood freely!"
"Need resources?
I have money."
"Need more soldiers?
I can recruit them."
"Need strength?
One battle and we have it."
He tucked away the scroll and looked into the distance.
"I don’t fear losses."
"What I fear is not having a chance to train."
Hudson drew a deep breath.
He looked Daniel in the eye and saluted solemnly.
"Your Grace, you are brilliant!"
Victor and Alan were also thrilled.
"So, Your Grace, when do we depart?"
Daniel looked at the map, placing his finger on Ironforge.
"Now!"
Bearclaw Highlands, North Wind Howling
A 6 million-strong army advanced steadily.
At the front was Doom Legion’s 5 million adventurers, a black mass stretching beyond sight.
They were divided into hundreds of formations, each commanded by an officer, and all coordinated under Vice Legion Commander Alan.
Despite the massive numbers, there was no chaos.
Daniel stood atop a small hill at the rear, nodding with satisfaction.
"Alan, well done."
Alan grinned beside him.
"Your Grace, these players may not be individually strong, but they follow orders."
"I set rules: disobedience results in expulsion; good performance earns guild points."
"With sufficient rewards, obedience is guaranteed!"
Daniel nodded.
Indeed, Alan had grasped the players’ weak points.
As long as guild points and rewards were in place, they would obey—even running unarmed into enemy lines wouldn’t be a problem.
Behind the players was Polaris Legion’s 1 million NPC army.
This was the true elite force.
All units were level 80+, fully equipped and highly trained.
Infantry formations, archer formations, cavalry formations, mage corps, summoners, priests...
All worked in harmony, moving with precision.
Most striking of all were the War Machines at the center.
Over 300 trebuchets, ballistae, and shield wagons, operated by specialized engineer units, advanced steadily.
Many were platinum-grade machines personally crafted by Daniel, each devastatingly powerful.
"Report—!"
A mounted scout galloped in and reined before Hudson.
"General Hudson, a Dwarven tribe spotted 20 li ahead!"
"Mid-tier City scale, approx.
100,000 troops, walled defenses!"
Hudson’s spirits lifted.
"It’s finally arrived."
He looked at Daniel.
"Your Grace, shall we attack?"
Daniel nodded.
"Follow the plan."
Anvil Tribe – Mid-Tier City Dwarven Settlement
Built into the mountains, surrounded by a 20-meter stone wall, with archer towers every 100 meters.
Dwarven warriors lined the walls, axes and warhammers in hand, eyes vigilant.
In the center, a massive forge belched smoke, clanging sounds of hammering never ceasing.
Anvil Chieftain Bronzebeard stood on the wall, brow furrowed.
"Humans... why are they attacking us?"
He could not understand.
The Dwarves had been secretly supporting goblin activities, but in a very discreet manner.
Humans should not have discovered this so quickly.
Yet the evidence was before him.
Scouts reported that millions of troops were advancing toward Anvil Tribe.
"Chieftain, what should we do?"
A dwarf officer asked anxiously.
Bronzebeard took a deep breath.
"Alert Ironforge of the human attack immediately and request reinforcements!"
"Also, order preparations for battle!
Activate all war machines!"
"Let the humans witness the might of dwarves!"
With his command, the war machines on the walls activated.
[Dwarven Thunder Cannon (Platinum-Grade) ×50]
A unique Dwarven magical artillery piece, crafted from silver-grade and thundersteel, engraved with lightning runes.
Fires a compressed lightning sphere that explodes on impact.
Range: 1,000m
Attack Power: 25,000
Special Effect: Lightning explosion radius 50m, double damage to metal armor

A special trebuchet launching molten lava spheres mined from the earth’s core.
Explodes on impact, splattering lava that burns continuously.

chapters.title: Chapter 67 -67-Human Warriors Are Insane
paragraphs: Looking out across the battlefield, countless ordinary defensive installations were set up along the city walls.
Ballistae, trebuchets, rolling logs, giant stones—everywhere there were mechanisms designed to crush invaders.
Bronzebeard gazed at these machines, his mind momentarily steadying.
"Come on, humans," he sneered. "Let me show you the true might of dwarven technology!"
Five miles away, Alan stood behind a massive shield wagon. Through his telescope, he carefully observed the approaching enemy horde.
"Well... this defense is formidable," he muttered. He lowered the telescope and began issuing orders.
"First, second, and third corps, advance from the left, center, and right!"
"Shield wagon units, take point and protect the infantry!"
"Archers, follow the shield wagons and suppress the walls!"
"Mages and summoners, hold your positions. Once their siege engines fire, destroy them immediately!"
"Cavalry, flank positions. When the gates open, charge in!"
One command after another flew down the ranks. Ten minutes later, the battle began.
"Attack!"
The horn sounded.
A massive human army of five million players surged forward.
At the front were the shield wagons.
Twenty-five platinum-grade shield wagons formed a single line.
Behind each wagon marched hundreds of infantry.
The heavy metal panels of the shield wagons could resist both arrows and stones.
They were the perfect cover for a siege assault.
Behind the shield wagons, dense lines of archers moved forward.
Crouched, taking advantage of the wagons’ protection, they were ready to fire back at any moment.
Further behind were the mages, summoners, and clerics.
Each prepared to provide fire support or healing as necessary.
On both flanks, the cavalry waited patiently, poised to strike the instant the gates opened.
Boom!
Boom—boom!
From the walls, Thunder Cannons roared to life.
Lightning spheres shrieked through the air, smashing into the shield wagons.
Crash!
Explosions rocked the battlefield, deafening the advancing troops.
One shield wagon took a direct hit. Its entire frame trembled violently, and cracks appeared across its protective plating.
"Holy shit! That’s intense!"
The players behind it flinched in fear.
But the bombardment was far from over.
Next, the Lava Throwers opened fire. Molten rocks plummeted from the battlements, striking players indiscriminately.
Boom!
The lava exploded, spraying scalding molten rock across the battlefield.
Any player touched by the lava instantly screamed in pain as their health rapidly drained.
Within moments, some fell to the ground with zero HP.
"Healers! Healers!"
"Get us healed, you idiots!"
"Look at my leg—it’s on fire, oh my god!"
"Don’t panic! Spread out! Everyone scatter!"
The battlefield descended into chaos.
But soon, the players stabilized their formation.
"Archers, fire back!"
Arrows rained from the human ranks, pinning down the dwarven archers.
"Mages and summoners, target those Thunder Cannons! Destroy them!"
Magic flared across the battlefield. Fireballs, ice arrows, lightning bolts, wind blades—they all struck the walls.
Shadows, ghosts, skeletal warriors, and magical beasts appeared atop the walls, summoned to disrupt the dwarves’ defense.
Crash!
A Thunder Cannon exploded under a barrage of fireballs.
Crash!
A Lava Thrower froze mid-operation, iced over by a precise magical attack, and became useless.
"Yes! That’s it!"
Alan waved his command baton vigorously, shouting above the noise.
"Shield wagon units, advance! Get closer to the walls!"
"Engineers, prepare the ladders!"
The shield wagons pushed forward under a relentless hail of fire.
One hundred meters.
Eighty meters.
Fifty meters.
Finally, the wagons reached the base of the walls.
"Ladders! Set up the ladders!"
Engineers dashed forward under fire, placing ladders against the battlements.
Players began climbing rapidly.
On the walls, dwarven warriors hurled rolling logs and massive stones down at the attackers.
But instead of hearing the expected screams of agony, a strange sound rose from below.
Excited shouts echoed from the human soldiers.
"Whoa... is this really a siege? This game feels so real!"
"Hahaha! Awesome! My head got smashed, holy shit, but I still have 1000 HP left!"
"Not gonna lie, these little dwarves are ugly as hell, every one of them has a messy beard!"
"I love this game! This is exactly the kind of battle I live for!"
"Keep climbing! Watch how I take these dwarves down!"
Players fell from stones, arrows, and lava, but more kept climbing, stepping over fallen comrades with unrelenting excitement.
This chaotic scene terrified the dwarves.
Hands that were tossing stones trembled uncontrollably.
Finally, the first human player reached the top of the wall.
"Hehe, I’m up—let’s go!"
He swung his weapon, lunging at the nearest dwarf warrior.
One by one, the second, third, and fourth players joined him. Soon, a brutal melee erupted along the battlements.
Meanwhile, at the city gates, battering rams smashed furiously against the reinforced doors.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
The thick wooden gates cracked with each strike.
"Keep pushing, brothers!"
"The gate’s down to one-tenth of its HP!"
Crash!
Finally, the gates collapsed.
"The gates are open!"
"Charge!"
"Go, Munich Squad, follow me!"
The cavalry poured into the city like a tidal wave.
The dwarven settlement’s fate was sealed.
Anvil clan chief, Bronzebeard, stood atop the walls, watching the battlefield descend into chaos. His face was pale as iron.
Facing millions of humans, he had never imagined holding the city would be possible.
Yet, he had expected a longer defense.
The walls were formidable. The humans seemed weak, some barely above level thirty.
And yet, they attacked like lunatics, fearless even in the face of death, their faces alight with excitement.
"Chief, retreat! We’ll cover you!"
A dwarf general gripped Bronzebeard’s arm.
He opened his mouth to speak, but before he could say anything, a sudden golden light pierced his chest.
He looked down at the massive gaping hole in his chest, disbelief written across his face.
Then he collapsed with a thundering crash.
[System Notice: Congratulations! You and your army have successfully conquered the "Anvil Tribe (Mid-tier City)"!]
[Battle Results:]

Dwarven Warriors Captured: 21,236
War Machines Seized: Thunder Cannon ×37, Lava Thrower ×52, Steam Crossbow ×143
Equipment Captured: Gold-grade ×327, Platinum-grade ×43, Epic-grade ×2
Resources Acquired: Silver-grade ore ×1,270,000 units, Thundersteel ×830,000 units, countless other materials
[Faction Points Earned: 9,263,760]
[Merit Points Earned: 2,847,200]
[Global Announcement!!!]
Under the leadership of player "Faustus," the human alliance has successfully conquered the dwarven mid-tier city "Anvil Tribe"!
This marks the first large-scale victory of humans over non-human races!
All participating human players receive an additional +1000 points!
This achievement has been recorded in the annals of war!

chapters.title: Chapter 68 -68-Reviving NPCs, Warrior Loyalty
paragraphs: All participating human players receive an additional +1000 points!
This achievement has been recorded in the annals of war!
[World Channel]
"Holy shit! We won big!"
"Faustus is awesome!"
"Five million against a hundred thousand, and we still lost over ten thousand? Those dwarves are too strong!"
"You don’t understand. Dwarves’ War Machines are the strongest in the entire continent. Just winning is impressive!"
"Exactly! I swear I saw one Thunder Cannon wipe out over a hundred people in a single shot!"
"My friend is in the Doom Legion. He said their seventh army lost over two thousand people..."
"Nonsense. The dwarves defending the city are incredibly strong. The important thing is, we won easily!"
"What about Faustus’ Polaris Legion? How were their losses?"
"Probably very few. Polaris Legion didn’t fight as the main force. I think Faustus deliberately held them back. He wanted us to level up and earn points."
"Of course. Polaris Legion’s NPCs are armed to the teeth. They are highly skilled professional soldiers. If they had gone all out, what chance would we have had?"
"Exactly. They are elite NPCs, and we are a player army. How can we compare?"
"Maybe Faustus was afraid that the NPCs would be lost too early. One NPC gone is gone forever. Players can die and respawn."
"Enough talk. I’m going to level up. Next siege, I’ll be at the front!"
At the core of the Anvil Tribe.
Daniel sat in the seat originally belonging to the clan chief, listening to the logistics officer’s report.
"Your Grace, the loot has been inventoried."
"Besides the war machines and equipment seized on the battlefield, we also found..."
The logistics officer opened the ledger and read out each item.
"Three dwarven war factories, capable of producing gold-grade and lower War Machines."
"Two silver-grade ore veins, producing about 500,000 silver-grade units annually."
"One thundersteel vein, producing about 300,000 thundersteel units annually."
"Five iron-grade ore veins, producing about 2,000,000 iron-grade units annually."
"Various rare metal reserves: approximately 5,000,000 units."
"Additionally..."
The officer paused, then continued.
"We found a large quantity of non-human races’ equipment in the warehouses."
"This includes beastfolk berserker axes, goblin priest staves, dark elf assassin daggers..."
"There was even an order for sea people weapons and equipment!"
He handed over a document.
Daniel looked at it and raised his eyebrow.
It was a trade order between the dwarves and the sea people.
It included 1,000 sets of gold-grade equipment and 100 sets of platinum-grade equipment. In exchange, the sea people would provide deep-sea pearls, coral, and young deep-sea beasts.
"Interesting," Daniel said, putting away the order.
The sea people had indeed joined in.
They were an amphibious race with long-standing interest in land-based resources.
Throughout Stellar’s history, they often clashed with land races.
Now they were trading with dwarves?
Daniel looked at the logistics officer.
"And the prisoners?"
"Your Grace, a total of 180,000 dwarves were captured."
"Of these, over 20,000 are warriors, the rest are civilians."
"As you ordered, all are in custody awaiting processing."
Daniel nodded.
"No need to keep them here. Send all of them to Polaris City, to the Eternal Core Furnace."
"Let them work in the forges."
The logistics officer froze.
"Your Grace, dwarves are stubborn. They might not obey..."
Daniel smiled.
"Simple. Those who don’t obey, we kill."
"Those who obey, can live."
"There will always be some who fear death."
The officer nodded thoughtfully.
After finishing the loot, Daniel left the Lord’s Manor.
Hudson, Victor, and Alan approached him.
"Your Grace, battle losses have been counted," Hudson said seriously.
"Polaris Legion warriors killed: 326."
"I have collected the bodies of the fallen warriors."
Daniel nodded.
Although the Polaris Legion did not fight as the main force, facing the dwarves’ elite warriors meant the players were difficult to kill efficiently. Masses could be wiped out instead.
To end the battle quickly, Victor had led a ten-thousand-strong elite squad to engage, and some casualties occurred.
"Very well. I will revive them," Daniel said.
He used the [Seraphic Revival] device.
[System Notice: You have spent 12,000,000 gold coins to revive Polaris Legion warriors ×326]
Golden light flashed.
The cold, lifeless bodies stood again.
They stared at their hands in confusion, then all looked at Daniel, full of excitement and fervor.
"Thank you, Your Grace!"
Daniel waved.
"You are warriors who shed blood for the Empire. I will never let a single warrior die on the battlefield."
"For the Empire!"
This short speech instantly ignited the warriors’ passion.
Their Duke possessed the power to revive the dead. Their eyes filled with battle intent and loyalty.
All warriors knelt on one knee, their loyalty to Daniel reaching one hundred percent.
"For the Empire! For Your Grace!"
The roar was deafening.
Daniel looked at Alan with satisfaction.
"And the Doom Legion?"
Alan gave a wry smile.
"Your Grace, Doom Legion lost 175,847 people, with countless injuries."
Daniel nodded calmly.
"No matter. Adventurers can respawn directly in the main city."
"Although many lost levels and are complaining..."
Daniel thought for a moment.
"Give them some compensation."
"Each gets 100 guild points and 10 gold coins."
"Tell them that rewards will double for outstanding performance in the next battle!"
Alan’s eyes lit up.
"Your Grace is wise!"
The next day, the army continued marching.
For the following seven days, they killed gods and humans alike.
LV70 Copper Hammer Tribe, 20,000, crushed.
LV85 Steel Mane Tribe, 105,000, destroyed.
LV92 Flame Tribe, 350,000, wiped out.
Along the way, thirty-seven medium and small dwarven tribes were eradicated.
Each conquered tribe provided resources and prisoners.
Daniel’s desk overflowed with loot lists.
Polaris Legion warriors’ levels increased steadily.
Doom Legion players leveled fastest, gaining experience through continuous battles.
Although dying caused some to lose levels, survivors’ levels increased rapidly.
Players noticed dwarves dropped high-quality equipment and resources more frequently.
With guild point and gold coin compensation, complaints vanished instantly.
In their place, a high battle spirit surged throughout the army.

It included 1,000 sets of gold-grade equipment and 100 sets of platinum-grade equipment.
In exchange, the sea people would provide deep-sea pearls, coral, and young deep-sea beasts.
"Interesting," Daniel said, putting away the order.
The sea people had indeed joined in.
They were an amphibious race with long-standing interest in land-based resources.
Throughout Stellar’s history, they often clashed with land races.
Now they were trading with dwarves?
Daniel looked at the logistics officer.
"And the prisoners?"
"Your Grace, a total of 180,000 dwarves were captured."
"Of these, over 20,000 are warriors, the rest are civilians."
"As you ordered, all are in custody awaiting processing."
Daniel nodded.
"No need to keep them here.
Send all of them to Polaris City, to the Eternal Core Furnace."
"Let them work in the forges."
The logistics officer froze.
"Your Grace, dwarves are stubborn.
They might not obey..."
Daniel smiled.
"Simple.
Those who don’t obey, we kill."
"Those who obey, can live."
"There will always be some who fear death."
The officer nodded thoughtfully.
After finishing the loot, Daniel left the Lord’s Manor.
Hudson, Victor, and Alan approached him.
"Your Grace, battle losses have been counted," Hudson said seriously.
"Polaris Legion warriors killed: 326."
"I have collected the bodies of the fallen warriors."
Daniel nodded.
Although the Polaris Legion did not fight as the main force, facing the dwarves’ elite warriors meant the players were difficult to kill efficiently.
Masses could be wiped out instead.
To end the battle quickly, Victor had led a ten-thousand-strong elite squad to engage, and some casualties occurred.
"Very well.
I will revive them," Daniel said.
He used the [Seraphic Revival] device.
[System Notice: You have spent 12,000,000 gold coins to revive Polaris Legion warriors ×326]
Golden light flashed.
The cold, lifeless bodies stood again.
They stared at their hands in confusion, then all looked at Daniel, full of excitement and fervor.
"Thank you, Your Grace!"
Daniel waved.
"You are warriors who shed blood for the Empire.
I will never let a single warrior die on the battlefield."
"For the Empire!"
This short speech instantly ignited the warriors’ passion.
Their Duke possessed the power to revive the dead.
Their eyes filled with battle intent and loyalty.
All warriors knelt on one knee, their loyalty to Daniel reaching one hundred percent.
"For the Empire!
For Your Grace!"
The roar was deafening.
Daniel looked at Alan with satisfaction.
"And the Doom Legion?"
Alan gave a wry smile.
"Your Grace, Doom Legion lost 175,847 people, with countless injuries."
Daniel nodded calmly.
"No matter.
Adventurers can respawn directly in the main city."
"Although many lost levels and are complaining..."
Daniel thought for a moment.
"Give them some compensation."
"Each gets 100 guild points and 10 gold coins."
"Tell them that rewards will double for outstanding performance in the next battle!"
Alan’s eyes lit up.
"Your Grace is wise!"
The next day, the army continued marching.
For the following seven days, they killed gods and humans alike.
LV70 Copper Hammer Tribe, 20,000, crushed.
LV85 Steel Mane Tribe, 105,000, destroyed.
LV92 Flame Tribe, 350,000, wiped out.
Along the way, thirty-seven medium and small dwarven tribes were eradicated.
Each conquered tribe provided resources and prisoners.
Daniel’s desk overflowed with loot lists.
Polaris Legion warriors’ levels increased steadily.
Doom Legion players leveled fastest, gaining experience through continuous battles.
Although dying caused some to lose levels, survivors’ levels increased rapidly.
Players noticed dwarves dropped high-quality equipment and resources more frequently.
With guild point and gold coin compensation, complaints vanished instantly.
In their place, a high battle spirit surged throughout the army.

chapters.title: Chapter 69 -69-At Ironforge: War Behemoths
paragraphs: One week later.
The army finally arrived at the gates of Ironforge!
This was a true mighty city.
The walls rose fifty meters high, forged from a mix of obsidian and silver-grade alloy, inscribed with countless defensive runes.
On the walls, rows upon rows of War Machines were stationed. At least a thousand of them.
At the city gates, two hundred-meter-tall dwarf stone statues stood on either side, exuding a terrifying aura.
These were the dwarves’ guardian statues, said to be capable of reviving during battle, though with limited uses.
Inside the city, a massive forge towered into the sky. Its flames dyed half the horizon red.
Ironforge was the main city of all dwarves in the region.
Its population numbered eight million, with 1.8 million soldiers.
Even a legendary level-280 dwarf supreme commander was stationed there.
Daniel stood on a high mountain outside the city, gazing at the towering fortress.
Behind him, six million troops were arrayed and ready.
He took a deep breath.
"Give the order: rest in place for one day."
"Tomorrow..."
His eyes sharpened.
"Attack the city!"
On Ironforge’s walls, dense formations of dwarves stood ready.
Two million warriors in total.
This was the combined force from Ironforge and all surrounding tribes.
They wore heavy plate armor and wielded battle axes or warhammers.
Their eyes burned with battle intent.
Every fifty meters along the wall, an arrow tower stood.
Each tower mounted blackgold-grade Thunder Cannons and Lava Throwers.
More frighteningly, inside the walls stood thirty towering War Machines.
They were twenty meters high.
The dwarves called them War Behemoths.
[Dwarf War Behemoth (blackgold-grade)]
These were colossal war machines, combining offense and defense.
Their appearance resembled a giant metallic tortoise.
Three Thunder Cannons rested on its back.
A catapult was hidden under its belly.
Its limbs were thick and powerful. Every step it took shook the ground.
Height: 20 meters
Length: 35 meters
Weight: approximately 500 tons
Armor thickness: 500 millimeters (silver-grade alloy)
Weapon configuration: Thunder Cannon ×3, Lava Thrower ×2, Giant Warhammer ×2
Special effect: can absorb magical damage and convert it to energy; can release [Thunder Roar] to stun surrounding enemies
Ironforge had thirty of these War Behemoths.
Piloting them were the dwarves’ elite Ironwrath warriors.
Every one was at least blackgold-grade or higher.
Any human legion facing such defenses would find them extremely difficult.
But at the foot of the city, the player army was buzzing with excitement.
[Legion Channel]
"Holy shit! Did you see those things? So cool!"
"What are those? Mechanical beasts?!"
"Dwarves’ War Behemoths! I saw them in the Luminara Dwarf Manual! Blackgold-grade!"
"Damn! Blackgold-grade? How tough is that?"
"Who cares how tough! Kill them and get the loot!"
"Exactly! We might lose some XP if we die, but a single blackgold-grade drop is huge!"
"Charge, brothers!"
"Charge what? The battle hasn’t even started!"
"Can’t we just be excited?"
"What do you think Faustus will do?"
"He’ll probably crush them directly. Do you not know his strength?"
"True..."
As the players chatted, a deep horn sounded from the mountaintop.
Woo—!
Everyone looked up in unison.
A massive flag rose from the mountain top.
It was entirely silver, with a radiant star embroidered at the center.
Golden tassels lined its edges.
The flag flapped in the wind, radiating a subtle sense of authority.
The Polaris banner!
Then, a gigantic black shadow descended from the sky.
Roar—!
The thunderous roar of a dragon echoed through the clouds.
It was a fifty-meter-long dragon, its scales resembling jagged rock.
A row of sharp stone spines ran along its back.
Its wings stretched wide, blotting out the sun.
An Earthmount Dragon!
On its back stood a figure.
Daniel!
He wore the Windstrider set.
Black Dragon Wings spread behind him.
In his hands, he held Moon Reaper.
Sunlight fell behind him, casting a golden glow.
[Legion Channel]
"Holy shit!!!"
"So cool!!!"
"That’s Faustus!!!"
"I’m fired up!"
"Charge! Follow the master!"
"Wait! He hasn’t given the order yet!"
"I can’t control myself! This is a battle of millions!"
"Exactly. In old online games, even ten-thousand-player battles were impressive. Now, millions!"
"Insane... I’m a university professor and I took a week off for this. Stellar is my life now..."
"The NPC generals’ battle skills are so professional. This game is top-tier!"
On Ironforge’s walls, a dwarf general in golden armor stepped forward.
[Ironwrath General Steelhammer (LV245·epic-grade)]
He tilted his head, staring at the dragon and the figure on its back.
His face was grim.
"Humans!"
His voice thundered across the battlefield.
"You truly wish to fight the dwarves?!"
"I admit your strength is not weak, but Ironforge is not a bone you can chew easily!"
"Retreat now, and we may let you go!"
"Otherwise—"
He raised his hand.
All War Machines on the wall simultaneously targeted the sky.
"We will make sure you never return!"
Daniel looked down at him, a slight smile on his lips.
"Too much talk."
He raised Moon Reaper.
Shattering Comet!
Arrowstorm!
Both skills released simultaneously.
A stream of light shot into the sky, splitting into thousands of golden arrows.
At the same time, countless arrows rained down from above, merging with the split arrows.
The sky filled with golden lights, falling like a meteor shower.
They smashed against the walls.
Boom! Boom! Boom! Boom! Boom!
Explosions thundered.
The walls were engulfed in golden fire.
When the dust settled, everyone gasped.
The so-called indestructible walls had been torn open, a hundred-meter-long breach.
Debris littered the ground.
Countless dwarf warriors on the walls were killed or injured.
Over ten War Machines were destroyed.
[Legion Channel]
"Holy shit!!!"
"One arrow destroyed the wall!!"
"Amazing! Is he really a player? Stronger than NPCs!"
"This is Faustus’ strength? I love it! Stellar’s number one!"
"Stop talking! Charge! The gates are open!"
"Brothers, move!"
"Damn humans!"
Five figures leapt from the city toward Daniel.
Leading them was Ironwrath General Steelhammer.
[Ironwrath General Steelhammer (LV265·epic-grade)]
Skills: [Ironwrath Battle Intent], [Great Axe Slash], [War Roar], [Steel Body], [Rage Burst]
Four more figures followed him.
[Ironwrath Knight Thunderhammer (LV258·epic-grade)]
[Ironwrath Berserker Firehammer (LV260·epic-grade)]
[Ironwrath Swordsman Stonebrute (LV255·epic-grade)]
[Ironwrath Warrior Windaxe (LV259·epic-grade)]
Each was epic-grade.
Each had at least 800,000 HP.
Seeing them, Hudson’s face changed.

chapters.title: Chapter 70 -70-Supreme-Grade Ascendant Starstone
paragraphs: "Your Grace! Watch out!"
He drew his longsword and was about to charge forward.
Alan raised his command saber, ready to order the entire army to attack.
But Daniel lifted a hand to stop them.
"No need."
He said lightly.
"Leave this to me."
Although he was still stuck at level 100, his four core attributes were now absolutely terrifying—enough to shake the heavens and move the earth.
Even the lowest of his four core attributes exceeded 15,000!
Add the bonuses from the Windstrider Set, the army standard, and various buffs...
His true combat power far surpassed the numbers on his character sheet.
Steelhammer swung his great axe, crossing the sky as he charged.
"Human, die before me!"
Daniel raised his bow. On the empty string, a golden, razor-sharp arrow naturally formed—clearly, a Nature’s Arrow!
The next instant, an Aetherlance shot forth!
The golden spear tore through the sky.
Steelhammer didn’t even have time to react. In a blink, the golden spear pierced his chest!
Boom—!
The horrifying damage number exploded, and his HP instantly dropped to zero.
Steelhammer’s body shattered into countless fragments midair, flames erupting into the sky!
[Ding! You have slain General Steelhammer of Ironwrath (LV265 · Epic-Grade BOSS)]
[Faction Points +500,000]
[Merit Points +100,000]
[Special Item Acquired: Ascendant Starstone ×1]
Silence fell over the battlefield.
Beside Daniel, generals Hudson, Victor, and Alan were utterly stunned.
The strength of this Dwarf was undeniable. Even they likely wouldn’t have been able to defeat him.
After all, Dwarves are not only adept at forging equipment and machinery—they are also formidable in combat.
As a general of this great Dwarf clan, his abilities and gear were anything but ordinary.
These generals had already prepared to lay down their lives to protect the Duke.
Yet the Duke had barely lifted a finger, and in an instant, had obliterated this Dwarf warrior?
This... is the combat power of a level 100 archer?
On the city walls, countless Dwarf warriors gaped, their eyes filled with disbelief.
That was General Steelhammer of Ironwrath!
A level 265 Epic-Grade powerhouse!
One of the thirty strongest warriors of the Dwarf clan!
And he was killed in a single arrow?
The remaining four Ironwrath warriors froze for a moment—not in fear, but in fury—and charged simultaneously.
Among the Dwarves, there was no concept of fear or retreat on the battlefield.
If one hesitated, it would be a disgrace to the entire clan!
"For our general!"
Daniel remained expressionless.
He silently admired their stubborn courage. Then, four golden streaks of light shot forth.
The next instant, four figures exploded midair, fireworks illuminating the battlefield!
[Ding! You have slain Ironwrath Knight Thunderhammer (LV258 · Epic-Grade)]
[Ding! You have slain Ironwrath Berserker Firehammer ...]
[Ding! ... You obtained Epic-Grade Equipment ×3, Thunder Verdict (Legendary-Grade) ×4]
[Faction Points +1,200,000]
[Merit Points +240,000]
[World Channel]
"Am I seeing this right? Five arrows, five epic-grade NPCs down?"
"Holy crap, those are 200+ level epic-grade bosses!"
"Seriously, I struggle to kill a level 50 elite-grade, and this god just oneshots epic-grade?"
"No kidding! Faustus is strong, but this is just over the top. One arrow each!"
"The leader’s HP was longer than my life... killed by one arrow?!"
"That damage... I’m shaking!"
"How much attack power does Faustus have?"
"I don’t know, but I do know he’s a god."
"Holy shit... is he the god of humans?!"
Daniel ignored the frenzy in the World Channel.
He looked down at the special item in his inventory.
[Ascendant Starstone (Legendary-Grade / Special Material)]
Effect: When used, grants an Epic-Grade NPC the potential to ascend to Legendary-Grade.
Description: A gem imbued with mysterious Strength, crucial for an Epic-Grade warrior to break into Legendary-Grade. Extremely rare.
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
Ascendant Starstone!
This was essential for an Epic-Grade NPC to ascend to Legendary-Grade, its value beyond doubt.
Without a second thought, he opened the guild warehouse and placed the Ascendant Starstone inside.
[Ding! You sold an item to Doom Guild: Legendary-Grade Ascendant Starstone (Legendary-Grade), price 1 Copper Coin. Millionfold Boost triggered!]
[Since the item is a special material, please choose: Quality Boost / Quantity Boost!]
"Quality boost!"
[Ding! Congratulations! You received 1 Gold Coin and upgraded Ascendant Starstone to Supreme-Grade!]
[Ascendant Starstone (Supreme-Grade / Special Material)]
Effect: When used, grants an NPC the potential to ascend to Supreme-Grade.
Description: Said to contain a fragment of the Strength of a Creator God. The key to breaking into Supreme-Grade. In the history of the continent, fewer than three have ever been produced.
Daniel drew a deep breath.
Supreme-Grade!
This was the current ceiling of power.
If an NPC could ascend to Supreme-Grade, they would become a strategic-level force!
He carefully stored the Ascendant Starstone.
Now was not the time to use it.
He would need to find the most suitable NPC.
He turned his attention to the other four spoils.
[Thunder Verdict (Legendary-Grade / Single-Use Item)]
Effect: When used, deals damage equal to 1,000% of the user’s attack power to all enemies within a 10,000-mile radius.
Usage Limit: Single-use. Consumed upon activation.
Description: A forbidden weapon passed down in the Dwarf clan, containing the Strength of the Thunder God. Damage potential is immense.
Daniel’s lips curved slightly.
1,000% of the user’s attack power, over 10,000 miles.
If a top-tier powerhouse wielded this... it would be like a humanoid nuclear bomb.
Now, multiplied by his attack power... at least several million damage!
Who in Ironforge could withstand it?
The Dwarf general had clearly intended to save it for a decisive moment.
Too bad—he had been killed by a single arrow.
Now, it belonged to Daniel.
Daniel stored the spoils and looked down at Ironforge.
Countless Dwarf warriors on the walls stared at him in terror.
No one dared to charge.
Five arrows, five epic-grade NPCs down—under such terrifying suppression, who would dare throw themselves into death?
Without hesitation, Daniel raised his bow.
Shattering Comet!
Arrowstorm!
He unleashed both skills in combination.
A golden storm of arrows rained down, covering the entire wall.
Boom boom boom—!
Explosions never ceased.
Dwarf warriors on the walls fell in waves.
War machines exploded one after another.
Arrow towers collapsed one by one.
Within just a minute, not a single Dwarf remained standing on the walls.
