He would need to find the most suitable NPC.
He turned his attention to the other four spoils.
[Thunder Verdict (Legendary-Grade / Single-Use Item)]
Effect: When used, deals damage equal to 1,000% of the user’s attack power to all enemies within a 10,000-mile radius.
Usage Limit: Single-use.
Consumed upon activation.
Description: A forbidden weapon passed down in the Dwarf clan, containing the Strength of the Thunder God.
Damage potential is immense.
Daniel’s lips curved slightly.
1,000% of the user’s attack power, over 10,000 miles.
If a top-tier powerhouse wielded this... it would be like a humanoid nuclear bomb.
Now, multiplied by his attack power... at least several million damage!
Who in Ironforge could withstand it?
The Dwarf general had clearly intended to save it for a decisive moment.
Too bad—he had been killed by a single arrow.
Now, it belonged to Daniel.
Daniel stored the spoils and looked down at Ironforge.
Countless Dwarf warriors on the walls stared at him in terror.
No one dared to charge.
Five arrows, five epic-grade NPCs down—under such terrifying suppression, who would dare throw themselves into death?
Without hesitation, Daniel raised his bow.
Shattering Comet!
Arrowstorm!
He unleashed both skills in combination.
A golden storm of arrows rained down, covering the entire wall.
Boom boom boom—!
Explosions never ceased.
Dwarf warriors on the walls fell in waves.
War machines exploded one after another.
Arrow towers collapsed one by one.
Within just a minute, not a single Dwarf remained standing on the walls.

chapters.title: Chapter 71 -71-Thunder Verdict, Apocalyptic Might
paragraphs: Daniel sheathed his bow and leapt down from the dragon’s back.
Black Dragon Wing unfolded behind him, and he streaked through the sky like a shooting star, landing on a breach in the city wall.
He glanced inside Ironforge.
Countless Dwarf warriors still occupied the frontline core, along with thirty War Behemoths, and a few hidden elite combatants.
But Daniel ignored them, instead pulling out the [Thunder Verdict].
"Let’s see what this can do."
The item resembled a crystal orb, within which tiny sparks of lightning danced and roiled.
He immediately activated the item, then hurled it deep into the city.
[Ding! You have used [Thunder Verdict (Legendary-Grade)]!]
In the next instant, the sky changed color.
What had been a clear day instantly darkened.
Storm clouds surged from every direction, converging into a massive vortex above Ironforge.
At the center, blinding lightning crackled.
Rumble—!
A hundred-meter-thick bolt of lightning descended from the heavens.
Then a second, a third...
Countless bolts struck simultaneously, covering all of Ironforge!
Boom boom boom boom boom—!
The heavens shattered, the earth quaked.
Buildings collapsed, walls crumbled, and Dwarf warriors evaporated in panic and confusion.
The War Behemoths—armored machines said to resist even powerful magic—were paper-like before the apocalyptic lightning.
One by one, they exploded, the dozens of Ironwrath warriors inside unable to even scream.
Five seconds.
The lightning lasted a mere five seconds.
But when it dissipated...
Ironforge’s walls and defensive structures had vanished entirely.
In their place lay ruins: scorched earth, shattered stones, smoking debris, and countless Dwarf corpses...
Daniel opened his system panel.
[Ding! You have slain Dwarf Warrior ×1,647,236]
[Ding! You have slain Ironwrath Warrior ×128]
[Ding! You have destroyed War Behemoth ×30]
[Ding! You have slain ...]
The notifications ran for a full minute.
Total Kills: 2,284,847!
Faction Points: +132,694,800!
Merit Points: +26,496,940!
For a moment, even Daniel, the architect of this devastation, was stunned.
He had expected the destructive power to be terrifying—but not this utterly catastrophic.
At that moment, a deafening roar came from the depths of the ruins.
"Humans—!"
"How dare you blatantly violate the peace treaty between our races, attacking our lands and slaughtering our people!"
"You will be a stain on history! The Dwarves will never forgive you!"
A massive figure rose from the rubble.
A five-meter-tall Dwarf, muscles coiled like steel, beard and hair white as snow, clad in golden armor, wielding a colossal warhammer.
His eyes burned with fury as they locked on Daniel.
Beneath him stood an even larger War Behemoth.

This giant was an entire size larger than normal Behemoths, forged from Blackgold-Grade, equipped with six Thunder Cannons on its back, twelve trebuchets in its belly, and limbs encased in thick armor.
[Dwarf Overlord · Forgestone (LV280 · Legendary-Grade BOSS)]
HP: 2,000,000 (including War Behemoth bonus)
Skills:
[King of the Dwarves]: Command-level aura, decreases all enemy attributes by 20% within range
[War Behemoth Mastery]: Complete control over War Behemoth; boss and Behemoth share HP
[Wrath of Thunder]: Calls down lightning on a wide area
[Seismic Crush]: Stomps the ground to cause earthquakes
[Steel Fortress]: Behemoth enters defensive stance, +500% defense for 60 sec
[Mutual Destruction]: At <10% HP, detonates Behemoth, dealing 1000% damage to all nearby enemies
[War Behemoth · Forgestone (Blackgold-Grade)]
HP: 2,000,000 (shared with Overlord)
Weapons: Thunder Cannon ×6, Lava Thrower ×4, Giant Warhammer ×2
Special: Absorbs magical damage; can unleash [Thunder Roar]
Daniel raised an eyebrow at the stats.
Level 280 Legendary-Grade NPC, 2 million HP, plus War Behemoth...
Yes, much stronger than the previous foes.
But... that’s it.
He drew his bow again.
Arrowstorm!
Golden arrows rained down from the sky, striking the War Behemoth.
Boom boom boom boom boom—!
Explosions deafening.
When the smoke cleared, the Behemoth still stood.
Over a third of its HP gone.
Overlord Forgestone was internally shocked. No wonder the five previous top-tier warriors were killed without resistance!
The Behemoth he controlled had substantial physical resistance and mitigated massive explosive damage—but even so, a single strike had removed a third of its HP!
This human commander was absurd—standing idle would only mean death!
Yet hope wasn’t completely gone. He noted Daniel was only level 100. If the human’s attack power was astronomical, there must be weaknesses elsewhere!
With that thought, he roared, maneuvered the Behemoth forward, and attempted to close the distance for melee combat.
Daniel, unaware of the strategy, merely admired the courage.
If he had known Forgestone’s thought process, he would have been impressed—logical, yet outmatched by a true hexagonal warrior, fully optimized for offense, defense, and crowd control.
Unhurried, he drew his bow.
Aetherlance!
The golden spear tore through the sky, instantly piercing the Behemoth’s chest.
Boom—!
HP instantly zeroed.
The Behemoth charged a few more steps, then collapsed in a thunderous crash.
Overlord Forgestone fell from the machine, lying on the ground, eyes wide, staring helplessly at the sky.
He couldn’t comprehend how these humans dared—let alone how they achieved it.
"Ho... How is this possible...?"
[Ding! You have slain Dwarf Overlord · Forgestone (LV280 · Legendary-Grade BOSS)]
[Faction Points +2,000,000]
[Merit Points +500,000]
[Skill Book Acquired: Wind’s Embrace (SSS-Grade) ×1]
[Special Item Acquired: Legendary-Grade Fire Stone ×1]
Daniel glanced at the skill book.
[Wind’s Embrace (SSS-Grade)]
Effects:
Wind Acceleration: +500% movement speed, +500% attack speed for 240 sec (Cooldown 5 min)
Wind’s Restraint: Locks one target in place, unable to move, attack, or use skills for 10 minutes (Cooldown 1 hr)
Wind Silence: The restrained target is simultaneously silenced, unable to use any skills
Description: A legendary wind forbidden technique that binds enemies with the Strength of wind, freezing them in time. The restrained can only watch death descend.
Daniel’s eyes gleamed.
Ten minutes of hard CC plus silence!
Combined with Aetherlance, who could withstand this?
He turned to the other loot.
[Fire Stone (Legendary-Grade / Material)]
Effect: Contains the pure Strength of Fire Element, usable for forging, enchanting, or activating special items
Description: Essence condensed from the depths of the Fire Elemental Plane. Extremely rare.
Daniel sold it directly to the guild.
[Ding! You sold to Doom Guild: Legendary-Grade Fire Stone, price 1 Copper Coin. Millionfold Boost triggered!]
[Since this is an elemental material, choose: Quality Boost / Quantity Boost!]
"Quality boost!"
[Congratulations! You received 1 Gold Coin and obtained Fire Elemental Core (Supreme-Grade)]
[Fire Elemental Core (Supreme-Grade / Material)]
Effect: Contains the core Strength of Fire Element, crystallized from the Fire Elemental Plane. Only Elemental Lord-level beings can condense it.
Daniel drew a deep breath.
Fire Elemental Core!
One of the ten core components needed for the Chronoverse Prologue Codex.
He had collected one so quickly!
He carefully placed the core in his inventory, adding it to his previous Primordial Core and Angel Holy Crystal—his collection was growing steadily.
[Server Announcement!!!]
[Under the leadership of player "Faustus," the human alliance has successfully captured the Dwarves’ main city, "Ironforge"!]
[This marks an Epic-Grade victory for humans against a non-human race!]
[All participating human players receive +5,000 extra points!]
[Player "Faustus" performed exceptionally in this battle, earning bonus rewards: +1,000 Attribute Points, +100,000 Contribution Points!]
[This achievement has been recorded in the annals of war!]

chapters.title: Chapter 72 -72-Legendary Warrior Aliris
paragraphs: [Server Announcement!!!]
[Under the leadership of player "Faustus," the human alliance has successfully captured the Dwarves’ main city, "Ironforge"!]
[This marks an Epic-Grade victory for humans against a non-human race!]
[All participating human players receive +5,000 extra points!]
[Player "Faustus" performed exceptionally in this battle, earning bonus rewards: +1,000 Attribute Points, +100,000 Contribution Points!]
[This achievement has been recorded in the annals of war!]
[Server Announcement!!!]
[Cosmic World Event #616 Major Achievement — Under the leadership of player "Faustus," the human Doom Guild has successfully captured the Dwarves’ main city, "Ironforge"!]
[As the first player to seize a non-human race’s main city, the following special rewards are granted:]
Legendary-Grade Follower · Aliris (LV1 Female Warrior) ×1
Contribution Points +100,000
Gold Coin +100,000
Epic-Grade NPCs ×100
Top-Tier Talent NPCs ×200
Polaris City NPC Population +10,000,000
[This achievement has been recorded in the "Stellar" Chronicles, forever etched in history!]
[World Channel]
"What the hell? Captured a non-human main city???"
"Ironforge? That’s the Dwarves’ stronghold... it’s gone just like that?"
"Ironforge is gone? That’s the main city! Millions of people! 1.8 million troops! And it’s just... gone?"
"I was at the scene, brothers. I almost lost my mind! I just saw Faustus God fly into Ironforge, and then thunder roared as all the frontline defenses and walls were reduced to rubble!"
"Scary as hell. Is it really that overpowered? Was that a nuke?"
"Who knows? Can someone explain?"
"I’ve studied Dwarven weapon history at the Great Radiance Museum. If Ironforge was destroyed by lightning, it was probably the forbidden Dwarven weapon, Thunder Verdict!"
"Wait... Faustus God used a Dwarf weapon to blow up a Dwarf city?"
"Hahaha, I can’t stop laughing!"
"The Dwarf overlords must be rolling in their graves..."
"Unstoppable! Absolutely unstoppable!"
"Faustus God, forever a god!"
"World #321 sends congratulations, and asks GM if we can borrow that hack..."
"This game definitely has insider accounts. Investigation recommended!"
"Reported, reported! This game is unplayable now!"
Above the ruins of Ironforge, golden light shimmered.
Hundreds of figures appeared out of thin air, forming neat ranks in front of Daniel.
At the forefront was a woman.
She stood approximately 1.75 meters tall, clad in exquisite silver-white light armor etched with intricate patterns.
Her long, fiery-red hair flowed to her waist, and her facial features were refined as if sculpted by an artist.
At her waist hung a slender one-handed sword, its scabbard adorned with seven differently-colored gemstones.
Her eyes were a rare pale gold, now calmly fixed on Daniel.
[Aliris · LV1 · Legendary-Grade Warrior (Follower)]
Base Attributes:
Attack Power: 1,500
Defense: 1,000
Specialties: Physical Attack, Physical Defense, Agility, Magic Resistance (all Legendary-Grade)
Skills:
Blade Storm – Swings the sword to create a storm, striking all enemies within 10 meters continuously for 5 seconds, each hit dealing 200% damage.
Guardian’s Will – Activates to reduce damage taken by herself and all allies within 50 meters by 50% for 30 seconds.
Break Army Strike – Charged powerful forward slash, dealing 500% damage with armor penetration (ignores 30% of target’s defense).
Indomitable Spirit – Automatically triggers when HP <10%, granting 3 seconds of invincibility and restoring 30% HP. Cooldown 24 hours.
Loyalty: 100% (Max)

Description: Descendant of the ancient human warriors. Raised on the frontier fighting non-human races, ascended to Epic-Grade at eighteen, reached the threshold of legend at twenty, and became the brightest star among the young generation of the ancient clan.
Aliris stepped forward, placing her right fist over her chest and kneeling on one knee.
Behind her, 100 Epic-Grade NPCs and 200 top-tier NPCs knelt in unison.
"Your Grace!"
Her voice was cool, clear, and firm, carrying the decisive tone of a soldier.
"From this day forth, we swear to follow Your Grace to the death, through fire and water, without hesitation!"
Three hundred NPCs shouted in unison:
"We swear to follow Your Grace to the death!"
Their voices echoed across the battlefield, full of overwhelming momentum.
Daniel looked at this heroic, valiant female warrior and nodded with satisfaction.
No wonder the reward for this world-class event was so rich after conquering so many Dwarven clans.
"Rise."
He opened his inventory and took out a pile of Exp Cards—items that grant massive experience, quickly leveling up NPCs.
He had purchased them in the War Shop with Merit Points, specifically for cultivating NPCs.
"Aliris, these will help you grow stronger. Distribute them as you see fit."
"As you command!"
Golden light exploded from the NPCs’ bodies.
Quickly, with the help of the Exp Cards, Aliris reached level 200!
[Aliris · LV200 · Legendary-Grade Warrior]
Current Attributes:
Attack Power: 1,500 → 148,500 (+1,500 per level)
Defense: 1,000 → 200,000 (+1,000 per level)
Aliris felt the surging Strength within her, her eyes filled with gratitude.
Daniel smiled, curious: "Why stop leveling now? I’ve got plenty more of these!"
He pulled out another stack of Exp Cards, ready to continue.
Aliris quickly waved him off.
"Your Grace, you cannot use more!"
Daniel raised an eyebrow: "Why not?"
Aliris explained seriously:
"To continue ascending, two conditions must be met.
First, the individual’s understanding must match their level. Only a strong heart can control this immense Strength.
Second, an Ascendant Starstone is required to assist the breakthrough.
Without it, only a sliver of luck allows ascension. At best, potential is damaged and one remains stuck at Legendary-Grade; at worst, the body explodes on the spot.
Even with an Ascendant Starstone, one’s insight must reach its limit. Both must work together—battle, experience, insight... none can be skipped.
Simply stacking levels with Exp Cards produces an unstable foundation. Even if one manages a lucky breakthrough, their power will be greatly reduced."
Daniel nodded thoughtfully.
He remembered the Ascendant Starstone in his inventory.
Once Aliris’s understanding met the requirements, he could use it to help her ascend.
After all, someone who became Legendary by twenty had immense potential.
And he had a Supreme-Grade Ascendant Starstone—enough to carry her all the way to Supreme-Grade if needed.
"Understood."
He put away the Exp Cards and looked at Aliris.
"From today on, you are my personal commander."
"These 100 Epic-Grade NPCs are under your command."
Aliris’s eyes lit up, and she saluted solemnly.
"As you command, Your Grace!"

Daniel raised an eyebrow: "Why not?"
Aliris explained seriously:
"To continue ascending, two conditions must be met.
First, the individual’s understanding must match their level.
Only a strong heart can control this immense Strength.
Second, an Ascendant Starstone is required to assist the breakthrough.
Without it, only a sliver of luck allows ascension.
At best, potential is damaged and one remains stuck at Legendary-Grade; at worst, the body explodes on the spot.
Even with an Ascendant Starstone, one’s insight must reach its limit.
Both must work together—battle, experience, insight... none can be skipped.
Simply stacking levels with Exp Cards produces an unstable foundation.
Even if one manages a lucky breakthrough, their power will be greatly reduced."
Daniel nodded thoughtfully.
He remembered the Ascendant Starstone in his inventory.
Once Aliris’s understanding met the requirements, he could use it to help her ascend.
After all, someone who became Legendary by twenty had immense potential.
And he had a Supreme-Grade Ascendant Starstone—enough to carry her all the way to Supreme-Grade if needed.
"Understood."
He put away the Exp Cards and looked at Aliris.
"From today on, you are my personal commander."
"These 100 Epic-Grade NPCs are under your command."
Aliris’s eyes lit up, and she saluted solemnly.
"As you command, Your Grace!"

chapters.title: Chapter 73 -73-Allied Shadowkin, Human Crisis
paragraphs: Meanwhile...
Skyhold, three hundred miles outside Lam River.
This was the southeastern border of human territory. Further south lay the vast, untamed Primeval Forest.
Deep within the forest hid a bottomless chasm.
Black mist constantly flowed from the rift, twisting into grotesque shapes in the air. From its depths came faint whispers and guttural roars.
At the edge of the rift stood a towering stone watchtower.
Built entirely from white jade and standing about fifty meters tall, its summit floated a massive orb of light, radiating a soft golden glow that sealed the surrounding black mist out.
This was a human Watcher’s Tower.
The Shadowkin were not minions of the Dark God—they were native to this world.
They were the descendants of the Great Abyss from the previous era, once rulers of the entire world before the Abyss closed.
Two thousand years ago, the gods and humans united to seal the Shadowkin beneath the abyssal rift.
To prevent their escape, humans built watchtowers at every rift, manned day and night.
At this moment, a small green figure crept stealthily toward the rift.
It was a Goblin.
Barely 1.2 meters tall, cloaked in black, with dark green skin visible beneath the hood.
Pointed ears, flattened nose, protruding teeth, and small eyes gleaming with cunning.
[Goblin Envoy · Kruel (LV150)]
He held a black token in his arms, etched with twisted runes and exuding an eerie aura.
[Abyssal Token (Special)]
Effect: Allows the holder to safely pass Shadowkin wards, immune to abyssal aura and undetected by Shadowkin attacks.
Description: A Shadowkin token, granted only to those recognized by the Shadowkin.
Kruel reached the edge of the rift, took a deep breath, and leapt.
The black mist immediately swallowed him.
Falling.
Falling.
After an unknown duration, his feet touched solid ground.
Opening his eyes, Kruel found himself in a massive underground chamber.
Black rock walls surrounded him, crawling with glowing moss that bathed the space in a grim, greenish light.
The floor was hard stone, engraved with complex runes that glimmered faintly red.
Ahead, two massive figures silently regarded him.
The one on the left stood roughly ten meters tall, covered in jet-black scales, with a pair of huge fleshy wings sprouting from its back. Two spiral horns atop its head crackled with lightning.
Its vertical pupils were dark gold, burning with eerie green flames at the center.
[Abyss Lord · Azmodar (LV??? · Legendary-Grade)]
The figure on the right was slightly smaller but exuded a far more sinister aura.
She had a female form, covered in dark purple scales, with six slender bony wings on her back, each tipped with a sharp spike.
[Nightmare Queen · Avelia (LV??? · Legendary-Grade)]
Their combined presence pressed down on Kruel like a mountain, nearly suffocating him.
He knelt heavily, barely daring to lift his head.
"Ex... esteemed Abyss Lord... Nightmare Queen..."
"I am Kruel, envoy of the Goblin tribe, sent by the High Priest to pay respects!"
Abyss Lord Azmodar leaned down, his massive eyes fixed on Kruel.
The gaze was like a predator observing an ant.
"A Goblin?"
His voice rolled like thunder, shaking the entire chamber.
"You green-skinned vermin dare to stand before me?"
Kruel trembled violently but forced himself to speak.
"Please, my lord! I bring urgent news!"
He took a deep breath and spoke rapidly:
"The Beastfolk, Elven rebels, Dwarves, Mammothfolk, Sea People, and Shadow Council... have formed an alliance!"
"They plan to launch a full-scale war against the humans!"
"I have come specifically to plead for your cooperation, to strike the humans from within and without!"
Azmodar and Avelia exchanged a glance.
"Humans?"
Avelia’s voice was hoarse and seductive.
"The Watchers are still above?"
Kruel nodded repeatedly.
"They are! Still standing!"
"So what is this? Are you courting death?"
Avelia’s eyes flashed red.
For countless years, if not for the Watchers guarding above, the Shadowkin army would have long torn the humans to pieces.
"Your Majesty, I came prepared!"
A smug expression crossed his face as he pulled a dark spear from his cloak.
Forged entirely from an unknown black metal, twisted runes etched along its shaft, the tip glimmered with a dark red light.
Merely holding it, one could feel the murderous intent contained within.
[Spear of Dalik (Special Weapon / Single-Use)]
Description: An ancient forbidden weapon of the Shadowkin, forged specifically to strike the gods. Its appearance always heralds bloodshed and chaos.
"With this, those human Watchers... hehe."
Kruel didn’t finish, but the implication was clear.
Azmodar stared at the spear, silent for three seconds, then laughed.
The roar rolled like thunder, shaking the chamber.
"Good! Good!"
"Two thousand years... we have finally awaited this day!"
His eyes burned with the fire of vengeance.
"Back then, the gods and humans united to seal us beneath this sunless abyss."
"It is time to make them pay!"
Avelia laughed too—an eerie, captivating sound.
"Humans... hahaha..."
"Those self-proclaimed paragons of justice have surely forgotten the era when we Shadowkin ruled."
"I cannot wait to make them truly feel what despair is!"
Inside the Ironforge Overlord’s Mansion.
Daniel sat at the head of the table, reviewing a long list.
It was the loot inventory after capturing Ironforge.
[Resource Collection List]
Mines:
Obsidian Mines ×12 (annual output ~5 million units)
Silver-Grade Mines ×8 (annual output ~2 million units)
Thundersteel Mines ×5 (annual output ~1.5 million units)
Iron-Grade Mines ×25 (annual output ~20 million units)
Platinum-Grade Ores (various) ×unknown (requires further exploration)
Materials:
Rare metal ingots ~30 million units
Magical materials ~5 million units
Alchemy materials ~2 million units
Enchantment materials ~1 million units
Equipment:
Epic-Grade ×47
Blackgold-Grade ×328
Platinum-Grade ×1,247
Gold-Grade and below ×countless
War Machines:
War Behemoth (Blackgold-Grade) ×30 (destroyed, requires repair)
Thunder Cannon (Platinum-Grade) ×237
Lava Thrower (Platinum-Grade) ×185
Steam Repeater (Gold-Grade) ×542
Other machinery ×countless
Gold Coins:
Ironforge reserves ~5 billion
Estimated value from selling valuable items ~2 billion
Population:
Dwarf warriors killed ~2.2 million
Civilian survivors ~230,000
Surviving artisans ~12,000 (including ~800 top-tier)
Daniel glanced at the list, a faint smile on his lips.
This operation... had paid off immensely.

chapters.title: Chapter 74 -74-The Non-Human Armies Besiege the City
paragraphs: Daniel closed the ledger and looked over at Hudson.
"General Hudson, has the reconstruction of Ironforge begun?"
Hudson nodded.
"Yes, Your Grace. Following your instructions, we’ve started remodeling the city to match human architectural style."
"It’s expected to take about a week, costing roughly... 1 million gold coins."
Daniel waved his hand dismissively.
"Money is never a problem!"
He opened the city-building interface and transferred the funds directly.
[You have transferred 100,000,000 gold coins to the City Construction Account]
"One hundred million—build it properly!"
"Fortify the walls, widen the streets, upgrade the buildings."
"I want this city to become a beacon of human conquest against the non-human races!"
Hudson twitched at the number.
One hundred million gold coins to renovate a single city...
This Duke really didn’t treat money as money.
"Yes, Your Grace!"
He turned and left to oversee the reconstruction.
Daniel leaned back in his chair, continuing to think about his next move.
With the Dwarves handled, who would be next?
Beastfolk?
Or the Dark Elves?
As he pondered, a message popped up in his private guild chat.
Opening it, he saw it was from an unfamiliar ID.
[Player "Skylight" whispers Faustus]
"Faustus God! Help!"
Daniel raised an eyebrow.
"What’s going on?"
"We’re stationed at Dawnlight City, but things have gone terribly wrong. The city is now surrounded by a massive non-human army!"
"At least 300,000 strong! Beastfolk, Goblins, Elves, Bimon, Mammoths... every race is here!"
"The leader seems to be Vantheon, head of the Stormbound Guild!"
"The garrison only has around 9,000 NPCs, and with our players, just over 10,000—we can’t hold them!"
"God, please save us!"
A cold light flashed in Daniel’s eyes.
Stormbound Guild, Vantheon.
So these guys had aligned with the non-human races.
He opened the map and located Dawnlight City.
A small frontier city at the northeastern edge of human territory, about 800 kilometers from Skyhold.
Small population, weak defenses.
If 300,000 non-human players really attacked, it was indeed indefensible.
As he prepared to reply, another message popped up.
[Player "Sunborn" whispers Faustus]
"The Lam River region within Skyhold is under coordinated attack by non-human players!"
"We’ve decided to hold the city! Requesting your aid, Guild Leader!"
Daniel paused.
Sunborn... he remembered this player. During the Doomgreen Forest Goblin hunt, this guy had single-handedly killed 2,847 Goblins, ranking in the top five.
He had taken note back then.
Daniel immediately replied.
"Hold the city."
"I’m on my way."
Meanwhile, Dawnlight City.
The atmosphere atop the walls was so tense it felt frozen.
Below, the black tide of an army stretched endlessly.
Beastfolk berserkers, Dwarf siege squads, Goblin priests, Dark Elf assassins, Bimon Behemoths, Mammoth war elephants... densely packed, at least 300,000 strong.
At the center, a massive banner flew high.
A twisted symbol embroidered upon it—the emblem of Stormbound Guild.
Vantheon stood atop a war chariot, surveying the city.
He wore a dark purple mage robe adorned with strange flame patterns, holding a black staff topped with a floating purple flame.
[Inferno Mage (S-Rare Class) · LV72]
Behind him, over 300,000 non-human race players surged forward.
"Brothers!"
Vantheon raised his staff, his voice echoing across the battlefield.
"Today is the day we non-human players make our mark!"
"This city is our first stepping stone!"
"Capture it, slaughter the inhabitants, and we’ll establish a foothold in the non-human faction!"
"Then, gear, skills, points... whatever we want will be ours!"
The army of over 300,000 roared in unison.
"Charge! Charge!"
"Beastfolk shall never be enslaved! Hahaha, finally we can proclaim it!"
"Beastfolk are fine, but my A-Rank Warhammer Destroyer has better value!"
"All these ugly creatures, for looks we still have the Elves..."
"Break in! For the points!!"
At the flanks of the army, three figures stood out.
On the left, a massive player, golden fur covering his body, wielding a gigantic bone club.
[Bimon Behemoth Player · Barbarian’s Hammer (LV65 · Bimon Berserker) · Non-Human Faction]
On the right, an even larger player, over four meters tall, thick gray fur, with two massive tusks protruding from his mouth.
[Mammoth War Elephant Player · Infinite Might (LV63 · Mammoth Guardian) · Non-Human Faction]
Between them stood an Elven female player.
She wore sleek emerald leather armor, her figure perfectly proportioned, her pale green eyes enchanting and piercing.
[Dark Elf Player · Sylphira (LV69 · Elf Assassin) · Non-Human Faction]
She looked at Barbarian’s Hammer and spoke coquettishly:
"Brother Barbarian’s Hammer, this city should be easy for you to take, right?"
The golden-furred giant’s bones practically melted at the term "brother." He patted his chest and vowed:
"Don’t worry! With defenses at this level, I can smash their gates with one strike!"
Sylphira turned to Infinite Might.
"And you, Brother Infinite Might?"
The mammoth nodded.
"Of course! Same here!"
Sylphira’s eyes gleamed with satisfaction.
These two simpletons... so easy to manipulate!
Though she secretly looked down on their simple-minded, brute-force approach, using them when necessary was quite convenient.
Vantheon watched and smirked.
Elves’ beauty talent is indeed useful.
Two idiots—stupid in real life, and just as dumb in the game!
He shook his head and raised his staff toward Dawnlight City.
"All forces, advance!"
Woooosh—!
The horn blared.
300,000-strong army surged like a tide toward Dawnlight City.
On the city walls.
Sunborn gripped his greatsword tightly, staring down at the approaching horde.
Six others stood beside him—his seven-person squad.
The priestess paled.
"C-Captain... can we hold them?"
Sunborn drew a deep breath.
"Even if we can’t... we will hold."
"Faustus God is coming!"
He turned to the other players on the walls.
"Brothers! Doom Guild reinforcements are on the way! Faustus God is en route!"
"If we just hold until he arrives, we win!"
"Do you have the confidence?"
Players exchanged glances, then erupted in a deafening roar.
"Yes!"
"To hell with it!"
"These idiot players normally don’t act like humans, but I’ll take a few down with me if I die!"
"Charge! For XP! For points!"
Sunborn grinned.
That’s the spirit.
He raised his greatsword.
"Prepare to engage!"

chapters.title: Chapter 75 -75-Using the Deathcurse Potion
paragraphs: [World Channel]
"Extra! Extra! Dawnlight City is surrounded by the non-human armies!"
"What? 300,000 against 10,000? That city is doomed!"
"Looks like there are Doom Guild players defending it!"
"Where’s Faustus? Why isn’t he coming to help?"
"Obviously, Faustus God just finished leading his army to conquer Ironforge. He’s probably resting now!"
"This is over. Sunborn’s done for."
"I bet they won’t last half an hour!"
"I’ll say one hour!"
"Place your bets!"
[Doom Guild Channel]
"The non-human players are acting brazen! Attacking a human city?!"
"The Doom Legion is still recovering from Ironforge. We, who just logged in, need to support Dawnlight City."
"I’ve already left with hundreds of guild members!"
"You’re all moving so slow—I’ve already arrived!"
Daniel’s gaze shifted away from the guild chat.
"A non-human army legion?"
His eyes narrowed. He quickly pulled a black vial from his inventory.
The bottle was completely black, etched with twisted skull patterns. Its cork was sealed with wax, and inside the dark liquid churned ominously.
[Deathcurse Potion (Single-Use)]
Effect: Upon using, the next player you kill will drop at least one piece of current equipment and lose 5 levels. However, if you are killed during this period, you lose 10 levels.
Description: A curse that gambles everything—either you die, or I perish.
Daniel had obtained this as a reward during the Beast Tide event—ten bottles in total, unused until now.
He decided it was time.
Daniel uncorked the vial and drank it in one gulp.
Gulp~
The black liquid slid down his throat, an icy chill immediately spreading through his body.
[Ding! You have used "Deathcurse Potion"!]
[Current Status: Death Curse (12 hours, until first kill or death)]
[Singer’s Gem Effect Triggered: All item effect durations increased 100×!]
[Death Curse Duration: 12 hours → 1,200 hours!]
A faint smile appeared on Daniel’s lips.
1,200 hours—exactly fifty days!
During these fifty days, every player he killed would lose 5 levels, drop their equipment, and have their inventory cleared.
Thinking this through, he opened his status panel.
[Death Curse BUFF]
Killing a player reduces their level by 5 (including current level).
Forces the drop of at least one piece of equipment (highest quality prioritized).
Forces the drop of all inventory items.
Description: Those killed by this curse are returned to pre-liberation status.
Seeing this near-BUG-level buff, Daniel immediately sprinted toward a nearby portal.
A flash of white light, and he vanished.
Dawnlight City
A flash of light.
Daniel arrived in an instant via God Speed, and the deafening sounds of battle met him immediately.
"Dawnlight City... has it fallen?"
He furrowed his brow, surveying the scene.
The human banners on the walls had been torn down, replaced by a variety of non-human flags:
The Beastfolk Lion Standard
Goblin Green Skull Banner
Dark Elf Serpent Banner
Countless non-human players burned, looted, and massacred within the city.
Even women, children, and the elderly weren’t spared.
A Beastfolk berserker swung his axe to splinter the door of a house, screams of women and children spilling out.
"Hahaha! All these NPCs are mine! Don’t even try to compete!"
"Perfect! Killing an NPC child gives more points than monsters!"
"Brothers, charge! Steal kills, steal points!"
A Dark Elf assassin emerged from the shadows, her dagger slicing the throat of an NPC elder, blood gushing.
"These civilians are so satisfying to kill! All the points, hahaha..."
A Goblin priest conjured a cloud of poisonous mist, the screams of trapped NPCs echoing inside.
"Hahaha! My poison fog is getting stronger!"
From the direction of the Lord’s Manor, fierce battle sounds rang out.
Although Doom Guild and other human players had arrived to reinforce, they were only slowing down the advance of over 300,000 elite non-human players.
The remaining defenders were concentrated at the Lord’s Manor.
As long as the manor held, the city remained under human control.
Daniel’s expression turned serious.
In the next moment, he unfolded Black Dragon Wings, his figure becoming a shadow as he streaked toward Lord’s Manor.
The gates of Lord’s Manor were tightly shut.
Outside, a dense sea of non-human players surrounded the manor, thirty thousand thick, stretching as far as the eye could see.
The leaders of the non-human faction stood together, greedily eyeing the manor, continuously commanding their warriors in repeated assaults.
"As long as we breach Lord’s Manor, Dawnlight City is ours!"
Vantheon stood atop a war chariot, raising his dark-flame staff.
A column of dark purple fire slammed against the gates, causing them to tremble and crack.
Next to him, the Dark Elf Sylphira casually tucked a strand of hair behind her ear.
"Hope you keep your word. Let’s avoid surprises with our resources."
Vantheon nodded.
"My Stormbound Guild’s reputation precedes me—trustworthiness isn’t an issue, is it?"
Sylphira gave him a faint, disdainful glance.
"Stormbound Guild, trustworthy? Who even believes that? You’re infamous worldwide. If I didn’t hold the cards, there’s no way I’d collaborate with you."
She didn’t expose him openly, instead turning to two male non-human players with slight irritation.
"Why haven’t you breached the gates yet? Hurry your people up!"
Hearing this, the two non-human leaders panicked.
"Miss Sylphira, please don’t be angry! I’ll command full assault immediately!"
"Once the city is ours, I want nothing—whatever you desire, it’s yours."
The speaker was the Bimon Behemoth player, Barbarian’s Hammer, pounding his chest with obsession-filled eyes.
The Mammoth War Elephant player, Infinite Might, nodded.
"Same here!"
Sylphira’s eyes flickered with slight disgust.
But disdain aside, she wouldn’t bother arguing—there was profit to be had.
Vantheon watched, a cold smile curling at the corner of his mouth.
"You really think bringing these two idiots along will gain you anything from me? Foolish!"
At that moment, a shadow descended from the sky, landing squarely in front of Lord’s Manor.
Boom!
The ground cracked, stones flew.
As the dust cleared, everyone could see the newcomer.
Clad in silver-white robes, a pair of black dragon wings spread behind him.
He held a silver-white longbow that shimmered faintly with moonlight.
His expression was calm, his gaze serene, as though the 300,000-strong army before him were nothing but air.
[Faustus · LV100 · Doom Guild Leader · Imperial Duke]
Cheers erupted instantly within Lord’s Manor!
"Faustus God! Faustus God has arrived!"
"Holy shit! He’s really here!"
"I knew it! The God wouldn’t abandon us!"
"Faustus God is invincible! Kill all these human traitors!"
Sunborn, Skylight, and others on the walls watched the lone figure blocking 300,000 soldiers, their blood boiling.
Skylight gripped his greatsword and shouted loudly:
"Brothers! Faustus God has arrived!"
"Prepare for the counterattack!"
On the walls, the remaining two thousand human players roared in unison.

chapters.title: Chapter 76 -76-Four Arrows, Securing the Battlefield
paragraphs: On the side of the non-human faction, Vantheon’s expression darkened abruptly.
Faustus!
Damn it—how did he get here?!
Wasn’t he at Ironforge?
How could he arrive on the battlefield so quickly?!
Sylphira froze, a flicker of panic crossing her otherwise flawless face.
Barbarian’s Hammer and Infinite Might exchanged glances, their eyes full of dread.
That was the infamous killer from the world announcements—the one who had leveled cities with a single arrow and oneshotted epic-grade NPCs.
For a moment, all 300,000 troops froze, unable to move.
Daniel slowly lifted his head, his gaze sweeping across the massive non-human army.
Cold as a blade, it forced everyone he looked upon to instinctively step back.
His eyes finally settled on Vantheon.
"Vantheon!"
His voice was calm, almost quiet, yet carried clearly to every ear.
"You’ve made the same choice in the end. A dog cannot change its nature."
Vantheon’s face turned pale as iron. He gritted his teeth.
"Faustus, who do you think you are?! Arrogant, huh?!"
"We have 300,000 soldiers! How many can you possibly kill alone?!"
A faint smile tugged at Daniel’s lips.
"Three hundred thousand?"
He raised Moon Reaper, and on the empty bowstring, a single golden arrow materialized out of thin air.
"Want to test it?"
Bang—!
The golden arrow tore across the sky and pierced Vantheon’s chest in an instant.
A terrifying damage number floated above Vantheon’s head.
His HP vanished instantly. He didn’t even have time to react before his body exploded into fragments.
[Ding! You have slain player "Vantheon" (Non-Human Faction)!]
[Death Curse BUFF Triggered!]
Target Level -5 (Current: 72 → 67)
Dropped Equipment ×7 (Dark Flame Staff, Shadow Robe, Shadow Gauntlets...)
Forced Drop of All Inventory Items (Gold, Materials, Potions, Scrolls...)
Gold and equipment sparkled across the ground, materials piled into small mountains.
Silence fell.
Over 300,000 non-human players stared blankly at the scene.
What? Killing a single player could drop this much loot?
But more terrifying was that being killed by Faustus reduced levels by 5?!
All that equipment exploded?!
And the entire inventory emptied?!
What kind of bugged skill is this?!
Luminara Respawn Point
Vantheon stumbled into the respawn area, face pale as death.
Those three system prompts had him questioning the game.
[Ding~ You were killed by player "Faustus," Death Curse BUFF triggered. Level -5!]
[Ding~ You were killed by player "Faustus," Death Curse BUFF triggered. Dropped Equipment ×7!]
[Ding~ You were killed by player "Faustus," Death Curse BUFF triggered. Forced drop of all inventory materials!]
He looked down.
His inventory was empty.
His level had dropped from 72 to 67, falling out of the top tier of players.
His equipment... gone.
Everything he had painstakingly acquired with countless gold coins—vanished.
His hands trembled, teeth chattered.
Then he opened the game forum, frantic, and started a post:
[REPORT! Faustus Hacking!]
[After being killed, I lost 5 levels, my equipment was blown away leaving only my undergarments, and my inventory was wiped! GM, are you paying attention?!]
The post instantly flooded with replies:
"Hahaha! What have you done to deserve this?"
"Faustus God: Heard you wanted fairness? I’ll give you fairness!"
"Level loss, high loot explosion rate, inventory wiped... is this killing or account deletion?"
"Vantheon: Bro, I’m back to square one overnight!"
"Stormbound Guild Leader wiped out—equipment and gold gone. Is this moral collapse or human corruption? Welcome to this episode of Inside Stellar’s Top Player..."
Dawnlight City
The square before Lord’s Manor glittered with dropped equipment, gold, and materials.
Over 300,000 non-human players stared at the pile—but none dared touch it.
They watched Daniel in disbelief, fear gradually creeping into their eyes.
What is this?
Killed by him, level drops 5, high loot, inventory wiped...
How is this different from having your account deleted?!
Sylphira snapped back to reality, forcing a faintly perfect smile, her voice dripping with delicate charm:
"Lord Faustus, we..."
Before she could finish, a golden arrow pierced her chest.
Critical hit! HP vanished instantly.
[Ding! You have slain player "Sylphira" (Non-Human Faction)!]
[Death Curse BUFF Triggered!]
Target Level -5 (Current: 69 → 64)
Forced drop of 4 pieces of equipment
Forced drop of all inventory items
Sylphira’s body collapsed, her emerald leather armor, dagger, rings... exploded outward, forming a small pile.
Her backpack erupted, scattering gold, materials, and potions everywhere.
Barbarian’s Hammer and Infinite Might froze for a moment, then erupted in rage.
"How dare you kill Sylphira!"
"Don’t you know who she is?! She’s a famous celebrity in Earth! You bastard, I’ll fight you!"
Barbarian’s Hammer roared, transforming into a Bimon Behemoth, golden fur bristling, swinging his massive bone club at Daniel.
Infinite Might also roared, transforming into a Mammoth War Elephant, his five-meter-tall body shaking the ground, tusks gleaming coldly.
Daniel’s expression was calm.
Aetherlance!
The golden spear tore through the sky, piercing Barbarian’s Hammer’s chest instantly.
Boom—!
The enormous body exploded into fragments.
[Ding! You have slain player "Barbarian’s Hammer" (Non-Human Faction)!]
[Death Curse BUFF Triggered...]
Immediately afterward, another Aetherlance shot forth.
Infinite Might had barely advanced halfway before the golden spear pierced him.
Boom—!
The Mammoth War Elephant collapsed, kicking up a storm of dust.
[Ding! You have slain player "Infinite Might" (Non-Human Faction)!]
[Death Curse BUFF Triggered...]
Just three arrows.
Three non-human faction leaders were wiped out.
Over 300,000 non-human players were left in stunned silence.
Daniel sheathed his bow, scanning them with cold, furious eyes.
With countless memories spanning multiple lifetimes, he loathed human traitors more than anything.
While countless humans had given their lives defending Earth and their people, these human turncoats had helped the non-human races open the gates to slaughter—proudly hunting their own kin.
The horrific scenes were still burned into his mind.
Kill.
He would annihilate every human traitor.
The murderous aura around Daniel thickened, seemingly freezing the very air.
The non-human players instinctively stepped back, sensing the deadly intent.
"Who else is left?"
Daniel’s voice was quiet, yet it struck every heart like a hammer.
Not a single one of the 300,000 non-human players dared move.

chapters.title: Chapter 77 -77-1 vs 300,000
paragraphs: "Who else is left?"
Daniel’s voice was quiet, yet it struck every heart like a hammer.
Not a single one of the 300,000 non-human players dared move.
Inside Lord’s Manor, the remaining two thousand human players were utterly dumbfounded.
"Killing the enemy general amidst an entire army... what is this?"
"These trash are nothing compared to the God! They literally wanted to stand before him, in front of 300,000 of their own minions, just to die!"
"Faustus God: you see me and don’t immediately kill yourselves, yet still dare bark at me? Boldness indeed!"
"Why is Faustus’s loot rate so ridiculous???"
"Faustus must be insane, right? He kills without even blinking!"
"I’m starting to regret joining the non-human faction... what about you?"
"Same here. Feels like there’s no way to get past Faustus!"
Just as the mass of players hesitated, a Beastfolk Berserker suddenly raised his battle axe, shouting loudly:
"Brothers! Faustus is only one person, and we have 300,000!"
"Numbers alone should overwhelm him!"
"Don’t be afraid—levels can be regained. If we kill him, the rewards will be huge!"
His words acted like a jolt of courage, reigniting hope among the previously hesitant non-human players.
Some joined in the encouragement.
"Exactly! Everyone knows Faustus is decked in artifacts! Let’s all gang up and blow him up!"
"Faustus is an archer—fragile. If the warriors push forward, killing him is just a matter of minutes!"
"Charge! Stop the nonsense!"
The 300,000 surged forward again.
Daniel’s expression remained calm as he slowly raised Moon Reaper.
Arrowstorm!
Shattering Comet!
He combined both skills.
A golden rain of arrows poured down, covering hundreds of meters!
Boom boom boom boom boom—!
Explosions deafened the battlefield.
The thousands of players at the front were instantly shredded into fragments.
[Ding! You have slain non-human faction players ×1,327!]
[Death Curse BUFF Triggered! Target Level -5! Forced equipment drop! Forced drop of all inventory items!]
The ground shimmered with gold and loot, piles of equipment, coins, and materials everywhere.
Yet the non-human players’ eyes burned red as they stepped over the corpses of their comrades and pressed onward.
"He’s only one person! Skills have cooldowns! His mana will run out!"
"Charge! Kill him!"
Daniel remained expressionless, firing arrow after arrow.
Each shot sent dozens or hundreds of players down.
They didn’t even have time to react before respawning at Luminara.
Seeing themselves naked and their inventories empty, they howled in despair.
"Ahhh! My gear!!!"
"Faustus!!! My skill book is gone!"
"Fuck! Bitch! I’m reporting this, Faustus is hacking!"
"What a joke! My equipment? These were platinum-grade items I worked a week to obtain!"
Countless players were killed by Faustus, all thrown back to square one overnight.
On the battlefield, Daniel stood alone before Lord’s Manor, facing the tide of 300,000 non-human players.
Arrow rain never ceased. Explosions erupted constantly.
The non-human players’ skills rained down like raindrops—but:
"MISS!"
"MISS!"
[Demon’s Whisper] granted immunity to all negative effects.
[Windstrider Robe] gave a 50% chance to fully dodge.
Combined with over 17,000 Agility, attacks from low-level players either did a single forced HP point or missed entirely.
He didn’t even need to dodge.
He simply stood there, harvesting arrow after arrow.
The spectacle shocked everyone present.
Faustus alone, trading volleys with 300,000 players—and not a single setback!
Thirty minutes passed.
Daniel’s arrows had yet to stop.
His mana and HP, aided by Infinite Grail, regenerated 1% per second, and with each kill, restored even more—almost limitless.
The non-human players began to crumble—not because they couldn’t fight, but mentally.
They watched their comrades being oneshotted, equipment raining down around them.
They saw those who charged forward appear ten seconds later in Luminara, naked and screaming.
Even the luckiest would lose at least one piece of their highest-quality gear.
The pressure of potentially losing everything at any moment was more terrifying than death itself.
Finally, some couldn’t hold on.
A Goblin priest turned and ran.
"I’m done! I don’t want to lose levels!"
Then the second, third... tenth, hundredth...
"Run!"
"A bunch of idiots still charging? Brainwashed or crazy!"
"I’m out, I don’t want to lose gear!"
The besieging non-human players dropped from hundreds of thousands to tens of thousands, then thousands, then hundreds.
Those hesitating saw this and panicked, fleeing en masse.
A cold glint flashed in Daniel’s eyes.
"Want to run now?"
He unfolded Black Dragon Wings and soared into the sky.
God Speed activated!
The next moment, he appeared in the densest cluster of non-human players.
Arrowstorm!
Golden arrows rained down, covering the entire fleeing force.
Boom boom boom boom boom—!
Thousands fell.
Then he appeared elsewhere.
Shattering Comet!
Arrows split into countless golden points, falling like a meteor shower.
Hundreds more were cut down.
With God Speed chain-blinking infinitely, Daniel’s figure streaked across the battlefield, each appearance taking hundreds of lives.
From above, he was a golden lightning bolt weaving through the fleeing horde.
Everywhere he passed, the ground shimmered with gold.
[Ding! You have slain non-human faction players ×1,847!]
[Ding! You have slain non-human faction players ×2,336!]
[Ding! You have slain non-human faction players ×1,217!]
System notifications flooded endlessly, unstoppable.
Sunborn, atop the Lord’s Manor walls, felt his blood boil.
"Brothers!"
He raised his greatsword, shouting.
"Faustus God is hunting 300,000 alone! Why are we standing still?"
"Charge! Harvest! Collect the loot!"
The remaining two thousand human players surged from Lord’s Manor like a tidal wave, chasing the fleeing non-human faction players.
The non-human forces had been utterly terrified by Daniel, unable to organize any resistance.
Some begged for mercy, some cried, some logged out in panic.
Those who had been killed respawned in Luminara, naked and empty-handed, wailing.
When they read the forums and saw Vantheon and countless others’ anguished posts, they finally understood:
Faustus—was truly untouchable.
Dawnlight City had been defended.
And it had been defended in a near legendary-grade fashion.
One man against 300,000.
"Faustus is insane! How the hell is this possible?!"
"I don’t want to lose levels! I don’t want to lose gear!"
"Faustus is a demon! A demon!"
The 300,000 non-human players scattered in chaos, fleeing in every direction.

Not a single one of the 300,000 non-human players dared move.

"I’m starting to regret joining the non-human faction... what about you?"
"Same here.

"Brothers!
Faustus is only one person, and we have 300,000!"
"Numbers alone should overwhelm him!"
"Don’t be afraid—levels can be regained.
If we kill him, the rewards will be huge!"

chapters.title: Chapter 78 -78-The Calculated Trap of the Human Watcher
paragraphs: [World Channel]
"Breaking news! Dawnlight City has held its ground!"
"What? Weren’t they surrounded by 300,000 non-human troops? How did they hold?"
"No one knows exactly when, but Faustus suddenly appeared! One arrow and Vantheon was gone, three more arrows took down three player leaders, and all 300,000 fled!"
"You think that’s all? Even crazier—Faustus killed level-5s, looted their gear, emptied their inventories... He’s basically gone wild!"
"Hahaha, I’m laughing myself sick! What do you need? Just take it straight from my bag, why bother pretending?"
"Everyone’s happy. Vantheon got slaughtered down to his last pair of underpants, his bag is empty, and he dropped to level 67!"
"This is hilarious! Stormbound Guild is completely finished now!"
"Do you know what Vantheon said at that moment? He actually asked Faustus how many he could kill. Faustus just shot four arrows, and over 300,000 players ran for their lives!"

"Don’t laugh—laugh and you won’t survive either. Wait until you see the forum breakdown of the Ironforge battle. Four players? Pathetic. Even epic-grade NPCs over level 200 couldn’t withstand a single arrow from the god!"
"Faustus is forever our god!"
Meanwhile, three hundred miles outside Lam River, Skyhold.
The Abyssal Rift.
A goblin in a black cloak hid behind a massive rock at the edge of the rift, staring intently at the chasm ahead.
His face was obscured in shadow, revealing only a pair of piercing, sinister eyes.
Cradled in his arms was a pitch-black spear.
The weapon stretched two meters long, forged from an unknown black metal, the shaft etched with twisted runes, the tip glowing a dark crimson.
[Spear of Dalik (Legendary / One-time Use)]

Effect: Within a 10-kilometer radius, inflicts intangible damage on God-kind or Human targets, drastically reducing defense, easily piercing all shields, leaving the target in a weakened state (Defense -100%, lasting 30 minutes).
Description: A special weapon painstakingly crafted by a fallen alchemist, designed specifically for gods and humans.
Kruel’s eyes glittered with fervor as he stared at the spear in his hands.
No matter how many times he looked at it, he felt it was absurdly powerful.
Alas, such a mighty weapon was consumable.
If only it were permanent... that pitiful Human Watcher would queue up to die, hah!
Suddenly—BOOOOM!
A deafening explosion erupted from deep within the rift, and black mist spewed forth like a volcanic eruption!
Kruel snapped to attention, quickly planting the Spear of Dalik into the ground, hands forming intricate seals.
He activated the spear immediately.
Red light radiated from the weapon, excitement surging in his chest.
An invisible wave pulsed outward, instantly engulfing a ten-kilometer radius.
Deep within the rift.
Two massive figures blocked the path of a human warrior, one behind the other.
[Abyss Lord · Azmodar (LV ??? · Legendary)]
[Nightmare Queen · Avelia (LV ??? · Legendary)]
And standing against them, a venerable old man with white hair and beard, dressed in a flowing white robe, wielding a golden longsword that shimmered with holy radiance.
His aged face belied the sharp, eagle-like gaze that radiated an aura even Shadowkin lords dared not challenge.
[Human Watcher · Carodion (Legendary)]
He was the Watcher guarding Skyhold’s northern abyssal defenses, a legendary warrior of renowned fame.
Azmodar bared his fangs in a wicked grin.
"Carodion... a hundred years. Still alive?"
"Why haven’t you died yet? Today, we’ll finish the job!"
Avelia’s laughter was seductive and sinister.
"Once you die, no one will be left to guard this rift."
Carodion snorted coldly, sword held horizontally before him.
"Is that all you’ve got?"
"Centuries of suppressing you, and today... nothing’s changed!"
Before his words could fade, Azmodar and Avelia struck simultaneously.
Azmodar opened his massive maw, spewing a torrent of black flame straight at Carodion’s face.
Avelia became a purple streak, six bony wings unfurling, jagged spikes striking from every angle toward Carodion’s back.
Unfazed, Carodion swung his golden sword.
A blade of radiant energy cut the flame in half.
At the same time, a shimmering golden shield enveloped him, blocking every attack from Avelia.
"Divine Protection Shield!"
The bony spikes clanged against the shield, scraping like metal, yet failing to pierce it.
Carodion sneered.
"Is that all you’ve got?"
"Pathetic!"
He twisted his sword, sending an even sharper wave of golden energy slicing toward Azmodar.
Azmodar dodged, but the blade grazed his black-scaled armor, leaving a deep wound.
"Centuries ago, you weren’t my match... and now, you still aren’t!"
Carodion’s golden blade rained down, forcing the two Shadowkin back step by step.
But then—
An invisible pulse suddenly enveloped the battlefield.
Carodion’s golden shield shattered without warning!
"What?!" His pupils contracted, and before he could react, a searing pain tore through his back.
SPLASH!
A black bone spike pierced through his chest from behind.
It was Avelia’s spike!
An attack that normally couldn’t even break his shield had passed straight through him.
All his defenses seemed to vanish.
"This... is impossible!"
Carodion looked down at the spike through his chest, disbelief in his eyes.
His Divine Protection Shield, his god-grade defensive gear—completely nullified?!
Azmodar’s face twisted into a cruel grin.
"Didn’t expect this, did you, Carodion?"
"We’ve been waiting centuries to kill you!"
He raised his hand, unleashing another wave of flame.
Carodion was thrown against the rock wall, coughing blood, his face ashen.
"Could it be... the Spear of Dalik?"
He managed to choke out the words, realization and fury flashing across his eyes.
"Damn Shadow Council... human parasites!"
Azmodar advanced step by step, each footfall shaking the ground.
"Yes... the Spear of Dalik."
"A special gift for the Watcher himself."
"How does it feel to have all your defenses stripped away?"
Carodion struggled to stand, blood flowing down his white robe.
He looked at the two Shadowkin before him, then at the widening rift above, eyes burning with grief.
"Shadowkin invade... the lives of humanity are in peril..."
"This is my fault... I was careless..."
He drew a deep breath, resolve hardening in his gaze.
"But to atone for my mistakes..."
Suddenly, Carodion surged forward, transforming into a golden streak of light toward Azmodar.
Azmodar’s expression changed drastically; he turned to flee.
"Carodion... you’re insane!"
Carodion latched onto Azmodar’s waist, screaming toward the heavens:
"Humanity shall never perish!"
BOOOOM!!!
An earth-shattering explosion erupted deep within the Abyssal Rift.
Golden radiance engulfed everything.

chapters.title: Chapter 79 -79-Watcher Falls, Shadowkin Invade
paragraphs: A long while passed before the smoke and dust finally began to settle.
When the haze cleared, both Azmodar and Carodion were completely gone.
Only Avelia remained in the distance, her face dark and livid.
"He actually self-destructed?"
"That damned bastard!"
She stared toward the far horizon and threw back her head with a furious roar.
"You human insects—every last one of you deserves to die!"
At that very moment, a blood-red system announcement resounded across the entire Stellar World.
[Emergency Server-Wide Announcement!!!]
[Human Watcher · Carodion (legendary-grade) has fallen!]
[At the northern defensive line of Skyhold in Universe No. 616, 300 li beyond the Lam River, a two-star Abyss Rift has erupted into a Shadowkin riot!]
[Attention all players of Universe No. 616! The Shadowkin are about to invade!]
[All players aligned with the human faction, proceed to the northern defensive line immediately and repel the Shadowkin invasion!]
[Repeat! The Shadowkin are about to invade! All human-faction players, reinforce the northern defensive line at once!]
The emergency announcement rang out again and again.
Those blood-red words flashed before the eyes of every player.
The World Channel was instantly flooded with frantic messages from players across countless worlds.
"Ohoho, a blood-red world announcement? This has to be some kind of juicy event reward, right? Hahaha..."
"Looks like World 616 really messed up this time. Hahaha, this is hilarious. Let’s see how they clean this up."
"I’m guessing your world’s Faustus cheated so hard that the GM had to crank up the difficulty for you!"
"A Shadowkin invasion? Holy shit, they’ve already triggered another major world event? I’m so jealous..."
Meanwhile, the players of World 616 were completely lost.
"What Shadowkin invasion? Could this be another masterpiece from the great Faustus?"
"If your brain doesn’t work, maybe leave it at home instead of bringing it out to embarrass yourself. Faustus is still in Dawnlight City!"
"Exactly. The Shadowkin invasion is happening in Skyhold. That’s ten thousand miles away from Luminara!"
"But our war against the non-human races isn’t even over yet, so why has some Shadowkin thing popped out of nowhere again?"
"You guys are amazing. A new map and a new race? Stop talking and charge already!"
Dawnlight City.
[Ding! Millionfold Boost triggered! Obtained gold coin +100000!]
[Ding! You picked up: [Venomfang Dagger (blackgold-grade)]!]
[Ding! You picked up: [Prismatic Crystal (platinum-grade)]!]
Through relentless slaughter, Daniel had already killed off most of the non-human races players.
Gold gleamed everywhere across the ground, while equipment, coins, and materials had piled up into literal mounds.
After hearing the system announcement, Daniel slowly drew in a deep breath.
"Hm? A Shadowkin invasion?"
"That’s not right. Why has the timing advanced this much?"
In his memories, the Shadowkin had remained suppressed within the Abyss Rift.
At the very least, it should have taken several more months before they could break through the rift passage and invade the Stellar World.
And Abyss Rifts were also divided into tiers.
The higher the grade of the rift, the more Shadowkin elites it could allow to cross over.
A two-star rift could permit two legendary-grade Shadowkin powerhouses to descend.
A nine-star rift, on the other hand, could allow nine legendary-grade Shadowkin powerhouses to enter the Stellar World.
The death of the Watcher also meant that Skyhold would now face not only legendary-grade Shadowkin, but also the blades and claws of countless Shadowkin warriors.
"Legendary-grade Shadowkin..."
A trace of worry gradually surfaced in Daniel’s eyes.
His four core attributes and overall combat power were already absurdly high.
Even so, he still had no confidence in facing a legendary-grade existence head-on.
Still, he possessed [God Speed], which granted him limitless instantaneous movement.
Combined with survival skills like [Voidstride], simply preserving his own life would not be difficult.
In order to find out what was going on, Daniel decided to head to the rift in person and see for himself why the situation had changed so drastically.
Without wasting another second, he used a portal and rushed toward Skyhold.
Three hundred li beyond the Lam River.
The site of the two-star Abyss Rift.
At that moment, countless fiends were pouring madly out of the rift.
Some were beast-shaped, their bodies covered in jet-black scales, their eyes burning with dark crimson fire.
Others were humanoid, more than two meters tall, wielding pitch-black weapons and radiating a foul demonic aura that made one’s skin crawl.
The beast-formed ones were collectively classified as fiends.
The humanoid ones, meanwhile, were known as Shadowkin.
When Daniel arrived near the rift, the sight before him made his heart sink at once.
A row of human corpses had been hung directly at the mouth of the rift.
Not a single one of those human powerhouses had an intact body left.
Some had been disemboweled.
Some had been beheaded.
Some had all four limbs twisted into grotesque angles no living body could ever endure.
Dried blood had stained the black rock below them a dark, ugly red.
Daniel cast a detection spell.
[LV??? · Deren (legendary-grade) · deceased]
[LV??? · Cedric (legendary-grade) · deceased]
[LV??? · Aurelia (legendary-grade) · deceased]
"Damn it..."
Daniel felt a heavy, suffocating anger rise in his chest.

This scene reminded him of his previous lives, when during the invasion wars of the non-human races, countless human powerhouses had thrown themselves forward one after another for the continuation of their people.
And now...
Human champions had been butchered just the same, then strung up before the rift entrance.
This was a naked humiliation of humanity, a ruthless trampling of its dignity.
A violent brutality surged through Daniel’s eyes, almost impossible to restrain.
At that moment, a Shadowkin powerhouse floating in midair narrowed her eyes as she examined him.
[Nightmare Queen · Avelia (LV??? · legendary-grade)]
The other Abyss Lord, Azmodar, had already perished together with Watcher Carodion in their mutual destruction.
Now, Avelia looked down on Daniel from above, her eyes full of contempt.
"How pitiful... a mere insect."
To someone like Avelia, a weakling such as Daniel was beneath even the worth of her personal attack.
Thus, she merely lifted a hand and gave a careless wave.
In an instant, countless Shadowkin warriors charged toward Daniel in a frenzy of excitement.
"Human worm, despair and beg for mercy!"
"Hahahahaha!"
Sensing the tide of Shadowkin warriors rushing at him, Daniel remained utterly calm.
God Speed activated.
A flash of white light streaked through the battlefield, and every single Shadowkin attack missed its mark.
In the next instant, Daniel appeared before the three mangled corpses of the fallen human powerhouses.
He took down those three bodies and lifted them onto his back.
Then, without the slightest hesitation, he activated God Speed once more.
Whoosh!
A great mass of Shadowkin elites swarmed in from all directions.
Yet none of them could touch him, and they could only watch helplessly as he vanished right before their eyes.
When Daniel appeared again, he was standing atop a high ridge.
He slowly and carefully laid the three bodies down.
He examined them in silence.
The corpses of these three human powerhouses had been ravaged beyond recognition.
Moreover, because they had not reached legendary-grade, there was no divine soul remnant left within their remains.
That meant they did not meet the conditions necessary to be revived with [Seraphic Revival].
And from those ruined bodies, shattered to a state almost beyond description, it was easy to imagine the agony and torment they must have suffered before death.
If an ordinary bystander had witnessed this, they might have done nothing more than praise the game’s realism.
They might have said the visuals were convincing, the texture was impressive, and the plot was dark, brutal, and full of depth.
But Daniel knew the truth.
These NPCs were, in a very real sense, living beings.
He forcibly suppressed the rage that was boiling inside him.
Then, facing the fallen dead before him, he spoke in a low voice.
"I will suppress the Abyss Rift."
"So rest now, brave souls... and may you sleep in peace."

sentences.text: A long while passed before the smoke and dust finally began to settle.
When the haze cleared, both Azmodar and Carodion were completely gone.
Only Avelia remained in the distance, her face dark and livid.
"He actually self-destructed?"
"That damned bastard!"
She stared toward the far horizon and threw back her head with a furious roar.
"You human insects—every last one of you deserves to die!"
At that very moment, a blood-red system announcement resounded across the entire Stellar World.
[Emergency Server-Wide Announcement!!!]
[Human Watcher · Carodion (legendary-grade) has fallen!]
[At the northern defensive line of Skyhold in Universe No.
616, 300 li beyond the Lam River, a two-star Abyss Rift has erupted into a Shadowkin riot!]
[Attention all players of Universe No.
The Shadowkin are about to invade!]
[All players aligned with the human faction, proceed to the northern defensive line immediately and repel the Shadowkin invasion!]
[Repeat!
The Shadowkin are about to invade!
All human-faction players, reinforce the northern defensive line at once!]
The emergency announcement rang out again and again.
Those blood-red words flashed before the eyes of every player.
The World Channel was instantly flooded with frantic messages from players across countless worlds.
"Ohoho, a blood-red world announcement?
This has to be some kind of juicy event reward, right?
Hahaha..."
"Looks like World 616 really messed up this time.
Hahaha, this is hilarious.
Let’s see how they clean this up."
"I’m guessing your world’s Faustus cheated so hard that the GM had to crank up the difficulty for you!"
"A Shadowkin invasion?
Holy shit, they’ve already triggered another major world event?
I’m so jealous..."
Meanwhile, the players of World 616 were completely lost.
"What Shadowkin invasion?
Could this be another masterpiece from the great Faustus?"
"If your brain doesn’t work, maybe leave it at home instead of bringing it out to embarrass yourself.
Faustus is still in Dawnlight City!"
"Exactly.
The Shadowkin invasion is happening in Skyhold.
That’s ten thousand miles away from Luminara!"
"But our war against the non-human races isn’t even over yet, so why has some Shadowkin thing popped out of nowhere again?"
"You guys are amazing.
A new map and a new race?
Stop talking and charge already!"
Dawnlight City.
[Ding!
Millionfold Boost triggered!
Obtained gold coin +100000!]
[Ding!
You picked up: [Venomfang Dagger (blackgold-grade)]!]
[Ding!
You picked up: [Prismatic Crystal (platinum-grade)]!]

Gold gleamed everywhere across the ground, while equipment, coins, and materials had piled up into literal mounds.
After hearing the system announcement, Daniel slowly drew in a deep breath.
"Hm?
A Shadowkin invasion?"
"That’s not right.
Why has the timing advanced this much?"
In his memories, the Shadowkin had remained suppressed within the Abyss Rift.
At the very least, it should have taken several more months before they could break through the rift passage and invade the Stellar World.
And Abyss Rifts were also divided into tiers.
The higher the grade of the rift, the more Shadowkin elites it could allow to cross over.
A two-star rift could permit two legendary-grade Shadowkin powerhouses to descend.
A nine-star rift, on the other hand, could allow nine legendary-grade Shadowkin powerhouses to enter the Stellar World.
The death of the Watcher also meant that Skyhold would now face not only legendary-grade Shadowkin, but also the blades and claws of countless Shadowkin warriors.
"Legendary-grade Shadowkin..."
A trace of worry gradually surfaced in Daniel’s eyes.
His four core attributes and overall combat power were already absurdly high.
Even so, he still had no confidence in facing a legendary-grade existence head-on.
Still, he possessed [God Speed], which granted him limitless instantaneous movement.
Combined with survival skills like [Voidstride], simply preserving his own life would not be difficult.
In order to find out what was going on, Daniel decided to head to the rift in person and see for himself why the situation had changed so drastically.
Without wasting another second, he used a portal and rushed toward Skyhold.
Three hundred li beyond the Lam River.
The site of the two-star Abyss Rift.
At that moment, countless fiends were pouring madly out of the rift.
Some were beast-shaped, their bodies covered in jet-black scales, their eyes burning with dark crimson fire.
Others were humanoid, more than two meters tall, wielding pitch-black weapons and radiating a foul demonic aura that made one’s skin crawl.
The beast-formed ones were collectively classified as fiends.
The humanoid ones, meanwhile, were known as Shadowkin.
When Daniel arrived near the rift, the sight before him made his heart sink at once.
A row of human corpses had been hung directly at the mouth of the rift.
Not a single one of those human powerhouses had an intact body left.
Some had been disemboweled.
Some had been beheaded.

Daniel cast a detection spell.
[LV??? · Deren (legendary-grade) · deceased]
[LV??? · Cedric (legendary-grade) · deceased]
[LV??? · Aurelia (legendary-grade) · deceased]

This scene reminded him of his previous lives, when during the invasion wars of the non-human races, countless human powerhouses had thrown themselves forward one after another for the continuation of their people.
And now...
Human champions had been butchered just the same, then strung up before the rift entrance.
This was a naked humiliation of humanity, a ruthless trampling of its dignity.
A violent brutality surged through Daniel’s eyes, almost impossible to restrain.

chapters.title: Chapter 80 -80-Thunder Verdict – Nuclear-Level Destruction!
paragraphs: The next moment, Daniel vanished from the high ground.
When he reappeared at the mouth of the rift, countless Shadowkin warriors howled and charged at him again.
The Shadowkin forces were terrifyingly coordinated. Though wild with excitement, their discipline rivaled even that of human legions.
Warriors led the front, arrows and dark spells raining from above...
An endless torrent of attacks descended upon Daniel.
In that instant, Daniel raised his hand, and a purple crystal materialized.
[Thunder Verdict (Legendary / One-time Use)]
Effect: Upon activation, within a radius of 10,000 meters centered on the user, deals damage equal to 1000% of the user’s attack power to all enemies.
This was a war prize Daniel had seized during the Dwarf War.
At the Battle of Ironforge, its destructive power had been unbelievable.
A single strike had reduced even Ironforge’s toughest outer shell to rubble!
In the next moment, Daniel released Thunder Verdict.
The crystal flew straight into the densest cluster of Shadowkin warriors.
BOOOOM!
The Abyssal Rift erupted in a mushroom cloud of purple lightning!
Countless Shadowkin monsters were obliterated as if they had melted like snowmen in the storm.
Damage numbers flashed wildly, the system alarm chiming incessantly.
Daniel paid no heed.
He teleported again and drew a second Thunder Verdict, hurling it toward another dense cluster of Shadowkin warriors.
BOOOOM!
Another massive mushroom cloud exploded.
Countless Shadowkin warriors turned to ash in the violet lightning.
"No!"
Avelia shrieked as she witnessed the devastation.
"Human ants! I will tear you apart!"
She hadn’t expected such a weak human to inflict this level of carnage on the Shadowkin.
Black tendrils of energy shot from her body, writhing toward Daniel like a storm of whips.
"Demonic Energy Tendrils!"
Daniel’s vision filled with black tendrils growing ever larger.
God Speed!
Through successive teleportations, he evaded the seemingly unstoppable attack with ease.
Meanwhile, he pulled out another Thunder Verdict.
He lifted his gaze to the ceaseless stream of Shadowkin emerging from the rift, and the crystal flew with precision.
It arced toward the rift’s entrance.
BOOOOM!
The entire entrance of the Abyssal Rift collapsed in an instant.
Countless Shadowkin elite warriors perished before they could even draw a breath.
Avelia’s fury exploded.
"Die, you wretch!"
She surged forward, radiating purple light toward Daniel.
But Daniel did not confront her directly; he continued to rely solely on God Speed.
Slash! Slash! Slash!
Avelia’s killing intent filled the sky, yet she could not touch Daniel.
He weaved through the void, untouchable, leaving her completely unable to track him.
"Shameless ants!!!"
Roaring in rage, Avelia suddenly seemed to recall something.
She produced an object from her body.
A fragment of bone, emitting a faint golden glow.
It was the remains of Watcher Carodion!
Holding up the bone shard, she taunted Daniel:
"Ant, this is your tribe’s Watcher’s remains... if you want it, come and take it."
"Otherwise, I might just lay it as flooring!"
Daniel’s eyes hardened.
He fixed his gaze on the fragment.
Avelia’s lips curved into a triumphant smile.
From Daniel’s earlier actions retrieving the human corpses, she knew he was a man of faith.
Such a person could never allow the bones of his kin to be desecrated.
"Remains..."
Daniel thought of a certain legendary-grade item in his possession.
If he could reclaim this bone fragment, he might have a chance to resurrect the Watcher!
After all, the Watcher had reached legendary-grade, and a portion of his divine soul still lingered in the remains.
Resolved, Daniel made his decision.
Success or failure, he would attempt it.
Avelia could see his intent and smirked with satisfaction.
She casually tossed the bone fragment into the air.
In the next moment, Daniel and Avelia vanished almost simultaneously.
Flash!
When Daniel reappeared, the fragment was firmly in his grasp.
At the same time, detailed information about the bone surfaced before his eyes:
[Watcher Carodion’s Remains (Legendary)]
Description: The remnants of Human Watcher Carodion after self-detonation, containing faint divine radiance.
"It really is the Watcher’s remains!"
Daniel whispered.
But the next instant—
A black broken blade pierced his body!
"Weak little insect! Die!"
Avelia’s face twisted into a conspiratorial grin.
[Ding! ’Demon’s Whisper’ triggered! Immune to this fatal attack!]
Flash!
Daniel vanished instantly, reappearing far away.
At the precise moment he was immune to the fatal blow, he used God Speed to escape entirely.
Avelia’s eyes flickered with surprise as she watched him leave unharmed.
She pursued again briefly...
But then she stopped.
Her mission was to guard the rift.
If the humans had set a trap and she left, allowing them to seize control of the rift, she would bear great guilt.
Despite her frustration, she gritted her teeth and watched Daniel disappear into the distance.
Back at the high ground, Daniel placed the Watcher’s remains down and immediately accessed the system.
[Seraphic Revival (Supreme-grade)]
Effect: Sacrifice a massive amount of gold coins to resurrect a deceased NPC.
Requirement: The target must have an intact body or retain divine essence.
He took a deep breath and placed Carodion’s remains into the golden light.
[Ding! You are using ’Seraphic Revival.’ Detected legendary-grade relic. Confirm payment of 900 billion gold coins to resurrect this NPC?]
[Note: Upon resurrection, the NPC will enter a soul contract with you. All memories prior to death will be erased, but full power is retained.]
900 billion gold coins.
A sum that would deter nearly anyone.
But to Daniel, money was just numbers.
"Yes!"
He confirmed decisively.
In an instant, golden light condensed before him, growing brighter and brighter.
Moments later, a complete human form emerged from the radiance.
Clad in white robes, aged in appearance but eyes sharp and piercing, radiating divine aura.
[Watcher · Carodion (Legendary) · Follower]
[Loyalty: 100% (Soul Contract)]
[Status: Resurrected, memories erased]
Carodion opened his eyes and looked at Daniel.
Gone was the weariness of his previous life, replaced by pure loyalty.
"My lord."
He touched his chest in salute, his voice deep and resolute.
"Watcher Carodion, awaiting your command."
